name: AACR Project GENIE (public releases)
description: International registry pooling real-world targeted tumor-panel sequencing from dozens of centers, with twice-yearly public releases of mutation, copy-number and fusion data plus limited clinical variables. The BPC (Biopharma Collaborative) adds deeply curated outcome data for selected cancer types.
scale: ~242,000 patients / ~290,000 samples (release ~20.0, mid-2026)
license: Custom GENIE terms of use — NO redistribution without AACR written permission; free registration

provenance.maintainer: AACR + Sage Bionetworks (Synapse); mirrored on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Largest real-world panel-sequencing corpus; strong for mutation-frequency/recurrence priors and for population-level validation of shared/actionable antigen targets.

agent_access: Download requires a free Synapse account and acceptance of terms; fetch via the Synapse Python/R client or command line (token auth), or query the public mirror on cBioPortal's API. Automatable with stored Synapse credentials.
caveats: REDISTRIBUTION PROHIBITED without AACR written permission — flag for any derived product. Targeted panels only (not WES/WGS); heterogeneous gene coverage across centers and releases; retractions occur between releases (track version).

name: GSE317244 / GSE317641 — Canine Acanthomatous Ameloblastoma & Oral SCC RNA-seq + snRNA-seq
description: Bulk RNA-seq (GEO GSE317244) and single-nucleus RNA-seq (GSE317641; 19 samples — 6 canine acanthomatous ameloblastoma, 10 oral squamous cell carcinoma, 3 healthy gingiva; ~205k nuclei) characterizing neuroepithelial reprogramming and ERBB vulnerability in canine oral tumours (Mol Ther Oncol 2026).
scale: snRNA: 19 samples / ~204,967 nuclei; + bulk RNA-seq

relevance.why: Oral-tumour gap filler with single-nucleus resolution across two tumour types plus healthy gingiva; ERBB axis is an actionable target and the atlas supports TME/antigen-expression work.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Bulk per-dataset sample counts not stated in text (DS1 new, DS2 reused prior data) — inspect GEO metadata.

name: Braun et al. 2020 — advanced RCC nivolumab (CheckMate 009/010/025)
description: Integrated WES + RNA-seq of advanced renal-cell carcinoma from the CheckMate nivolumab trials with clinical outcome; dissected genomic and transcriptomic correlates of PD-1 blockade response in RCC.
scale: ~311 patients across CheckMate 009/010/025 (WES; RNA-seq subset)

provenance.maintainer: Choueiri / Wu labs, Dana-Farber; Bristol Myers Squibb trials

relevance.why: Trial-grade RCC cohort with matched expression and outcome — strong for validating antigen/expression response models in a non-melanoma, low-TMB setting.

agent_access: Raw data controlled in EGA (three study accessions); access via EGA DAC approval + EGA download client (pyega3) with credentials. Processed tables/clinical in supplement.
caveats: EGA accessions sourced from a secondary re-analysis paper — confirm against the Nature Medicine data-availability statement. EGA access is per-dataset and can take days.

name: Canine Tumor WES/WGS Cohorts (lymphoma, melanoma, hemangiosarcoma)
description: Collection of public canine tumor exome/genome cohorts in SRA/ENA: lymphoma exomes across three breeds (Broad-sequenced), oral melanoma (ENA PRJEB12081), hemangiosarcoma/angiosarcoma comparative WGS/WES, glioma (PRJNA579792), mammary (PRJNA489159), and pan-tumor TMB/TP53 reanalyses (~600-710 cases).
scale: hundreds of tumor-normal pairs aggregated across studies

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA / ENA (various depositing labs incl. Broad, UPenn, UMN)

relevance.why: Somatic mutation landscapes across canine tumor types — raw material for canine neoantigen prediction (mutation calls -> candidate peptides), to be paired with DLA presentation models.

agent_access: SRA/ENA FASTQ/BAM (prefetch, no auth). Mixed references (CanFam3.1 mostly) — re-align/liftover.
caveats: Heterogeneous references, capture kits and metadata; many lack breed/germline detail. No MHC typing. Neoantigen calling blocked downstream by the DLA-prediction gap.

name: PRJNA1222422 / GSE289443 — Canine Thyroid Carcinoma WES + RNA-seq (Commun Biol 2025)
description: Comparative genomic/transcriptomic profiling of canine thyroid carcinomas: whole-exome (SRA BioProject PRJNA1222422) and RNA-seq (GEO GSE289443) on 30 tumours (25 follicular, 5 medullary; WES+RNA on 27, RNA-only on 3), contrasting molecular profiles with human thyroid cancer (Commun Biol 2025). Normal-thyroid RNA comparators drawn from BarkBase.
scale: 30 tumours sequenced (of 60 total); 27 WES+RNA, 3 RNA-only

relevance.why: New endocrine tumour type for the catalog with matched exome+expression and an explicit canine-vs-human molecular comparison; supports cross-species driver mapping.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). WES (SRA) and RNA (GEO) in separate archives — join by sample. Figure source data on figshare; some data on-request.

name: Cristescu et al. 2018 — pan-tumor PD-1 biomarkers (KEYNOTE trials)
description: Retrospective analysis across four KEYNOTE pembrolizumab trials (>300 samples, ~22 tumor types) jointly evaluating TMB and a T-cell-inflamed gene-expression profile (GEP) as predictors of PD-1-blockade response.
scale: >300 samples across ~22 tumor types (4 KEYNOTE trials)

relevance.why: Defines the operational T-cell-inflamed GEP and its interplay with TMB across many tumor types — a reference for combining expression context with antigen burden.

agent_access: No open individual-level repository; signature definitions and aggregate results are in the paper/supplement. Patient-level trial data require sponsor (Merck) data-sharing request (e.g. via a clinical-trial data-request platform).
caveats: Sponsor-controlled; not an automated-fetch resource. Useful mainly for the published GEP gene set and thresholds. License for supplementary content not explicitly stated.

name: Melanoma checkpoint-blockade WES/RNA cohort (dbGaP phs000452; Van Allen 2015 + Liu 2019)
description: Whole-exome (and later RNA-seq) of metastatic melanoma treated with checkpoint blockade, with response/survival outcomes — a core resource for neoantigen-load vs response modeling. Van Allen 2015 (anti-CTLA-4) deposited as v2.p1; Liu 2019 (anti-PD-1, integrative) extended it as v3.p1.
scale: Van Allen: ~110 WES tumor/normal pairs (anti-CTLA-4); Liu 2019: larger integrative anti-PD-1 melanoma cohort (WES+RNA)

provenance.maintainer: Van Allen / Liu et al., Dana-Farber / Broad Institute (dbGaP)

relevance.why: Response-annotated melanoma exomes/transcriptomes to relate neoantigen load/quality to ICB outcome — a benchmark cohort for Veritope's presentation/immunogenicity signals.

agent_access: CONTROLLED: dbGaP DAR/DUA approval + eRA Commons required. Not agent-fetchable. Note version split (v2 = Van Allen, v3 = Liu); confirm the version a given analysis needs.
caveats: Controlled-access; no redistribution. Processed MAF/mutation tables for these cohorts are often re-published openly via cBioPortal (study 'skcm_dfci_2015' etc.) — prefer those for open reuse.

name: DepMap / CCLE (Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia + Dependency Map)
description: Broad Institute's cell-line multi-omics: whole-exome/WGS, RNA-seq expression, fusions, copy-number, methylation and metabolomics for ~1,800 cancer cell lines, alongside CRISPR and RNAi dependency and drug-sensitivity screens. The reference resource for cancer cell-line genotype-to-phenotype.
scale: ~1,800 cell lines (omics); ~1,000+ with deep multi-omic profiles
license: DepMap Terms and Conditions (usage agreement; attribution); some metadata CC BY 4.0

relevance.why: Cell lines are the experimental substrate for testing predicted antigens (expression + HLA + presentation). DepMap links a line's mutations/expression to its genotype, so predicted neoantigens can be matched to validatable in-vitro models.

agent_access: Fully automatable: CSV/parquet from the download page, an open AWS bucket (s3://depmap-omics-ccle/, no account), and a portal API. No DUA. Click-through terms ask for attribution only.
caveats: License is a usage agreement, not a standard open license — attribution required, verify before redistribution. Cell lines are not patients (no germline/tumor-microenvironment context); HLA types must be inferred from the omics or from the companion lines.

name: FidoCure / One Health Company Canine Clinico-Genomics
description: Real-world canine precision-oncology platform: targeted panel sequencing (coding exons of oncogenes/tumor suppressors) plus treatment outcomes. Published analyses cover 2,119 dogs (genomics for ~1,108) across >19 tumor types, and a 508-dog splenic hemangiosarcoma study.
scale: ~2,119 dogs (genomics ~1,108); company claims >5,500 dogs
license: article CC BY (2023 npj Precis Oncol); raw data not public

relevance.why: Largest real-world canine clinico-genomic outcome linkage; valuable aggregate statistics, but not an open dataset.

agent_access: Only summary/supplementary tables are public; patient-level data "upon reasonable request". No bulk download, no API.
caveats: Proprietary; targeted panel (not WES/WGS); company scale claims unverified. NOT redistributable — treat as reference/collaboration target, not a fetchable corpus.

name: NCI Genomic Data Commons (GDC)
description: NCI's harmonized cancer genomics repository and the canonical home of TCGA, TARGET, CPTAC, HCMI, Foundation Medicine, MMRF and dozens of other projects. All data are reprocessed against a common reference (GRCh38) with uniform pipelines, so mutation, copy-number, expression and clinical files are directly comparable across projects. Data are split into an open tier (reprocessed somatic mutation calls, gene expression, copy-number, clinical/biospecimen) and a controlled tier (BAM/CRAM reads, germline, raw genotypes) gated by dbGaP.
scale: ~50,000+ cases across ~90+ projects (portal current count; ~44k cases at v39)
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (data-use terms; no single SPDX license)

provenance.maintainer: National Cancer Institute (NCI), Center for Cancer Genomics; operated by U. Chicago

relevance.why: Primary open source of somatic mutation calls (MAF) and RNA-seq expression across tumor types — the raw material for enumerating candidate neoantigens and confirming that the mutated gene is expressed. Controlled tier gives read-level evidence for variant/allele-specific-expression validation.

agent_access: Open-tier files via a documented REST API and the gdc-client download tool — no auth, scriptable, bulk manifests supported. Controlled-tier files require a GDC token minted after dbGaP authorization (Authorization header / token file); the token expires and must be refreshed. No scraping needed; everything is API-addressable.
caveats: Controlled tier (reads, germline) needs an approved dbGaP Data Access Request tied to a specific study (e.g. phs000178 for TCGA) — per-study, renewable, institution-signed. Open-tier redistribution is governed by NIH GDS/data-use certification, not an open license; cite and respect publication-embargo norms. GRCh38 harmonization means legacy hg19-based calls differ from current ones.

name: Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project (Cancer Programme)
description: UK national WGS programme; the cancer arm provides matched tumor/germline whole genomes with linked NHS clinical and cancer-registry data. Data never leave a secure Research Environment (NGRL) — no bulk export; approved researchers analyze in situ.
scale: ~15,600 cancer-programme participants (germline+somatic WGS); ~13,880 tumors analyzed
license: Genomics England Research Network / Discovery Forum access agreement (no redistribution; no download)

provenance.maintainer: Genomics England Ltd (UK Department of Health)

relevance.why: Population-scale WGS with deep real-world clinical linkage; valuable for validating antigen/driver findings in an independent national cohort and for outcome association.

agent_access: NO data download. Analysis only inside the secure Research Environment after joining the Research Network or a Discovery Forum (industry) partnership. Pipelines must run inside the walled garden; results export is reviewed. Not compatible with an external automated fetch pipeline — the compute goes to the data.
caveats: Membership application + (for industry) paid access; airlock review on any results taken out. UK-governed, consent/registry-linked. Hardest fit for an automated external pipeline.

name: Canine Osteosarcoma Bulk RNA-seq — GSE238110 (DOG^2 cohort)
description: Bulk mRNA-seq of 186 canine primary osteosarcoma tumors (DOG^2 cohort), reused by multiple comparative canine/human osteosarcoma and tumor-microenvironment studies.
scale: 186 primary tumors
license: public (NCBI GEO; no explicit license, US-gov public-domain norms)

relevance.why: Largest single canine osteosarcoma transcriptome series; TME deconvolution and expression context for antigen candidates.

agent_access: GEO supplementary counts + SRA FASTQ (prefetch); no auth; FTP bulk.
caveats: Expression only — no HLA/DLA typing, no immunopeptidome. Align to a fixed reference.

name: Gide et al. 2019 — melanoma anti-PD-1 +/- anti-CTLA-4 (WES/RNA-seq)
description: Metastatic melanoma treated with anti-PD-1 monotherapy or combined anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4, with WES and RNA-seq and response/survival; emphasized on-treatment biopsies as stronger predictors than baseline.
scale: ~73-91 patients (WES and/or RNA-seq across pre/on-treatment)
license: ENA/EGA submission terms (RNA-seq open on ENA; WES controlled on EGA)

provenance.maintainer: Wilmott / Scolyer / Long labs, Melanoma Institute Australia

relevance.why: Combination-therapy melanoma cohort with on-treatment transcriptomes — complements Hugo/Riaz for antigen/expression dynamics under single vs dual blockade.

agent_access: RNA-seq openly retrievable from ENA PRJEB23709 (no auth). WES controlled in EGA EGAD00001005738 (DAC + pyega3).
caveats: Accessions sourced from re-analysis papers — confirm against the Cancer Cell data statement. Mixed open/controlled by modality.

name: GSE122916 — Canine Prostate Cancer FNA + Tissue RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of canine prostate tissue and fine-needle aspirates spanning malignant and non-malignant samples (reanalyzed in a biomarker-prioritization framework, PMC8584104: 10 malignant and 14 non-malignant prostate tissue/FNA samples). Canine prostate cancer is predominantly castration-resistant, a model for aggressive human disease.
scale: ~24 samples (malignant + non-malignant tissue and FNA)

relevance.why: Canine prostate expression reference; underpins a canine/human castration-resistance comparison (bioRxiv 2024) relevant to cross-species target discovery.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Small malignant n. The comparative bioRxiv preprint key_ref was rate-limited at verification — confirm whether it deposits new accessions beyond this series. Framework DOI verified on PMC8584104.

name: GSE190374 / PRJNA786902 — Nine Canine Prostate Cancer Cell Lines RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of nine canine prostate cancer cell lines compared with original tumour tissues, revealing diverse therapeutic-target signatures (Cancer Cell Int 2021). SRA study SRP349649 / BioProject PRJNA786902.
scale: 9 canine prostate cancer cell lines (+ tumour tissue)

relevance.why: Canine prostate cancer cell-line panel expands the canine in-vitro model collection and pairs cell lines with source tumours for expression fidelity checks.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Cell lines — not primary cohort.

name: GSE208664 — Canine Soft-Tissue Sarcoma, 3 Subtypes FFPE RNA-seq (PLoS ONE 2022)
description: Comparative whole-transcriptome RNA-seq across three canine soft-tissue sarcoma subtypes from FFPE material, with FASTQ, metadata and read-count files deposited (PLoS ONE 2022). Complements GSE214154 with subtype-resolved expression.
scale: canine STS, 3 subtypes (FFPE RNA-seq)

relevance.why: Subtype-level STS expression reference; useful to stratify the integrated cohort and for canine-human STS expression mapping.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). FFPE-derived — expect degradation artifacts.

name: GSE214154 / PRJNA882864 — Canine Soft-Tissue Sarcoma Integrated Omics (Sci Rep 2023)
description: Integrated RNA-seq (GEO GSE214154, 29 samples) and matched tumour/normal whole-exome sequencing (SRA BioProject PRJNA882864) of canine soft-tissue sarcomas, reporting recurrent TP53 and KMT-gene mutations and recurrent PDGFB fusions (Sci Rep 2023).
scale: 29 STS RNA-seq samples + 29 tumour/normal WES pairs

relevance.why: Matched expression + exome in an under-covered tumour group; fusion and driver calls give both neoantigen candidates (fusions) and expression context for them.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). RNA in GEO, WES in SRA — link by sample IDs. Heterogeneous STS subtypes within the cohort.

name: GSE238110 — Canine Osteosarcoma Bulk RNA-seq (DOG^2 / COTC022)
description: Bulk mRNA-seq of 186 canine primary osteosarcoma tumors (DOG^2 cohort / COTC022), NovaSeq 6000 (GPL25760). Widely reused by comparative OSA studies. Raw count matrix provided.
scale: 186 primary tumors
license: public (NCBI GEO; no explicit license, US-gov public-domain norms)

relevance.why: Largest single canine OSA transcriptome; TME deconvolution + expression context for antigens.

agent_access: GEO supplementary counts + SRA FASTQ (prefetch); no auth; FTP bulk.
caveats: Expression only; no DLA typing or immunopeptidome. Pin a reference for alignment.

name: GSE288068 — Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma Tumour + Cell-Line Transcriptomes (Engleberg 2025)
description: RNA-seq of canine histiocytic sarcoma (18 HS-affected tumours vs 5 normal samples, plus three HS cell lines), identifying multiple therapeutic target pathways (Engleberg et al., Cancers 2025). Canine HS is a spontaneous model for the rare human histiocytic/dendritic neoplasms, with breed predisposition (e.g. Bernese Mountain Dog, Flat-Coated Retriever).
scale: 18 tumours + 5 normal + 3 cell lines (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: Michigan State University / NIH Genomics Core

relevance.why: First-pass transcriptome for a previously uncovered canine tumour type with a direct rare-human-cancer analogue; supplies HS expression references and candidate targets.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Modest cohort; normals n=5. Cell-line and tumour data mixed in one series — separate by sample metadata.

name: GSE295311 — Canine Osteosarcoma GeoMx Spatial Transcriptomics
description: NanoString GeoMx digital spatial profiling of osteosarcoma-bearing pet dogs enrolled in a clinical trial; companion spatial layer to the bulk GSE238110 cohort.
scale: spatial ROIs across trial dogs

relevance.why: Spatially resolved immune/tumor compartments — rare canine spatial dataset for microenvironment work.

agent_access: GEO download; no auth.
caveats: Targeted panel (not whole-transcriptome spatial); small ROI count.

name: Hartwig Medical Foundation database
description: Dutch non-profit hosting uniformly processed whole-genome sequences of metastatic (and increasingly primary) tumors with matched normals and clinical/treatment-response data. A leading resource for metastatic cancer genomics and mutational landscapes under treatment.
scale: ~8,000+ patients WGS (metastatic solid tumors)
license: Hartwig license agreement per data request (DR-xxx); no redistribution

relevance.why: Metastatic-tumor WGS captures the antigen landscape at the disease stage therapy actually targets, including treatment-driven evolution — complementary to primary-tumor cohorts like TCGA.

agent_access: Submit a data request; a Data Access Board reviews it and you sign a license agreement. On approval, data are delivered (typically cloud bucket/transfer), after which access is programmatic. No anonymous or API-first access; application-gated.
caveats: Request is project-scoped and license-bound with publication rules; no redistribution. Each project gets a DR-number. Turnaround is weeks.

name: Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN) Data Portal
description: NCI-funded multi-institution atlas of human tumors across the pre-cancer-to-advanced continuum, with single-cell, spatial, imaging, bulk and clinical data under a common data model. Open-access derived/Level-3+ data plus controlled-access lower-level and identifiable data.
scale: 20+ atlases, millions of cells + spatial/imaging across cancer types

provenance.maintainer: NCI Human Tumor Atlas Network / Sage Bionetworks (Synapse)

relevance.why: Multi-modal, deeply clinically annotated human tumor data spanning single-cell and spatial — high-value for linking antigen-presentation state to tumor progression.

agent_access: Open-access files downloadable (free Synapse account for Synapse-hosted files). Programmatic access via Synapse REST API / CLI / R client, and ISB-CGC BigQuery for clinical/metadata queries; portal generates DRS manifests for cloud (SB-CGC). Controlled files require approved dbGaP application (phs002371) — not agent-automatable.
caveats: Controlled tier needs institutional dbGaP DUA; cannot be auto-ingested. Explicit reuse license for open-access files not clearly stated per-file — check portal terms. Third-party `htan` PyPI wrapper exists (MIT) but is unofficial.

name: Hugo et al. 2016 — anti-PD-1 melanoma (WES/RNA-seq + response)
description: Metastatic melanoma treated with anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab/nivolumab); whole-exome and transcriptome of pretreatment tumors with response annotation. Defined the "IPRES" innate anti-PD-1 resistance transcriptional signature.
scale: ~38 patients (WES); 28 RNA-seq (GSE78220)
license: GEO/SRA public submission (open); cite source paper

relevance.why: Open anti-PD-1 melanoma expression + mutation cohort for benchmarking expression-based and neoantigen-based response models.

agent_access: RNA-seq openly downloadable from GEO GSE78220; raw reads in SRA SRP067938 (UCLA) and SRP090294 (Vanderbilt) via fasterq-dump — no auth, fully automatable.
caveats: Small, melanoma-only. WES access route less uniform than the RNA-seq; confirm per-sample.

name: Hugo 2016 anti-PD-1 melanoma (GEO GSE78220 + SRA SRP067938/SRP090294)
description: Genomic + transcriptomic profiling of metastatic melanoma on anti-PD-1 therapy, with response annotation. RNA-seq in GEO (GSE78220); whole-exome in SRA. Widely reused for response/neoantigen and expression-signature modeling.
scale: 38 WES samples; 28 with RNA-seq (15 responders / 13 non-responders, pre-treatment)

relevance.why: OPENLY accessible response-annotated melanoma RNA-seq (GEO) — rare for ICB cohorts (most are dbGaP); good for expression/neoantigen-context modeling without a DUA.

agent_access: GEO RNA-seq (GSE78220) openly downloadable, no auth; WES in SRA (SRP067938 UCLA, SRP090294 Vanderbilt) openly accessible. Fully automatable.
caveats: Open, but SRA raw WES is large. Small cohort. GEO processed data = FPKM tables; raw reads via SRA.

name: ICDC OSA01
description: Multi-platform sequencing (WGS/WES/RNA-seq) of canine appendicular osteosarcoma.
scale: osteosarcoma cohort (count via API)

relevance.why: Osteosarcoma somatic landscape for neoantigen candidate generation.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No MHC typing/immunopeptidome; counts via API.

name: ICDC OSA03
description: Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (methylation) of human and canine osteosarcoma — rare public canine tumor methylome.
scale: human + canine OSA WGBS (count via API)

relevance.why: One of the few public canine tumor methylomes; epigenetic context for antigen expression.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Methylation only; counts via API.

name: ICDC TCL01
description: Whole-exome sequencing of canine cancer cell lines (multi-tumor). Overlaps SRA PRJNA503864.
scale: ~33 canine cancer cell lines

relevance.why: Candidate substrate for in-house DLA-restricted immunopeptidomics.

agent_access: ICDC API + SRA FASTQ; open.
caveats: No MHC typing; see PRJNA503864/503860.

name: ICDC TCL01 — Canine Cancer Cell-Line WES
description: Whole-exome sequencing of canine cancer cell lines (osteosarcoma, lymphoma, melanoma, hemangiosarcoma and others) for druggable-target discovery. Overlaps SRA BioProject PRJNA503864 (33 canine cancer cell lines).
scale: ~33 canine cancer cell lines

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC; original: Das et al.

relevance.why: Cell lines are candidate substrates for in-house DLA-restricted immunopeptidomics (MHC-I elution) to begin closing the canine presentation gap.

agent_access: FASTQ/BAM via SRA (prefetch/fasterq-dump, no auth); calls via ICDC.
caveats: No native MHC-ligand data; DLA typing of lines not standardized.

name: ICDC UBC02
description: Molecular subtypes of canine urothelial carcinoma with tumor immune signatures (genomics/transcriptomics). One of the few ICDC studies with an explicit immune-signature focus.
scale: urothelial cohort (count via API)

relevance.why: Tumor immune-signature transcriptomics — closest ICDC study to immune context, but still no MHC-ligand/TCR data.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Immune "signatures" are expression deconvolution only, not antigen-level data.

name: ICDC UC01
description: Whole-exome sequencing of canine urothelial carcinomas lacking BRAF V595E; identifies in-frame BRAF/MAP2K1 deletions as alternative MAPK activation.
scale: WES cohort (BRAF V595E-negative)

relevance.why: Somatic variants for neoantigen candidate generation in bladder cancer.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Exome variants only; no MHC data.

name: ICGC 25K (legacy International Cancer Genome Consortium)
description: The original ICGC data release: ~24,000 donors across ~80 projects and 20+ tumor types. Simple somatic mutations, structural variants, expression and methylation are available in two tiers — open-access aggregated/somatic summaries, and controlled-access raw and germline data in EGA.
scale: 24,289 donors (22,330 with molecular data), ~80 projects
license: ICGC data-access policy (open tier) / DACO + EGA DUA (controlled tier)

provenance.maintainer: ICGC / OICR (legacy DCC, partially migrated to AWS/Collaboratory and EGA)

relevance.why: Large, diverse open somatic mutation corpus for neoantigen enumeration without a DUA, spanning tumor types and populations complementary to TCGA.

agent_access: Open somatic/aggregated files downloadable programmatically from the legacy DCC/mirrors (no auth). Raw and germline data require DACO approval plus EGA dataset-level access and the EGA download client (ega-fuse / pyega3) with credentials.
caveats: Legacy portal partially deprecated; some endpoints moved to AWS Collaboratory / EGA. Controlled tier is doubly gated (DACO then EGA). Build-hg19 calls predominate.

name: ICGC ARGO (Accelerating Research in Genomic Oncology)
description: Successor to ICGC, aiming to uniformly analyze tumor genomes with harmonized, deep clinical data across international programs. Clinical data on the ARGO Data Platform are open to any registered user; molecular (sequence/variant) data are controlled and gated by the ICGC Data Access Compliance Office (DACO).
scale: ~7,000+ donors, 9 programs, ~180,000 files (Release 15)
license: ICGC ARGO data-use / DACO terms (not an open license)

relevance.why: International, prospectively collected tumors with uniform processing extend antigen-discovery beyond US cohorts and add populations/cancer types underrepresented in TCGA.

agent_access: Clinical data downloadable by any registered platform user (programmatic via platform API). Controlled molecular data require DACO approval (2-year term), after which a download client / API token is issued. Not scrape-able; auth-gated end to end for molecular files.
caveats: DACO application is institution-signed and project-scoped; approval can take weeks. Some raw data mirrored in EGA with separate per-dataset access (up to 48h provisioning).

name: Gabriella Miller Kids First Data Resource
description: NIH Common Fund pediatric resource spanning childhood cancers and structural birth defects, with WGS/WES and RNA-seq plus clinical data. Summary data are browsable in the Portal; individual-level genomic data are controlled via dbGaP and analyzed through the integrated CAVATICA cloud platform.
scale: ~30,000+ participants with WGS or RNA data (cancer + congenital)
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; dbGaP DUA via Kids First Data Access Committee

provenance.maintainer: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (DRC) + NIH Common Fund

relevance.why: Pediatric tumors (fusion-driven, low-TMB) stress-test antigen pipelines built on adult cancers and add fusion-neoantigen and germline-predisposition context.

agent_access: Summary/metadata browsable openly via the Portal (and its API). Individual-level data require a dbGaP Data Access Request approved by the Kids First DAC; approved data are pushed to CAVATICA (Seven Bridges) for in-cloud analysis rather than local download.
caveats: Controlled tier under pediatric dbGaP DUA; analysis is cloud-native (CAVATICA), not a simple download. Separate proposal/submission step beyond the dbGaP request.

name: Liu et al. 2019 — metastatic melanoma anti-PD-1 integrative (WES/RNA-seq)
description: Large integrative anti-PD-1 melanoma cohort (including prior-CTLA-4-treated patients) with WES and RNA-seq and clinical modeling; showed TMB's predictive value is confounded by melanoma subtype and prior therapy.
scale: 144 patients WES; 121 RNA-seq
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP DUA)

provenance.maintainer: Van Allen lab, Dana-Farber / Broad; Schadendorf (Essen)

relevance.why: One of the larger single anti-PD-1 melanoma cohorts with matched WES+RNA — good power for antigen/expression response modeling and for studying TMB confounders.

agent_access: Reads controlled via dbGaP phs000452.v3.p1; supplementary clinical/mutation tables and a companion GitHub repo (vanallenlab/schadendorf-pd1) hold processed data and code (open).
caveats: Shares the phs000452 accession with Van Allen 2015 — overlapping patients; dedupe before pooling. Controlled DUA for reads.

name: Canine Lymphoma Exomes, 3 Breeds (Elvers 2015)
description: Matched tumor-normal exome sequencing of lymphomas from boxer (T-cell), cocker spaniel (B-cell), and golden retriever (mixed); Roche custom 50 Mb canine exome; Broad-sequenced. Showed breed-specific somatic patterns.
scale: tumor-normal exomes across 3 breeds

relevance.why: Breed-stratified lymphoma mutation sets; germline-background effect on somatic patterns.

agent_access: SRA; accession in paper supplement (not surfaced in search — VERIFY exact PRJNA).
caveats: Accession VERIFY (check supp http://genome.cshlp.org/content/suppl/2015/09/16/gr.194449.115.DC1). CanFam3.1-era.

name: Mariathasan et al. 2018 — IMvigor210 urothelial atezolizumab (RNA-seq/WES)
description: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma treated with atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1) in the IMvigor210 trial, with RNA-seq, mutation data and response; linked TGF-beta signaling in fibroblasts to immune exclusion and non-response.
scale: ~348 patients with RNA-seq (298-348 depending on modality)
license: Processed data: Genentech IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package (custom terms); raw: EGA DUA

relevance.why: Widely used urothelial ICI benchmark; the processed expression+clinical R package is a near-open resource for validating response/expression models outside melanoma.

agent_access: Processed gene-expression + clinical data distributed as the IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package (download + install, scriptable). Raw sequence data controlled in EGA EGAS00001002556 (DAC approval + pyega3).
caveats: R-package terms are custom (academic reuse widely practiced). EGA accession appears with some variation across re-analyses (EGAS00001002556 vs others) — verify the intended modality/accession.

name: Canine MCT Laser-Capture-Microdissection RNA-seq (Sci Rep 2026)
description: RNA sequencing of neoplastic mast cells isolated by laser-capture microdissection from FFPE biopsies of 32 canine cutaneous mast cell tumours across grades, reporting grade-associated molecular alterations with reduced stromal contamination.
scale: 32 canine cutaneous MCTs (LCM RNA-seq)

relevance.why: Purest available primary-MCT expression signal (tumour cells only), ideal for MCT-specific marker and antigen discovery once the deposit is located.

caveats: NOT YET VERIFIED: the Nature article page is access-gated and the repository accession (likely GEO/SRA) was not surfaced in its visible data-availability text — retrieve the exact accession from the full-text Data Availability section before use. Catalogued here so the dataset is tracked; mark access unconfirmed until the ID resolves.

name: Miao 2018 clear-cell renal carcinoma ICB cohort
description: Whole-exome (+ clinical) profiling of metastatic clear-cell RCC treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, linking PBRM1 loss and genomic features to response. Response-annotated; processed data mirrored on cBioPortal.
scale: WES; validation cohort ~63 ccRCC patients on PD-1/PD-L1 +/- CTLA-4 blockade
license: cBioPortal data: open (ODC-ODbL / free reuse); dbGaP raw: controlled

provenance.maintainer: Miao/Van Allen et al., Dana-Farber / Broad

relevance.why: Non-melanoma (RCC) ICB response cohort broadens tumor-type coverage for neoantigen/response modeling.

agent_access: Processed mutations/clinical openly on cBioPortal datahub (GitHub) — agent-fetchable, no auth. Raw sequence via dbGaP (controlled). Prefer cBioPortal for open reuse.
caveats: Raw reads controlled; cBioPortal copy is processed-level and openly reusable. Confirm the exact cBioPortal study id.

name: Miao et al. 2018 — immune checkpoint response in clear-cell RCC (WES)
description: Whole-exome sequencing of clear-cell (and other) renal-cell carcinoma treated with PD-1/ PD-L1 or CTLA-4 blockade, with response annotation; identified truncating PBRM1 mutations associated with ICI benefit in ccRCC.
scale: ~35 ccRCC (plus additional non-ccRCC); WES + matched normal
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP DUA)

relevance.why: Extends antigen/response modeling to a low-TMB cancer (RCC) where response is driven more by specific driver loss than by bulk neoantigen load.

agent_access: Reads controlled via dbGaP phs001493 (approved DAR + token). Summary MAF/clinical in supplement. Cite v3.p1 for the live record.
caveats: Controlled DUA. Low-TMB disease — a useful negative/edge case for TMB-centric predictors.

name: MSK-IMPACT Clinical Sequencing Cohort (public release)
description: Public, de-identified release of Memorial Sloan Kettering's targeted panel sequencing of >10,000 advanced-cancer patients (Zehir et al. 2017), with mutation, copy-number and structural-variant calls plus clinical annotation. Hosted openly on cBioPortal (msk_impact_2017); larger MSK-MET and later releases also public.
scale: 10,336 patients / 10,945 tumors (2017 release); larger in later MSK releases
license: Open for scientific use via cBioPortal (ODbL-governed hosting); cite Zehir et al.

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; hosted on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Very large real-world advanced/metastatic cohort with hotspot-focused calls — good for recurrence priors on actionable/shared antigens, though panel-limited for exome-wide neoantigen discovery.

agent_access: Fully open via the cBioPortal API and study ZIP — no auth. Programmatic and bulk-friendly.
caveats: Targeted panel (341–505 genes), NOT whole-exome — captures only panel-covered variants, so it under-counts the neoantigen space. De-identified; redistribution follows cBioPortal (ODbL) + citation of the source paper.

name: MSK-MET (Nguyen et al. 2022) — pan-cancer metastasis genomics
description: Very large pan-cancer cohort (~25,000 patients) integrating MSK-IMPACT tumor genomics with detailed metastatic-site annotation to map organotropism and genomic correlates of metastatic spread; de-identified data released publicly on cBioPortal.
scale: ~25,000 patients across 50+ cancer types (targeted panel)
license: Open via cBioPortal (ODbL-governed hosting); cite source paper

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering; hosted on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Massive real-world cohort tying tumor genotype to metastatic behavior — useful for recurrence priors on actionable/shared antigens and for stage/site-aware target prioritization.

agent_access: Open via cBioPortal (API + study ZIP), no auth, automatable.
caveats: Targeted panel (not WES/WGS) — no neoantigen-level or expression data. Confirm the exact cBioPortal study id (expected msk_met_2021) on the datasets page before scripting.

name: Open Targets Platform
description: Not a neoantigen DB per se: a target-identification/prioritization platform integrating genetics, genomics, expression, and cancer evidence (e.g. Project Score CRISPR screens, Cancer Gene Census, Cancer Genome Interpreter). Relevant to this domain for antigen/target gene prioritization (tumor-associated antigen genes, expression specificity) rather than peptide-level neoantigens.
scale: Whole-genome target-disease evidence; quarterly releases (tens of GB bulk)
license: CC0 1.0 (platform data); code Apache-2.0; some source datasets carry own terms

provenance.maintainer: Open Targets consortium (EMBL-EBI, Wellcome Sanger, GSK, et al.)

relevance.why: Best-licensed (CC0) route to tumor-antigen TARGET prioritization — expression specificity, tractability and cancer evidence to rank candidate antigen genes before descending to peptide level.

agent_access: Fully automatable: GraphQL + REST API, EMBL-EBI FTP, Google Cloud/BigQuery, and an AWS S3 bucket (open-targets-public-data-releases) listable without an account. No auth for public data.
caveats: Platform data are CC0 (excellent for reuse/ML), but the licence page notes individual source datasets have their own terms — e.g. Cancer Gene Census is "commercial use for Open Targets" (NOT free commercial reuse); check per-source terms before commercial use. Gene/target level, not peptide/neoantigen level.

name: PCAWG (Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes)
description: Uniform whole-genome analysis of 2,658 cancers (tumor + matched normal) across 38 tumor types, jointly from ICGC and TCGA. Deep catalog of coding and non-coding somatic drivers, structural variants, mutational signatures and whole-genome expression. Most molecular, clinical and specimen summaries are open; identifying data (germline alleles, raw reads) are controlled via both TCGA (dbGaP) and ICGC (DACO).
scale: 2,658 donors / whole genomes, 38 tumor types

relevance.why: Only large uniform WGS cohort covering non-coding and structural variants — essential for antigens arising outside the exome (SV junctions, non-coding drivers, retained introns) that WES-only cohorts miss.

agent_access: Open molecular/consensus files (VCF/MAF) via ICGC DCC and mirrors (UCSC Xena PCAWG hub is fully open, no auth). Controlled germline/reads need dbGaP (TCGA portion) AND DACO (ICGC portion) plus token/EGA clients.
caveats: Somatic SNVs from TCGA donors require separate dbGaP authorization even within the open workflow. Dual-consortium access is the main automation barrier for read-level data.

name: PetDx OncoK9 — Canine cfDNA Liquid Biopsy (NOT public)
description: Commercial multi-cancer early-detection liquid biopsy using plasma cell-free DNA NGS in dogs (CLASSiC prospective screening study; >1,100-dog clinical validation). Catalogued for completeness; underlying data are proprietary and there is conflicting evidence the product/company may have wound down in 2024.
scale: >1,100 dogs (validation); CLASSiC prospective cohort

relevance.why: Demonstrates canine cfDNA feasibility; relevant to monitoring, not to presentation/recognition modeling. No usable public data.

agent_access: No public dataset, no API. Publications only.
caveats: Proprietary and NOT redistributable; reports of 2024 discontinuation conflict with 2026 pubs — verify company status before relying on it. Included only to mark the boundary of what is public.

name: PRJEB12081 — Canine Oral Melanoma (ENA; Hendricks)
description: ENA-hosted canine oral melanoma sequencing used in pan-tumor TMB/TP53 reanalyses; part of the canonical reusable canine WES/WGS set.
scale: oral melanoma cohort

relevance.why: Reusable melanoma WES/WGS for mutation/neoantigen pipelines.

agent_access: ENA bulk FASTQ (Aspera/FTP); no auth.
caveats: Reanalysis paper notes missing patient info (breed). Older reference build.

name: PRJNA1090544 — Canine Oral Mucosal Melanoma Exomes
description: Exome sequencing of canine oral mucosal melanomas compared with human melanoma mutation spectra.
scale: oral mucosal melanoma exome cohort

relevance.why: Melanoma mutation landscape; canine oral melanoma is a lead immunotherapy indication (cf. Oncept vaccine) — high-value for presentation/neoantigen work.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: VERIFY accession; mucosal (not UV-driven) melanoma — lower TMB than human cutaneous.

name: PRJNA1154710 — Canine Oral Osteosarcoma Genomics
description: Genomic landscape of canine oral osteosarcoma; confirms SETD2 and DMD among genes mutated in ~half of samples, paralleling appendicular OSA (Gardner et al.).
scale: oral OSA tumor-normal set

relevance.why: Somatic OSA variants for neoantigen candidates; recurrent SETD2/DMD biology.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ (prefetch); no auth.
caveats: Gardner et al. (2019) SETD2/DMD appendicular-OSA genome accession not confirmed here — check that paper's data-availability directly.

name: PRJNA1399620 — Canine Hemangiosarcoma Organoid RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of 5 HSA and 5 nodular-hyperplasia patient-derived 2.5D organoid lines (orthotopic xenograft study).
scale: 10 organoid lines (RNA-seq)

relevance.why: Organoid models as functional antigen-presentation substrates.

agent_access: SRA; no auth. BioSamples SAMN54501156+.
caveats: Organoid (not primary tumor) expression. VERIFY.

name: PRJNA268531 / SRP050276 — TRAF3 in Canine+Human B-cell Lymphoma
description: Sequencing from a study of TRAF3 genetic inactivation in canine and human B-cell lymphoma.
scale: canine + human lymphoma samples

relevance.why: Cross-species shared driver (TRAF3) evidence.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: DOI VERIFY; older CanFam3.1-era data.

name: PRJNA376380 / PRJNA562916 / GSE95183 — Canine HSA RNA-seq Subtypes
description: RNA-seq/microarray defining canine hemangiosarcoma molecular subtypes (angiogenic, inflammatory, adipogenic); basis for ML gene-signature work.
scale: multi-cohort HSA transcriptomes

relevance.why: Subtype-resolved HSA expression; immune (inflammatory) subtype relevant to recognition.

agent_access: GEO + SRA; no auth.
caveats: Mixed platforms; batch effects. VERIFY per-accession mapping.

name: PRJNA421895 — Canine Oral Melanoma Whole-Transcriptome
description: RNA-seq whole-transcriptome profiling of canine oral melanoma (radiotherapy effect + outcome gene signature).
scale: oral melanoma RNA-seq cohort

relevance.why: Expression context for melanoma antigens and immune signatures.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Expression only. VERIFY accession.

name: PRJNA448733 / PRJNA685036 / PRJNA1007700 — Shetland Sheepdog iUC Genomes
description: Whole-genome (PRJNA448733, PRJNA685036) and whole-tumor (PRJNA1007700) sequencing from the Shetland-sheepdog invasive urothelial carcinoma GWAS/NIPAL1 study; arrays GSE241367, ChIP-seq GSE254079.
scale: iUC WGS + arrays + ChIP-seq

relevance.why: Germline + somatic + regulatory layers for bladder cancer; breed-predisposition genetics.

agent_access: SRA + GEO; no auth.
caveats: Spread across multiple accessions; join carefully.

name: PRJNA489159 / SRP159481 — Canine Mammary Tumor WES + WTS
description: Whole-exome (197 dogs) and whole-transcriptome (158 dogs) sequencing of canine mammary gland tumors with matched controls (185/197 WES and 64/158 WTS matched). Scientific Data resource.
scale: WES 197 dogs; WTS 158 dogs

relevance.why: Large matched WES+RNA-seq mammary resource; strong substrate for neoantigen + expression pipelines.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth. Single-sample example SRX4636206.
caveats: WES and RNA-seq sample sets differ; partial matched normals.

name: PRJNA503864 / PRJNA503860 — Canine Cancer Cell-Line WES
description: Whole-exome sequencing of ~33 canine cancer cell lines (osteosarcoma, lymphoma, melanoma, hemangiosarcoma, others) for druggable-target discovery; matched normal/stroma under PRJNA503860. Underlies ICDC TCL01.
scale: ~33 cell lines (WES)

relevance.why: Cell lines are the most practical substrate for generating canine immunopeptidome data in-house.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: No DLA typing; cell-line genotypes drift.

name: PRJNA518003 / PRJNA576344 — Canine Mast Cell Tumour Exomes + Gene Panel (Vozdova 2020)
description: Whole-exome sequencing of canine cutaneous mast cell tumours identifying recurrent somatic mutations in 87 genes, including 10 recognized human cancer drivers (Vozdova et al., Vet Comp Oncol 2020). Exome reads are under BioProject PRJNA518003; targeted gene-panel NGS under PRJNA576344. Beyond the well-known KIT, the study flags additional recurrently mutated genes.
scale: canine MCT exomes + targeted panel

provenance.maintainer: Institute of Animal Genetics and Biotechnology / Veterinary Research Institute, Czechia

relevance.why: Mast cell tumour is one of the most common canine skin cancers and a priority under-covered tumour type; the somatic mutation set supplies candidate canine neoantigen loci beyond KIT.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (INSDC/NCBI open). Exome, not RNA — pair with MCT expression data for neoantigen prioritization. Confirm sample-vs-run counts on NCBI.

name: PRJNA552034 — Canine Hemangiosarcoma Exome (Megquier, 47 GR)
description: WES of 47 golden retriever hemangiosarcomas (+ RNA-seq of 74 multi-breed HSA) showing shared mutational landscape with human angiosarcoma (TP53, PIK3CA/PIK3R1). BioSamples SAMN12173468-561.
scale: 47 WES (GR); 74 RNA-seq (multi-breed)

relevance.why: Strong dog<->human (angiosarcoma) comparative mutation set for neoantigen modeling.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Separate RNA-seq accession may exist — check paper data-availability. VERIFY.

name: PRJNA559406 / PRJNA308949 — Canine Invasive Urothelial Carcinoma RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of 15 canine iUC tumors defining two expression clusters by BRAF V595E status (PRJNA559406); earlier iUC RNA-seq under PRJNA308949.
scale: 15 iUC tumors (+ earlier cohort)

relevance.why: Bladder-cancer expression clusters; BRAF-driven biology shared with human.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Small n; expression only.

name: PRJNA574196 — Canine Insulinoma Malignant-Progression RNA-seq (Sci Rep 2020)
description: Bulk RNA-seq characterizing malignant progression of canine insulinoma from normal pancreatic tissue through primary tumour to metastatic disease (Sci Rep 2020). Canine insulinoma is a spontaneous model of functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour.
scale: normal + primary + metastatic insulinoma (RNA-seq)

relevance.why: Covers a previously uncatalogued endocrine tumour type with a stage-progression axis (normal→primary→met) useful for progression-associated antigen/expression analysis.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Accession from paper data statement; the Nature article page is access-gated — reconfirm run counts on the NCBI record.

name: PRJNA579792 — Canine Glioma WES/WGS
description: Canine glioma WES/WGS deposited in SRA; part of the reusable canine tumor sequence set (distinct from ICDC GLIOMA01's integrated multi-omic release).
scale: glioma tumor-normal set (count VERIFY)

relevance.why: Glioma somatic variants; cross-reference with ICDC GLIOMA01.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: Study details/sample counts VERIFY at NCBI.

name: PRJNA648932 — Canine Multicentric B-cell Lymphoma WGS (Sparks 2020)
description: Whole-genome sequencing of six dogs with multicentric B-cell lymphoma treated with CHOP — first canine lymphoma WGS cohort.
scale: 6 cases (WGS)

relevance.why: Genome-wide somatic variant discovery for B-cell lymphoma neoantigens.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Only 6 cases. VERIFY accession at NCBI.

name: PRJNA677995 / PRJNA417727 — Canine Splenic HSA Exome (heterogeneity + actionable mutations)
description: Exome/deep sequencing of canine splenic hemangiosarcoma documenting extensive intra/inter-patient heterogeneity (PRJNA677995) and actionable mutations (PRJNA417727; PIK3CA, TP53, NRAS etc.).
scale: splenic HSA tumor sets

relevance.why: Druggable/actionable HSA mutations; heterogeneity caution for neoantigen calling.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: High heterogeneity complicates clonal neoantigen inference. VERIFY accessions.

name: PRJNA805123 — Canine DLBCL WGS (Fanelli 2025)
description: Whole-genome sequencing of 10 canine DLBCL cases expanding the aberration spectrum.
scale: 10 cases (WGS)

relevance.why: Recent canine DLBCL genomes for variant/neoantigen work.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Methods noted a publication-tied embargo — confirm current release status at NCBI before use.

name: PRJNA808112 — Golden Retriever B-cell Lymphoma Methylome
description: Genome-wide methylome of aggressive B-cell lymphoma in golden retrievers; reveals a conserved hypermethylome. Rare canine tumor methylation dataset.
scale: golden retriever DLBCL methylome cohort

relevance.why: Epigenetic context for antigen/gene expression in lymphoma.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: Methylation only. VERIFY accession.

name: Riaz et al. 2017 — nivolumab melanoma (pre/on-treatment WES/RNA-seq)
description: Melanoma treated with nivolumab, with paired pre- and on-treatment whole-exome and RNA-seq, enabling analysis of mutational/neoantigen dynamics and transcriptional change under PD-1 blockade.
scale: ~65-68 patients; 49 with RNA-seq (GSE91061)
license: GEO/SRA public submission (open); cite source paper

provenance.maintainer: Chan / Wolchok labs, Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: On-treatment timepoints capture immune-editing of the antigen landscape — valuable for modeling which presented antigens are under selection during therapy.

agent_access: RNA-seq via GEO GSE91061 (open); raw reads via the linked SRA project (SRA Run Selector), scriptable with no auth. Mutation/neoantigen tables in supplement.
caveats: Melanoma-only, modest size. SRP project ID not stated in-paper — resolve via the GEO series' SRA link.

name: Riaz 2017 nivolumab melanoma (GEO GSE91061)
description: Pre- and on-treatment tumor RNA-seq (and exome) of melanoma treated with nivolumab (anti-PD-1), response-annotated. Captures treatment-induced transcriptional change; a standard ICB response benchmark.
scale: RNA-seq: ~51 pre-treatment + ~58 on-treatment samples from ~65 patients on nivolumab

provenance.maintainer: Riaz/Chan/Wolchok et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Openly accessible paired pre/on-treatment ICB transcriptomes — useful for modeling response dynamics and neoantigen context without controlled access.

agent_access: GEO openly downloadable (GSE91061), no auth; raw reads via linked SRA. Automatable.
caveats: Open. Exome component may require SRA/dbGaP — verify if WES raw is needed. Count-per-patient vs sample differs (paired samples).

name: Rizvi et al. 2015 — NSCLC pembrolizumab (WES + neoantigen/response)
description: Non-small-cell lung cancer treated with pembrolizumab; whole-exome sequencing linking nonsynonymous mutation burden and candidate neoantigens to durable clinical benefit. One of the first demonstrations of TMB as a checkpoint-response biomarker.
scale: ~34 patients (two independent cohorts; WES)

provenance.maintainer: Chan / Rizvi labs, Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Canonical TMB/neoantigen-vs-response NSCLC dataset for benchmarking neoantigen callers against clinical benefit outside melanoma.

agent_access: Mutation annotation files (MAF), clinical and neoantigen tables are in the paper's supplementary materials (downloadable). No confirmed raw-read repository deposit.
caveats: Very small. License for the supplementary data is not explicitly stated (mark unknown); reuse likely requires citing the paper. Confirm whether raw reads were later deposited to dbGaP before relying on read-level data.

name: Rizvi 2015 NSCLC anti-PD-1 mutational landscape
description: Whole-exome sequencing of non-small-cell lung cancer treated with pembrolizumab across two cohorts, establishing nonsynonymous TMB / neoantigen burden as a correlate of PD-1 blockade benefit. Response-annotated tumor exomes.
scale: WES, discovery n=16 + validation n=18 NSCLC; nonsyn-TMB threshold ~178

provenance.maintainer: Rizvi/Chan et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Landmark TMB/neoantigen-vs-ICB-response dataset in NSCLC — a key cross-tumor-type benchmark beyond melanoma.

agent_access: UNRESOLVED: no public repository accession located in the Data Availability (dbGaP/ENA not confirmed). Likely controlled or on-request. Mutation tables are in the paper's supplement (openly readable).
caveats: download_url + license unknown; raw-data location unverified — treat as controlled/on-request until confirmed. Small cohort. Use the supplementary mutation tables for open reuse.

name: Samstein 2019 MSK-IMPACT pan-cancer TMB/ICB cohort (cBioPortal)
description: Targeted-panel (MSK-IMPACT) mutation + TMB + survival data across many cancer types, including ~1,661 checkpoint-inhibitor-treated patients, establishing TMB as a pan-cancer survival correlate after ICB. Openly released via cBioPortal / MSK data catalog.
scale: ~1,661 ICB-treated patients (+ untreated comparators); genomic + TMB + survival (MSK-IMPACT panel)
license: cBioPortal/MSK open release (free reuse; verify terms)

provenance.maintainer: Samstein/Morris/Chan et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Large OPEN pan-cancer TMB-vs-ICB-survival dataset — benchmark for TMB/neoantigen-burden signals across tumor types without controlled access.

agent_access: Open via cBioPortal (study id ~'tmb_mskcc_2018') and MSK data catalog (dataset 10452): download or REST/API. Agent-fetchable, no auth.
caveats: Panel (not WES) — TMB is panel-estimated, not full neoantigen calls. Confirm the exact cBioPortal study id before programmatic pull. License is an open release; verify specific reuse terms.

name: Samstein et al. 2019 — pan-cancer TMB & ICI survival (MSK-IMPACT)
description: ~1,660 ICI-treated patients across multiple cancer types profiled with the MSK-IMPACT targeted panel, with overall survival; established cancer-type-specific TMB cut-points for checkpoint-blockade benefit.
scale: ~1,661-1,662 ICI-treated tumors (targeted panel)
license: Open via cBioPortal (ODbL-governed hosting); cite source paper

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering; hosted on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Large real-world ICI outcome cohort for TMB priors and for calibrating per-cancer-type antigen-burden thresholds — fully open via cBioPortal API.

agent_access: Open via cBioPortal study tmb_mskcc_2018 (API + ZIP), no auth. Fully automatable.
caveats: Targeted panel (MSK-IMPACT), not WES — TMB is panel-derived; no neoantigen-level or expression data. A companion NSCLC study (nsclc_pd1_msk_2018) is separate.

name: Snyder 2014 CTLA-4 melanoma neoantigen exomes
description: Whole-exome sequencing of melanoma treated with CTLA-4 blockade, one of the first studies linking neoantigen landscape to checkpoint response. Response-annotated tumor exomes; neoantigen predictions in the paper.
scale: WES of melanoma from 64 CTLA-4-treated patients (discovery + validation)

provenance.maintainer: Chan/Snyder et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Early response-annotated neoantigen cohort for CTLA-4 blockade; cross-reference with Van Allen for anti-CTLA-4 neoantigen-vs-response modeling.

agent_access: CONTROLLED: raw sequence via dbGaP (secondary sources report phs000452.v2.p1 — VERIFY the exact Snyder accession on dbGaP/NEJM supplement, as phs000452 is primarily the Van Allen study). DAR/DUA required.
caveats: Accession attribution uncertain (reported phs000452.v2.p1 from a secondary source) — confirm before relying. Controlled-access. Mutation/neoantigen summary tables are in the NEJM supplement (openly readable).

name: Snyder et al. 2017 — urothelial anti-PD-L1 multi-omic (WES/RNA-seq/TCR)
description: Exploratory multi-omic analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma treated with atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1): WES, RNA-seq and TCR sequencing with clinical response; examined systemic and somatic factors in PD-L1-blockade response/resistance.
scale: ~29-30 patients (multi-omic)
license: dbGaP DUA (reads); cBioPortal open (processed calls); Adaptive immuneACCESS (TCR)

provenance.maintainer: Chan / Hellmann labs, Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Rare cohort pairing tumor genomics with TCR repertoire and ICI outcome — bridges antigen presentation to T-cell recognition in a non-melanoma cancer.

agent_access: Reads controlled via dbGaP phs001783. Somatic calls + CNA + clinical open on cBioPortal (blca_cmo_06155_2016, API). TCR data on Adaptive Biotechnologies immuneACCESS (snyder-2017-plosmedicine), free registration.
caveats: Accession/study-id from a secondary source — verify against the PLoS Medicine statement. Very small cohort. TCR data under Adaptive's immuneACCESS terms.

name: SRP137798 — Canine DLBCL Genomic Landscape (77 cases)
description: Genomic landscape of canine diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: RNA-seq + exome + genome across ~77 cases, defining clinically relevant subtypes.
scale: ~77 cases (multi-modal)

relevance.why: Largest multi-modal canine DLBCL resource; subtype-resolved mutations and expression.

agent_access: SRA; no auth. Reused by lncRNA follow-up studies.
caveats: DOI VERIFY; mixed data types need demultiplexing by sample.

name: St. Jude Cloud (pediatric cancer genomics)
description: Pediatric cancer genomic data-sharing ecosystem (PCGP, RTCG, Clinical Pilot and more) hosting paired tumor/normal WGS, WES and RNA-seq with clinical data, plus analysis apps. The largest public pediatric cancer genomics resource; raw sequence data are controlled behind a signed agreement and DACO-style committee.
scale: ~12,000 WGS, ~7,700 WES, ~2,200 RNA-seq samples (2020); ~12,000 total in portal
license: St. Jude Cloud Data Access Agreement (committee-reviewed; no redistribution)

relevance.why: Deep paired tumor/normal pediatric WGS+RNA — ideal for fusion- and SV-derived neoantigens and for validating that antigen pipelines hold in low-TMB childhood cancers.

agent_access: Browse/metadata open; raw data require a signed Data Access Agreement reviewed by a data access committee, after which data are accessed inside the DNAnexus-based cloud platform (compute-to-data) rather than bulk-downloaded locally.
caveats: Signed agreement + committee review; cloud-native analysis model. Portal and docs report slightly different sample totals — confirm current counts in the live Data Browser.

name: TARGET (Therapeutically Applicable Research to Generate Effective Treatments)
description: NCI pediatric cancer genomics program covering high-risk childhood malignancies (ALL, AML, neuroblastoma, Wilms tumor, osteosarcoma, kidney tumors). Multi-omic tumor/normal profiling with clinical outcomes, served through the GDC alongside TCGA.
scale: ~5,000 cases across ~6 pediatric cancer types
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs000218 for controlled data)

provenance.maintainer: NCI Office of Cancer Genomics; served via GDC

relevance.why: Pediatric tumors have low mutational burden and distinct driver landscapes; useful for testing whether antigen-discovery pipelines generalize beyond adult, high-TMB cancers and for fusion-derived neoantigen work (fusion-rich pediatric sarcomas).

agent_access: Same mechanics as TCGA via the GDC API: open derivatives tokenless; controlled reads via dbGaP phs000218 + GDC token.
caveats: Controlled data under pediatric dbGaP DUA; additional privacy sensitivity for minors. Smaller per-disease cohorts limit statistical power.

name: The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)
description: Landmark multi-omic atlas of ~11,000 patients across 33 cancer types, jointly run by NCI and NHGRI. Provides matched tumor/normal WXS, WGS (subset), RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, DNA methylation, copy-number and reverse-phase protein arrays with clinical follow-up. Now served through the GDC (harmonized) and the legacy portal; summary derivatives are openly downloadable, read-level and germline data are controlled.
scale: ~11,315 cases, 33 tumor types
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs000178 for controlled data)
last_updated: project complete 2018; harmonized releases ongoing via GDC

relevance.why: The best-characterized pan-cancer cohort for linking somatic variants to expression and immune context — foundational for antigen-discovery benchmarks and for training expression/immunogenicity models on diverse tumor types.

agent_access: Open derivatives (MAF, expression matrices, clinical) via GDC API, no auth. Controlled reads/germline need dbGaP phs000178 approval + GDC token. UCSC Xena / cBioPortal mirror processed subsets with simpler bulk access (see those entries).
caveats: Must cite per TCGA publication guidelines; controlled data under dbGaP DUA with institutional signing authority and study-specific terms. Batch effects across tissue source sites are documented and need correction.

name: TCGA MC3 somatic mutation calls (Multi-Center Mutation Calling)
description: The consensus, reproducible somatic-mutation call set for TCGA, produced by an ensemble of seven callers with artifact filtering (~3.5M variants across ~10,000 exomes). The de facto standard TCGA mutation table for pan-cancer analyses.
scale: ~3.5M somatic variants, ~10,000 tumor exomes (33 cancer types)
license: NIH GDS Policy; PUBLIC MAF open, CONTROLLED MAF via dbGaP (phs000178)

provenance.maintainer: TCGA MC3 working group / GDC; Ellrott et al.

relevance.why: The cleanest open pan-cancer somatic-variant table for enumerating candidate neoantigens across all 33 TCGA cancer types in one harmonized file.

agent_access: Public MAF (mc3.v0.2.8.PUBLIC.maf.gz) is a single open download from the GDC publication page / GDC API — trivially automatable. CONTROLLED and validation MAFs need dbGaP phs000178 + token.
caveats: Public MAF is filtered (some low-confidence/germline-risk calls removed) — the CONTROLLED MAF has the full set. hg19-based. Confirm the exact GDC file UUID at download time.

name: TCGA PanCanAtlas harmonized derived data
description: The curated bundle of batch-corrected pan-cancer matrices released with the 2018 PanCanAtlas papers: RNA-seq expression (EB++ adjusted), RPPA protein, 27K/450K methylation, miRNA, SNP6 copy-number segments, ABSOLUTE purity/ploidy and segmented CN, PARADIGM pathway activities, and the TCGA Clinical Data Resource (CDR) survival endpoints.
scale: ~11,000 tumors, 33 cancer types (multi-omic matrices)
license: NIH GDS Policy; listed derived files open, ABSOLUTE MAF controlled

relevance.why: One-stop harmonized expression + copy-number + purity + survival for all TCGA tumors — the substrate for antigen-expression filtering and outcome association without per-study wrangling.

agent_access: Individual files downloadable via direct GDC API links from the publication page (no auth) plus an ISB-CGC BigQuery mirror for SQL access. The ABSOLUTE somatic MAF is controlled (dbGaP). Fully automatable except that one file.
caveats: Files are release-frozen (2018); expression is EB++ batch-adjusted (document the normalization when combining with GDC current releases). Purity correction matters for variant-allele-frequency / expression interpretation.

name: The Cancer Immunome Atlas (TCIA)
description: Pan-cancer immunogenomic resource derived from TCGA (>8,000 samples, 20 solid cancers): precomputed immune infiltrates, immune-subset expression, cancer-germline antigens, HLA alleles, PREDICTED neoantigens, tumor heterogeneity, immunophenoscore (IPS), and clinical data. Free download. Predicted/derived, not experimentally validated.
scale: >8,000 TCGA samples across 20 solid cancers; per-sample HLA, neoantigen, IPS, infiltrate tables

provenance.maintainer: Trajanoski lab, Medical University of Innsbruck

relevance.why: Ready-made pan-cancer predicted-neoantigen + HLA + immune-context tables tied to TCGA outcomes — fast substrate for target triage and immune-context modeling without running the pipeline.

agent_access: Web portal with free download of the precomputed tables; no documented API. Automatable via table download. Underlying TCGA raw data are controlled (GDC/dbGaP) but these derived summaries are open.
caveats: license: unknown — no explicit data license stated; underlying TCGA data governed by NIH GDC terms. Neoantigens are PREDICTED (NetMHC-class), not validated. 2017 vintage — predictions reflect that era's tools/references.

name: Thorsson et al. 2018 — The Immune Landscape of Cancer (TCGA PanImmune)
description: Immunogenomic characterization of >10,000 TCGA tumors across 33 cancer types, defining six immune subtypes and releasing a large per-sample immune feature matrix (immune cell fractions, cytolytic activity, TCR/BCR diversity, neoantigen load, signatures).
scale: >10,000 tumors, 33 cancer types; ~160 immune features per sample
license: NIH GDS Policy; feature matrix open (derived); underlying controlled data via dbGaP

provenance.maintainer: TCGA PanImmune working group / GDC; Thorsson et al.

relevance.why: Directly provides per-tumor neoantigen load, immune-cell composition and TCR/BCR diversity alongside subtype labels — a ready-made immune context layer for prioritizing antigen targets and for recognition modeling.

agent_access: The per-sample immune feature matrix is an open download (GDC PanImmune page) and is mirrored/queryable via CRI iAtlas; no auth. Automatable.
caveats: Features are derived (deconvolution/signature estimates), not direct measurements — document the methods. Raw inputs remain under TCGA access tiers.

name: Van Allen et al. 2015 — anti-CTLA-4 melanoma (WES/RNA-seq + response)
description: Pretreatment metastatic melanoma biopsies with matched germline from 110 patients treated with ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4), with whole-exome and RNA-seq and annotated clinical benefit. A foundational cohort linking mutational/neoantigen load to checkpoint-blockade response.
scale: 110 patients (pretreatment tumor + germline WES; RNA-seq subset)
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP DUA)

provenance.maintainer: Van Allen / Garraway labs, Dana-Farber / Broad

last_updated: 2015 (phs000452; later extended by Liu 2019 to v3.p1)

relevance.why: Ground-truth cohort for training/validating neoantigen-based response predictors: somatic variants + expression paired with real checkpoint-blockade outcomes.

agent_access: Raw reads (WES SAM/BAM, RNA-seq FASTQ) controlled via dbGaP phs000452; needs an approved DAR + download token. Mutation/neoantigen summary tables are in the paper's supplement (open, directly downloadable).
caveats: Controlled DUA for reads. Small cohort; melanoma-only. v2.p1 vs v3.p1 (Liu 2019) overlap — dedupe patients if combining with Liu.

name: Canine DLA-DR15/DR12 class II immunopeptidomics
description: First immunopeptidomics-derived MHC class II binding motifs for two common canine DR alleles (DLA-DRB1*015:01 / DR15 and DLA-DRB1*012:01 / DR12), the only direct canine class II ligand data available.
scale: 838 DLA-DR15-associated + 644 DLA-DR12-associated peptides

relevance.why: The only canine class II presentation data - essential and currently almost unique for any DLA class II modeling.

agent_access: Peptide lists in paper supplementary files; raw MS likely in PRIDE (accession not confirmed at catalog time - search PRIDE for "DLA-DR" / Canis familiaris). Partly publisher-gated.
caveats: PRIDE accession and data license UNCONFIRMED - verify in the paper's data availability statement. Only two alleles. Extremely sparse (the canine class II gap).

name: Canine DLA immunopeptidomics (primary studies)
description: The small set of primary studies that experimentally define canine MHC (DLA) peptide-binding motifs via MS elution - essentially the only direct canine immunopeptidomics data available. Includes class I (DLA-88*50101) and the first class II motifs (DLA-DRB1*015:01, DLA-DRB1*012:01), plus a canine tumor-antigen presentation set deposited in PRIDE.
scale: DLA-88*50101: ~3,720 eluted peptides (~2,436 nonamers); DLA-DR15: 838; DLA-DR12: 644; tumor set under PXD074485

provenance.maintainer: Multiple academic labs; raw data via PRIDE/ProteomeXchange

relevance.why: The core experimental substrate for canine presentation modeling. Directly enables (and bounds) Veritope's dog immuno-oncology work; everything else canine is sequence-only.

agent_access: Raw MS via PRIDE (bulk, CC0); motif/peptide lists via paper supplementary files (per-publisher access). Fetchable but scattered across papers - requires assembly.
caveats: SPARSE by design: only a handful of DLA alleles characterized, mostly class I and a couple class II. No consolidated canine atlas exists. This gap is the key comparative-oncology constraint - likely a build-it-ourselves opportunity.

name: Canine marginal zone lymphoma single-cell + spatial atlas (GSE343505)
description: Longitudinal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of canine marginal zone lymphoma presented as a comparative-oncology model; deposited in GEO. TCR V(D)J content not confirmed from metadata.
scale: longitudinal scRNA + spatial cohort (GSE343505)

relevance.why: Adds canine tumor immune single-cell data for the dog comparative arm; candidate source if it includes V(D)J reads.

agent_access: Open GEO series GSE343505; matrices via GEO FTP/HTTPS, automatable.
caveats: TCR V(D)J inclusion NOT confirmed — verify in the GEO record before relying on it for TCR work. DOI not located. Dog.

name: Hoang/Griffith 2024 single-cell canine TCR repertoire (PRJNA742469)
description: First dedicated single-cell (10x) canine TRA/TRB V(D)J + scRNA profiling, covering healthy PBMC, healthy lymph node, melanoma PBMC and lymphoma lymph node — the strongest purpose-built public canine TCR dataset found.
scale: 16 samples / 11 dogs; 77,809 V(D)J-expressing cells; 5 samples with scRNA-seq

provenance.maintainer: Griffith labs, Washington University / University of Missouri

relevance.why: THE key public canine TCR resource for a comparative-oncology (dog) arm — includes canine melanoma and lymphoma samples and custom CanFam3.1 10x references.

agent_access: Raw scRNA/scTCR FASTQs open in SRA (SRP326193) under BioProject PRJNA742469; SRA Toolkit/ENA for programmatic bulk download. Custom canine reference at genomedata.org/10X_canine_ref/.
caveats: Not antigen-labeled (no canine epitope specificity). Small cohort. No canine VDJdb/McPAS equivalent exists; this plus SRA RNA-seq reanalysis is essentially the entire public canine TCR landscape.

name: Canine TCR repertoires from public RNA-seq (SRA)
description: Canine TCR repertoires reconstructed from public dog RNA-seq in the SRA using TRUST4/MiXCR with IMGT canine references, spanning blood, lymphoid, solid tissue and tumor samples; plus companion single-cell canine TCR V(D)J atlases of healthy dogs.
scale: ~1,808 RNA-seq samples (1,361 PE + 447 SE) from ~1,063 dogs; 613 tumor samples

relevance.why: The only meaningful public canine TCR coverage found — essential for any comparative-oncology (dog) arm; raw reads are reprocessable with canine IMGT references.

agent_access: Underlying reads are public in SRA (programmatic via SRA Toolkit/ENA); derived repertoire tables depend on authors' supplements. Reprocessing is compute-heavy but fully automatable.
caveats: No single curated canine TCR database — this is reanalysis of scattered RNA-seq, so quality and annotation vary. NOT antigen-labeled. No canine equivalent of VDJdb/McPAS exists; canine coverage across all other resources in this domain is effectively zero. This is the key comparative-oncology gap.

name: Canine TCR repertoires reconstructed from public RNA-seq (SRA reanalysis)
description: Computational reconstruction of canine TCR repertoires from existing public dog RNA-seq in the SRA using TRUST4/MiXCR with IMGT canine references, across blood, lymphoid, solid tissue and tumors — the broadest (if indirect) canine TCR coverage.
scale: ~1,808 RNA-seq samples (1,361 PE + 447 SE) from ~1,063 dogs; 613 tumor samples

relevance.why: Largest-breadth canine TCR coverage (incl. 613 tumor samples) for the dog comparative arm; reprocessable from open reads with canine IMGT refs.

agent_access: Underlying reads open in SRA/ENA (programmatic via SRA Toolkit); derived repertoire tables depend on the preprint's supplements. Reprocessing is compute-heavy but automatable.
caveats: Preprint (verify peer-review status). Reconstructed from bulk RNA-seq (not targeted TCR-seq); quality/annotation varies. Not antigen-labeled. Dog.

name: NCI Comparative Oncology Program (COP) / COTC Trials
description: NIH/NCI Center for Cancer Research program running clinical trials in pet dogs with spontaneous cancer across a ~19-site academic network (COTC). NCI provides trial design, oversight and data management (C3D real-time capture); public correlative data flow into ICDC.
scale: ~19 sites; ~10 completed studies; ~450 dogs enrolled across recent trials
license: custom (data ownership often with drug sponsor; public subset via ICDC)

relevance.why: The institutional backbone of U.S. comparative oncology; a partnership/data channel, not a bulk dataset. Public outputs are already in ICDC.

agent_access: Program is not itself a downloadable dataset; raw trial data ownership often sits with the drug sponsor. Access public correlatives through ICDC; trial-level data by agreement.
caveats: Sponsor-owned data not redistributable; public access is the ICDC subset only.

name: PRJEB7734-PRJEB7736 / PRJNA288568 — CTVT + 186 Canid Whole Genomes (Decker 2015)
description: Whole-genome sequencing of CTVT tumours alongside 186 canid reference genomes (dogs, wolves, coyotes) used to reconstruct the CTVT somatic mutation landscape and evolutionary history (Decker et al., Genome Research 2015). Reads are split across ENA BioProjects PRJEB7734-PRJEB7736 (submitter deposits) and NCBI PRJNA288568.
scale: CTVT genomes + 186 canid WGS

provenance.maintainer: Transmissible Cancer Group, University of Cambridge; Wellcome Sanger Institute

relevance.why: Deepest somatic-mutation characterization of a transmissible canine cancer plus a large canid germline panel — a somatic/germline contrast useful for canine variant filtering and for understanding long-term tumour-genome evolution.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (INSDC open-access). Reads span multiple projects across ENA and NCBI; de-duplicate samples before combining. Large WGS — plan storage/egress.

name: SAMEA2358413 / SAMEA2358415 — Original CTVT Founder Genomes (Murchison 2014)
description: The two CTVT genomes first sequenced by Murchison et al. (Science 2014), which established the ~11,000-year origin and ~1.9M somatic substitutions of the CTVT clone (Australia and Brazil tumours). Deposited as ENA biosamples SAMEA2358413 (genome 1) and SAMEA2358415 (genome 2); reused by downstream CTVT studies.
scale: 2 CTVT tumour genomes (WGS)

provenance.maintainer: Wellcome Sanger Institute; Transmissible Cancer Group, Cambridge

relevance.why: Foundational CTVT genomes; anchor for mutational-signature and clonal-cancer comparisons across the canine oncology dataset.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (INSDC). These are sample accessions, not a BioProject — resolve to runs via ENA before download. Only two genomes; use with Decker 2015 panel.

name: NCI Integrated Canine Data Commons (ICDC)
description: NCI Cancer Research Data Commons (CRDC) node aggregating harmonized canine cancer data — clinical/biospecimen metadata, bulk RNA-seq, WGS, WES, genotyping arrays and DNA methylation — across spontaneous companion-dog tumors. Data come from the Comparative Oncology Program/COTC, PRECINCT, and individual canine researchers, structured to the ICDC data model and queryable by cohort. Current studies (12): COTC007B, COTC022 (appendicular osteosarcoma SOC), GLIOMA01 (comparative glioma), MGT01 (mammary/breast), NCATS-COP01 (canine-human transcriptomics), ORGANOIDS01 (urothelial organoids), OSA01 (osteosarcoma multi-platform), OSA03 (human+canine osteosarcoma WGBS), TCL01 (canine cancer cell-line WES), UBC01 (vemurafenib in BRAF-mutant bladder cancer), UBC02 (urothelial subtypes + immune signatures), UC01 (urothelial WES, BRAF-V595E-negative).
scale: ~35 TB; ~11-12 studies, ~678 cases, ~937 samples (figures vary by release)
license: custom (open access; use with attribution; no named SPDX license)

provenance.maintainer: NCI Center for Biomedical Informatics & Information Technology (CBIIT) / CRDC

last_updated: 2026-06 (CRDC update: +44 COTC022 files, Data Model Navigator refresh)

relevance.why: Primary open canine oncology multi-omics resource; anchors Veritope's comparative strategy. Rich on genomics/transcriptomics but carries NO MHC-ligand, immunopeptidome or TCR data — a gap we must fill from elsewhere or generate ourselves.

agent_access: REST API + web portal; cohort building then analysis in CRDC Cloud (Seven Bridges Cancer Genomics Cloud). Metadata queryable programmatically; large sequence files (BAM/VCF) are cloud-hosted. No login for open data; no documented hard rate limits but prefer the API over scraping the Angular SPA (the HTML is JS-rendered and returns no content to plain fetchers).
caveats: No explicit SPDX license — "open access with attribution" only; confirm redistribution terms per study. Per-study case/sample counts not exposed on static pages (need API/portal). Portal is a single-page app, so direct curl of /#/explore yields no data — use the API.

name: ICDC COTC007B
description: COTC preclinical trial comparing three indenoisoquinoline (topoisomerase-I inhibitor) drug candidates in tumor-bearing dogs, with pharmacodynamic/correlative data. Early ICDC clinical-trial study.
scale: small trial cohort (tumor-bearing dogs)

relevance.why: Demonstrates the COTC->ICDC data pipeline for PK/PD; no omics presentation layer.

agent_access: ICDC API / portal; open, no auth.
caveats: Clinical/PK only; no genomics or immune data.

name: ICDC COTC022 — Appendicular Osteosarcoma Standard-of-Care
description: Prospective COTC trial of standard-of-care in dogs with appendicular osteosarcoma; genomics + transcriptomics correlatives. Transcriptomes mirrored in GEO GSE238110 (see below). Actively updated.
scale: trial cohort (dozens of dogs); +44 files added 2026-06

relevance.why: Osteosarcoma is a flagship comparative (dog<->pediatric human) indication; clean trial-linked genomics for modeling tumor genetics, though no antigen-presentation layer.

agent_access: Via ICDC API / CGC; same access model as parent ICDC.
caveats: No immune/MHC data. Counts only via API.

name: ICDC GLIOMA01 — Comparative Canine/Human Glioma Genomics
description: Multi-omic molecular life-history study of spontaneous canine (and matched human) gliomas; the TCIA companion collection (ICDC-Glioma) holds imaging for the same subjects.
scale: ~81 subjects (multi-omic)
license: custom (ICDC open access); TCIA imaging CC BY 4.0

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC / The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA)
