relevance.why: Paired cross-species omics + imaging; strong template for comparative tumor-biology modeling.

agent_access: Genomics via ICDC API; imaging via TCIA REST API (NBIA) — bulk DICOM download supported.
caveats: No MHC/immunopeptidome/TCR layer; glioma is immunologically cold.

name: ICDC MGT01
description: Molecular comparison of canine mammary gland tumors and human breast cancer (genomics).
scale: genomics cohort (count via API)

relevance.why: Breast/mammary cross-species comparison; hormone-driven tumor biology.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No immune/MHC data. Counts only via API.

name: ICDC NCATS-COP01
description: NCATS/Comparative Oncology Program canine-human transcriptomics study for diagnosing/treating cancers.
scale: transcriptomics cohort (count via API)

relevance.why: Cross-species transcriptomic reference for drug repurposing.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No MHC/immune layer; counts via API.

name: ICDC ORGANOIDS01
description: Healthy and urothelial-carcinoma canine organoids for personalized-medicine modeling (genomics).
scale: organoid panel (count via API)

relevance.why: Organoids are candidate substrates for functional presentation assays.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No native immune data; counts via API.

name: ICDC UBC01
description: Clinical trial of vemurafenib activity in dogs with BRAF-mutant bladder (urothelial) carcinoma.
scale: trial cohort (count via API)

relevance.why: BRAF-targeted therapy response in dogs; translational to human BRAF cancers.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Counts via API; no immune layer.

name: Kaabinejadian/Yari 2026 canine & human tumor DLA/HLA immunopeptidome
description: The most substantial canine (DLA) class I immunopeptidomics release to date: DLA-bound peptides eluted from canine tumors (osteosarcoma, anal sac carcinoma, oral melanoma) and DLA-transduced mono-allelic cells, with matched human HLA data showing shared tumor antigen peptides across species.
scale: Canine tumors: e.g. 7,520 (oral melanoma, DLA-88*003:02/*006:01/*017:01), 1,335 (anal sac, DLA-88*004:02), plus DLA-88*501:01/*501:02; mono-allelic DLA cells
license: MS: CC0 1.0 (PRIDE default); RNA-seq: SRA BioProject terms

provenance.maintainer: University of Oklahoma HSC (Hildebrand lab); PRIDE + SRA

relevance.why: THE anchor canine presentation dataset for Veritope: real DLA-eluted tumor peptides across multiple DLA-88 allotypes, and direct evidence of canine/human shared tumor antigens - the cross-species bridge the thesis depends on.

agent_access: MS: PRIDE/ProteomeXchange PXD074485 (open, bulk-downloadable). Canine tumor RNA-seq: SRA BioProject PRJNA1428288. No auth.
caveats: Still only a handful of DLA-88 allotypes and almost entirely class I; DLA class II barely covered. Raw MS needs reprocessing. Nonetheless the richest canine source - directly addresses the canine data gap flagged across this domain.

name: PRJEB19508 — CTVT Regression RNA-seq (Frampton 2018)
description: Bulk RNA-seq of serial biopsies from canine transmissible venereal tumours (CTVT) undergoing vincristine-induced and natural regression vs. non-regressing tumours. The study (Frampton et al., Cancer Cell 2018) identified immune/inflammatory regression signatures and proposed CCL5 as a candidate driver of tumour rejection. CTVT is a naturally transmissible clonal cancer — a unique model of allogeneic tumour rejection and immune escape in an outbred canine host.
scale: serial biopsies, regressing + non-regressing CTVT (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: Transmissible Cancer Group, University of Cambridge (Murchison lab)

relevance.why: Rare in vivo transcriptomic record of spontaneous immune-mediated tumour regression against an allogeneic (foreign-genotype) tumour; directly informs what a successful anti-tumour immune response looks like at the expression level.

agent_access: ENA bulk FASTQ over HTTPS/FTP via Browser API or Aspera, no auth. Programmatic filereport endpoint (result=read_run) returns run accessions and download paths.
caveats: No explicit reuse license (ENA/INSDC open-access policy applies; cite the paper). CTVT is clonal — tumour genotype differs from the host dog, so host-matched analyses require care. Confirm run-level accessions on the ENA record before bulk pull.

name: SRP046723 — Canine Oral / Head-and-Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (PLoS Genet 2015)
description: Sequencing of canine spontaneous head-and-neck / oral squamous cell carcinomas shown to recapitulate their human counterparts at the molecular level (PLoS Genetics 2015). SRA study SRP046723.
scale: canine HNSCC/OSCC cohort

relevance.why: Explicit canine-human HNSCC molecular-equivalence dataset; a template for the cross-species validity argument central to the comparative-oncology thesis.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Confirm exact assay/sample composition on the SRA study record; accession taken from downstream citation.

name: AntiJen v2.0 — quantitative immunology database (TAP, proteasome, MHC)
description: Database integrating quantitative functional, thermodynamic, kinetic, biophysical and cellular immunology measurements, including peptide binding to TAP transporters and proteasome cleavage/ processing data, alongside peptide-MHC and TCR/antibody binding. A primary source of antigen- processing (TAP transport + proteasomal cleavage) training data; successor to JenPep.
scale: ~24,000-31,000 curated entries from published experiments

relevance.why: Rare source of quantitative TAP-transport and proteasome-cleavage data — the processing steps that gate which non-canonical/spliced sequences can ever reach HLA.

agent_access: Web search interface only (per-category search pages); no bulk-download/API documented — likely requires scraping. RRID:SCR_001750.
caveats: NO explicit license (flag). Legacy resource (core data ~2005, not actively updated); verify the ddg-pharmfac.net mirror resolves. Mixed species.

name: CCLE Quantitative Proteomics (Nusinow/Gygi)
description: Deep TMT mass-spectrometry proteomes of 375 CCLE cancer cell lines (>9,000 proteins per experiment across 42 multiplexes), complementing the CCLE transcriptomes. Lets predicted antigen source proteins be checked at the protein (not just mRNA) level.
scale: 375 cell lines; ~12,000 proteins quantified
license: Processed tables: with paper/DepMap (verify); raw files on MassIVE CC0 1.0

provenance.maintainer: Gygi Lab, Harvard Medical School; distributed via DepMap and MassIVE

relevance.why: Antigen presentation requires the source protein to actually be expressed and degraded; protein-level evidence across cell lines strengthens candidate-antigen prioritization beyond RNA, and ties directly to DepMap-matched lines for validation.

agent_access: Normalized protein-abundance CSV/supplemental tables are directly downloadable (no auth) from the Gygi lab page and DepMap. Raw MS (MassIVE MSV000085836) is CC0 but distributed via a Globus transfer that currently requires emailing the authors — not fully anonymous.
caveats: Values are ratios relative to internal bridge channels (not absolute) — normalize before cross-line comparison. Confirm the exact license on the normalized tables (CC0 is stated only for the MassIVE raw deposit).

name: CPTAC Proteogenomics (Proteomic Data Commons)
description: NCI Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium: matched proteome, phosphoproteome, whole-exome, whole-genome, transcriptome and clinical data across ~10 cancer types. Genomic files live in the GDC; proteomic (mass-spec) files live in the open-access Proteomic Data Commons (PDC).
scale: ~10 cancer types; thousands of samples (pan-cancer harmonized)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CPTAC; proteomics via PDC, genomics via GDC

relevance.why: Proteogenomics directly links the genome/transcriptome to the expressed, degradable proteome — the strongest evidence that a candidate neoantigen's source protein is actually made in the tumor; some studies also include direct MHC-ligandome data.

agent_access: PDC proteomics are open-access with a GraphQL/REST public API and per-file downloads — no login. Matched genomic reads sit in the GDC and may be controlled (dbGaP). Largely automatable for the proteomic/processed layer.
caveats: A Data Use Agreement is referenced for some content; raw-read genomic counterparts in GDC can be controlled. Proteomics is a few cancer types, not pan-cancer at TCGA scale.

name: GSE120272 — Canine C2 Mast Cell Line Transcriptome (G-quadruplex study)
description: RNA-seq of the canine C2 mastocytoma cell line (and a matched human line) profiling whole-transcriptome response to a G-quadruplex-binding small molecule (Zorzan et al., Sci Rep 2018). Provides a canine mast cell tumour in-vitro expression baseline and a directly paired canine/human comparison.
scale: canine + human mast cell line RNA-seq (treatment vs control)

relevance.why: Paired canine/human mast cell transcriptomes support cross-species expression mapping; a usable canine mast-cell-line reference for the MCT program.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Cell-line, drug-perturbation context — not a primary-tumour cohort. Small sample number.

name: Keskin 2019 personal neoantigen vaccine (glioblastoma; dbGaP phs001519)
description: Phase Ib personalized neoantigen vaccine trial in newly diagnosed glioblastoma; intratumoral neoantigen-specific T-cell responses measured. Tumor WES + bulk RNA-seq deposited in dbGaP; design used HLA-I-predicted peptides.
scale: Phase Ib GBM cohort; 7-20 predicted HLA-I-binding peptides/patient; WES + bulk RNA-seq

relevance.why: Personalized-vaccine evidence in a 'cold', low-TMB tumor (GBM) — stress-tests neoantigen design where antigen load is limiting; high value for a design program.

agent_access: CONTROLLED: WES + bulk RNA-seq via dbGaP phs001519.v1.p1 (DAR/DUA). Immunogenicity data in paper openly readable.
caveats: Controlled-access. Small phase-Ib cohort. Low-TMB setting limits neoantigen counts.

name: Canine Nasal Carcinoma Organoid RNA-seq (Front Vet Sci 2026)
description: Bulk RNA-seq of patient-derived canine nasal carcinoma organoids (n=6) vs normal nasal cells (n=4), used for drug-sensitivity testing and functional characterization of S100A2 (Yamamoto/Elbadawy/Sasaki, Front Vet Sci 2026). First organoid model for this tumour type.
scale: 6 NC organoid + 4 normal nasal samples (RNA-seq)

relevance.why: Fills the nasal-carcinoma gap and adds a canine organoid model; S100A2 highlighted as a candidate target.

caveats: NOT YET VERIFIED: data-availability statement says data are "in online repositories" with the accession in the article/Supplementary material; the repository ID (this group typically uses DDBJ/DRA) was not in the main text. Retrieve the exact accession from the supplementary files before download. Catalogued so the dataset is tracked.

name: NCI Surgery Branch neoantigen-reactive T-cell depositions (dbGaP phs003064 / phs002792)
description: Single-cell transcriptomic/VDJ (and CITE-seq) data of neoantigen-reactive T cells from metastatic human cancers, from the Rosenberg lab's neoantigen screening program. Experimentally VALIDATED tumor-reactive / neoantigen-reactive T cells with paired TCRs — recognition-focused. Multiple papers deposit under separate dbGaP studies.
scale: scRNA-seq + scVDJ / CITE-seq of neoantigen-reactive T cells across metastatic cancers (per-study cohorts)

provenance.maintainer: Steven Rosenberg lab, NCI Surgery Branch (NIH)

relevance.why: Real neoantigen-reactive TCR/transcriptome data for training recognition models and designing TCR-based therapeutics; gold-standard functional validation.

agent_access: CONTROLLED: dbGaP requires an approved Data Access Request / DUA and a PI with an eRA Commons account — NOT agent-fetchable without institutional approval. Related accessions: phs003064.v1.p1, phs002792.v1.p1.
caveats: Controlled-access (DUA) — redistribution forbidden; access gated. Verify each paper's specific accession; some supplementary summary data (TCR tables) are in the papers themselves and openly usable.

name: NFAT-reporter TCR-activation functional screen datasets
description: Datasets from reporter-based functional TCR-antigen screens (Jurkat/engineered lines with NFAT/NFkB/CD69 reporters, e.g. ACDC, TPR-KO, pMHC-pseudotyped-lentivirus library screens) that assign binder/non-binder or activation calls to TCR x pMHC pairs at scale. Functional (signaling) specificity labels rather than binding-only.
scale: study-dependent: e.g. ~7,173 binders / 17,020 non-binders (ACDC); 30k+ TCRs screened
license: per-publication; varies (often CC BY on bioRxiv preprints)

relevance.why: Functional activation calls (not just binding) give physiologically-grounded positive and negative TCR-pMHC labels — valuable complements to multimer/display data for recognition models.

agent_access: Data via journal/preprint supplementary tables + GEO/SRA deposits (fetch with GEO/SRA APIs per accession). No unified portal or API; per-paper harvesting.
caveats: Emerging/heterogeneous; many are preprints — accessions and licenses vary and some are unstated (mark unknown, verify per source). Reporter thresholds differ across platforms, so harmonize activation calls before pooling. Mostly MHC-I/CD8-focused.

name: Ott 2017 personal neoantigen vaccine (melanoma; dbGaP phs001451)
description: Phase I personalized neoantigen (long-peptide) vaccine trial in melanoma with immunogenicity readouts; the tumor WES + RNA-seq used to design the vaccines are deposited in dbGaP (accession added by a 2018 corrigendum). Links genomics to experimentally measured vaccine-induced T-cell responses.
scale: Phase I melanoma cohort; WES + RNA-seq (vaccine design) + T-cell immunogenicity readouts

relevance.why: End-to-end personalized-vaccine evidence (design genomics -> validated immunogenicity) — a template/benchmark for Veritope's design program.

agent_access: CONTROLLED: WES/RNA-seq via dbGaP phs001451.v1.p1 (DAR/DUA + eRA Commons). Immunogenicity tables in the paper are openly readable.
caveats: Controlled-access raw data. Original paper said "on request"; corrigendum added the dbGaP accession — cite the corrigendum. Small phase-I cohort.

name: Sahin 2017 personalized RNA mutanome vaccine (melanoma)
description: Phase I personalized RNA (mutanome) neoantigen vaccine trial in melanoma with poly-specific T-cell immunogenicity readouts — the BioNTech RNA-vaccine proof of concept. Design genomics + immunogenicity outcomes.
scale: Phase I melanoma cohort; per-patient RNA vaccines targeting up to ~10 mutations each

provenance.maintainer: Sahin/Türeci et al., BioNTech / University of Mainz (TRON)

relevance.why: Companion to Ott 2017 for the RNA-vaccine modality; immunogenicity data inform neoantigen selection/design.

agent_access: UNRESOLVED: no public repository accession located in the Data Availability — likely data-on-request from the authors (industry sponsor). Verify on nature.com/articles/nature23003.
caveats: download_url + license unknown; sequencing data may not be openly deposited (industry sponsor). Immunogenicity results in the paper are readable but raw data access uncertain.

name: Proteasome spliced/non-spliced peptide generation database (Specht et al. 2020, Mishto/Liepe)
description: Large curated database of in-vitro proteasome digestion products — both spliced and non-spliced peptides generated by purified proteasomes from synthetic polypeptide substrates — built for analysing and predicting proteasomal cleavage and peptide splicing. Antigen- processing training data underpinning spliced-epitope prediction. MS raw data on PRIDE + processed tables on Mendeley Data.
scale: Thousands of proteasome-generated spliced/non-spliced peptide products

provenance.maintainer: King's College London / MDC Berlin / MPI (Mishto & Liepe labs)

relevance.why: Ground-truth proteasome cleavage/splicing data for building and validating antigen- processing models that decide which sequences can be generated and presented.

agent_access: PRIDE (raw MS) + Mendeley Data (processed tables) bulk download, no auth. Article CC BY 4.0.
caveats: In-vitro proteasome products (synthetic substrates), not direct HLA ligands — bridges to presentation via processing models. Human proteasomes.

name: TESLA (Tumor nEoantigen SeLection Alliance) benchmark (Synapse syn21048999)
description: Consortium benchmark pairing patient tumor WES, tumor RNA-seq, and clinical-grade HLA typing with experimental T-cell validation of predicted epitopes — the reference dataset for benchmarking neoantigen prediction pipelines. Contains BOTH predicted candidates and experimentally VALIDATED immunogenicity (binding/immunogenicity outcomes).
scale: 6 subjects (3 metastatic melanoma, 3 NSCLC); 608 predicted epitopes experimentally assessed for T-cell binding

provenance.maintainer: Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy & Cancer Research Institute (Sage Bionetworks/Synapse)

relevance.why: The canonical open benchmark tying predictions to experimental immunogenicity — directly usable to validate and compare Veritope's neoantigen ranking/recognition models.

agent_access: Synapse requires a (free) registered account and acceptance of governance/conditions-of-use before download; programmatic access via synapseclient. Not anonymous bulk.
caveats: access: registration + Synapse governance/terms (not fully open); check conditions of use / any restriction. Only 6 subjects — small but deeply validated; a benchmark, not a volume source.

name: GSE306810 / GSE306811 — Canine Urothelial Carcinoma Organoid Biobank (2026)
description: A canine invasive urothelial (bladder) carcinoma-derived organoid biobank with RNA-seq deposited across GEO series GSE306810 and GSE306811, positioned as a comparative/ translational platform (Zdyrski et al., Clin Transl Med 2026; bioRxiv 2025).
scale: canine urothelial carcinoma organoid panel (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: Iowa State University (Zdyrski / Mochel / Allenspach group)

relevance.why: Living organoid resource for an under-covered tumour; complements iUC primary-tumour genomics already in the catalog and enables functional antigen/target validation.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Organoids (biobank access via the group may be request-based even though the sequence data are open). Two GEO series — check split.

name: CZ CELLxGENE Discover + Census
description: CZ CELLxGENE Discover aggregates standardized, Cell-Ontology-annotated single-cell datasets (including many tumor/immune collections) into a single queryable corpus. The Census is a versioned, deduplicated API layer over that corpus for slicing cells by tissue, disease, cell type and more without downloading whole datasets.
scale: Census LTS 2025-11: ~99.6M unique human cells, tens of M mouse; Discover >93M unique
license: CC BY 4.0 (platform); per-dataset collection licenses vary

relevance.why: The single best programmatic entry point for cross-study human single-cell slices: pull immune/tumor cell populations by ontology term at scale for reference building and model training.

agent_access: First-class Python and R APIs (cellxgene-census) over a TileDB-SOMA backend: query by metadata, stream matrices, fetch precomputed embeddings; no auth; versioned/reproducible releases (pin a Census version). Also per-dataset H5AD download. Excellent for automation.
caveats: Deduplicate with is_primary_data=TRUE to avoid double-counting cells shared across collections. Platform metadata is CC BY 4.0 but individual source collections may carry their own license — check collection-level terms before redistribution.

name: DICE (Database of Immune Cell Expression, eQTLs and Epigenomics)
description: Bulk RNA-seq expression (TPM) and eQTLs across ~15 sorted human immune cell types/states from healthy donors, plus epigenomic layers. Reference normal expression for immune cell subsets.
scale: 1561 RNA-seq samples; ~13-15 immune cell types/activation states; eQTL VCFs

provenance.maintainer: La Jolla Institute for Immunology (Vijayanand lab)

relevance.why: Immune-cell-specific normal expression and eQTLs — important because many tumor-associated antigens are shared with immune cells; helps avoid targets expressed in normal immune subsets and informs immune-context interpretation.

agent_access: Per-cell-type TPM tables + eQTL VCFs download from the site (HTTPS, no auth); no public API yet. Individual-level genotypes under dbGaP controlled access.
caveats: LICENSE CONFLICT (CC BY 4.0 vs CC BY-SA 4.0) — verify on the downloads License tab. No API. Individual genotype/eQTL data controlled (dbGaP). Blood immune cells only.

name: EMBL-EBI Expression Atlas
description: Curated, re-analyzed database of gene and protein expression across studies and organisms, with a Baseline component (tissue/cell-type expression, incl. reprocessed GTEx, HPA, FANTOM5) and a Differential component. Single-cell Expression Atlas adds cell-type resolution. A FAIR, harmonized normal-expression lookup across many reference datasets.
scale: Thousands of studies; baseline tissue atlases for human/mouse + many species

relevance.why: One harmonized interface to normal baseline expression across GTEx/HPA/FANTOM5 and more, reducing per-source parsing. Fast first-pass "where is this gene normally expressed" filter.

agent_access: Per-experiment TSV/MTX downloads over HTTPS/FTP; RNAseq-er API; Bioconductor ExpressionAtlas R package pulls datasets programmatically. No auth.
caveats: EBI terms of use are CC BY 4.0 for EBI-generated content, but imported datasets retain their source licenses (and the citation should credit the original study) — check per-experiment. Derived/reprocessed values (not raw). Confirm the exact 2026 NAR DOI before citing.

name: ENCODE (Encyclopedia of DNA Elements)
description: Comprehensive maps of functional genomic elements — transcription (RNA-seq, CAGE), chromatin accessibility (DNase/ATAC), histone marks and TF binding (ChIP-seq), methylation — across many human cell lines, primary cells, and tissues. Relevant here for baseline expression and regulatory context of candidate target genes.
scale: >650k experiments/files across human + mouse biosamples

relevance.why: Baseline expression plus regulatory activity (promoter/enhancer usage, accessibility) in normal cells helps interpret whether/where a target gene is active and regulated, supporting self vs. tumor-specific discrimination and antigen-source reasoning.

agent_access: Full metadata + file download via REST API (JSON) and batch-download endpoint; also mirrored on AWS Open Data (S3, no account). No auth. Rate limit ~10 GET/s per user/lab.
caveats: Terms allow free use incl. commercial, but cite per ENCODE policy. Not CC0 (the CC0 label in some registries refers to catalog metadata, not the data). Mostly cell lines; tissue coverage narrower than GTEx. No canine data.

name: FANTOM5 Promoter/Enhancer Expression Atlas (CAGE)
description: CAGE (Cap Analysis of Gene Expression) atlas of transcription-start-site and enhancer activity across a very broad panel of primary cells, tissues, and cell lines. Defines promoter-level and enhancer-level expression — useful for isoform/TSS-aware "is this promoter active in normal tissue" questions that gene-level RNA-seq can miss.
scale: ~1800 human + ~1000 mouse CAGE libraries; ~200k human CAGE peaks; ~65k enhancers

relevance.why: TSS/promoter- and enhancer-level resolution complements GTEx for detecting alternative promoters that could generate tumor-specific transcript variants vs. normal. Includes a dog CAGE component, aiding the comparative-oncology (canine) program.

agent_access: Bulk download over HTTP or lftp from datafiles/latest/ on fantom.gsc.riken.jp; BED/TSV expression tables, no auth. Reprocessed mirror at dbarchive.biosciencedbc.jp.
caveats: Dataset is stable/legacy (not actively re-released). Coordinates mostly hg19/mm9/mm10 — may need liftOver to GRCh38. Attribution: "FANTOM5 (c) RIKEN, CC BY 4.0".

name: Genotype-Tissue Expression Project (GTEx)
description: Reference of gene and isoform expression (bulk RNA-seq) across ~54 non-diseased tissue sites from nearly 1000 post-mortem donors, with matched genotype for eQTL/sQTL analysis. The flagship normal-tissue transcriptome baseline for defining where a gene is and is not expressed across the healthy human body. V10 is the current release; V11 re-annotates V10 against GENCODE 47 without new samples.
scale: ~17,000 samples, ~948 donors, 54 tissue sites (V8); V10 current

provenance.maintainer: NIH Common Fund GTEx Consortium (Broad Institute LDACC; portal hosted by Broad)

relevance.why: Primary "where is this expressed in normal tissue" filter. A candidate tumor antigen whose gene is broadly expressed across vital tissues in GTEx is a specificity/safety liability; low/absent normal expression supports tumor-selectivity.

agent_access: Open-access gene/transcript TPM and read-count matrices download directly from the portal over HTTPS, no auth. REST API v2 (gtexportal.org/api/v2) serves median and per-sample expression as JSON. Protected raw sequence + full donor metadata require an approved dbGaP application (phs000424.v10.p1), hosted on AnVIL/Terra (egress fees apply).
caveats: Post-mortem tissue (RIN/ischemia effects). Only summary expression is open; raw reads and genotypes are controlled-access via dbGaP — do not assume bulk fetch of individual-level data. No canine data. Portal terms, not a named CC license; cite the consortium.

name: Human Cell Atlas (HCA) Data Portal / DCP
description: The Human Cell Atlas Data Coordination Platform: a large, standardized archive of primarily healthy human single-cell datasets with harmonized metadata and portal-generated count matrices. Core reference for normal-tissue baselines that tumor single-cell data is contrasted against.
scale: tens of millions of cells across hundreds of projects

provenance.maintainer: Human Cell Atlas consortium / CZI / EBI / UCSC

relevance.why: Healthy-tissue single-cell baselines are essential to define tumor-specific deviations in antigen-presentation and immune composition.

agent_access: Azul REST web service for programmatic query; Data Browser bulk download via curl-style manifests; anonymous S3 (AWS Open Data) access to the bucket. No auth for open data. Preferred path is the Azul/Data Browser API, not direct data-store calls.
caveats: Portal homepage carries a CC BY-NC-ND notice for site content, distinct from the CC BY 4.0 that governs the datasets — confirm per-project page. Mostly healthy, not tumor, tissue. HCA-CLI being retired in favor of Data Browser bulk download.

name: HLA Ligand Atlas
description: A reference immunopeptidome of HLA class I and class II ligands eluted from benign (non-malignant) human tissues collected at autopsy/surgery, spanning many organs and subjects. Designed as a "normal tissue" baseline to subtract self-peptides when nominating tumor-specific targets.
scale: ~90,000 HLA-I and ~140,000 HLA-II ligands; 225+ samples; ~29 tissues; 21+ subjects; 51 HLA-I / 86 HLA-II allotypes
license: CC BY 4.0 (to verify on download page)

relevance.why: Critical negative/benign reference: a candidate tumor antigen presented on normal tissue here is a safety flag. Directly informs target triage for presentation and design programs.

agent_access: Flat-file downloads (peptide tables + metadata) directly fetchable, no auth. Site occasionally returns 503 under load; retry. Bulk-downloadable.
caveats: Data license not explicitly surfaced on landing page at fetch time (preprint/paper are CC BY 4.0) - verify on the data page before redistribution. Human only; no canine equivalent (a known gap for comparative-oncology baselines).

name: HLA Ligand Atlas (benign / normal-tissue immunopeptidome)
description: Reference of naturally presented HLA class I and class II ligands eluted from benign (non-malignant) human tissues across many organs and multiple donors, with paired HLA typing. The key normal-tissue immunopeptidomics "self-presentation" reference for filtering candidate presented antigens. (Note: an immunopeptidomics resource — cross-references the presentation agent.)
scale: ~227 benign tissue samples; tens of thousands of HLA-I/II ligands; DIA extension added

provenance.maintainer: University of Tübingen (Rammensee/Walz groups) and collaborators

relevance.why: Directly answers "is this peptide presented on NORMAL tissue?" — the most specific self-filter for target/epitope selection, removing candidates whose HLA ligands appear on benign tissue.

agent_access: Downloadable tables from hla-ligand-atlas.org; raw MS data mirrored on PRIDE (PXD020186) and MassIVE (MSV000096271) via FTP/Globus. No auth.
caveats: Data is CC0 (public domain) — unusually permissive; the paper text is CC BY 4.0 (don't conflate). Sample/ligand counts differ between preprint/published versions — note version. OVERLAPS the presentation agent's catalog; cross-reference rather than deep-duplicate. Donor HLA coverage is finite (not all alleles represented).

name: Human Protein Atlas (HPA)
description: Multi-section atlas mapping human protein expression across tissues (IHC), single cells, subcellular location, blood, brain, pathology (cancer), and immune cells, integrating antibody-based imaging with RNA-seq (incl. GTEx/FANTOM5 consensus). Gives both protein-level and transcript-level normal-tissue distribution per gene.
scale: >10M IHC images; ~20,000 genes; 40+ normal tissues; single-cell + blood atlases

provenance.maintainer: Human Protein Atlas project (KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden; Knut & Alice Wallenberg Fdn)

relevance.why: Protein- and cell-type-level normal expression and subcellular localization — directly informs whether a target is tumor-restricted and whether it is surface/presented. Pathology section links normal vs tumor expression for the same gene.

agent_access: Per-gene JSON/XML/TSV via query API (proteinatlas.org/ENSG...xml), plus bulk downloadable TSV files (normal tissue, pathology, subcellular, RNA consensus). No auth. Older versions at v##.proteinatlas.org for reproducible pinning.
caveats: Current license is CC BY 4.0 (older versions were CC BY-SA 3.0 / CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 — pin the version you cite). A few embedded third-party datasets carry their own terms (e.g. CC BY-SA). Antibody-based IHC has specificity caveats; use reliability scores. Images are large.

name: Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP)
description: NIH program building 3D, single-cell-resolution maps of healthy human tissue using multimodal spatial and single-cell assays (scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, CODEX/multiplexed imaging, spatial transcriptomics, imaging/MS). A reference for normal cell-type composition and spatial organization across organs.
scale: Thousands of datasets across ~20+ organs; multimodal, continually growing

provenance.maintainer: NIH Common Fund HuBMAP Consortium (HIVE / Pittsburgh HuBMAP IEC)

relevance.why: Spatial, cell-type-resolved normal reference helps localize whether a target's expression in normal tissue sits in vulnerable cell types (e.g. vasculature, neurons), sharpening on-target/off-tumor risk assessment beyond bulk tissue averages.

agent_access: RESTful search/entity APIs (registered at SmartAPI); bulk download via manifest + HuBMAP CLT and Globus Transfer API/endpoints. Portal viewing open; downloading requires free HuBMAP registration; external API access may need a Helpdesk request. Protected raw seq on dbGaP.
caveats: Download (not viewing) needs registration — note the auth step for any pipeline. Protected tier (PHI-bearing raw sequence) is controlled via an NIH Data Access Committee. File formats heterogeneous across assay types.

name: Human Proteome Map (HPM)
description: Draft map of the normal human proteome from high-resolution Fourier-transform MS of 30 histologically normal human tissues and primary cells (adult + fetal), reporting protein abundance across tissues. Web resource plus deposited raw data (PRIDE PXD000561).
scale: 30 normal tissues/cell types; ~17,000 genes with protein evidence; >290k peptides

provenance.maintainer: Pandey Lab (Johns Hopkins / Institute of Bioinformatics, Bangalore)

relevance.why: Direct MS evidence of protein presence/abundance across normal tissues — a protein-level self reference to check whether a candidate antigen's protein is detectable in normal tissue.

agent_access: Browse/download tables from the portal; underlying raw MS data as bulk download from PRIDE (PXD000561) over FTP/Globus. Portal download is simple; raw files are large.
caveats: No explicit license on the portal; the PRIDE record notes the authors ask that anyone considering COMMERCIAL use contact the PI (pandey@jhmi.edu) — treat as a redistribution/commercial-use flag for a company. Static 2014 dataset. Overlaps ProteomicsDB/HPA; dedup by gene/peptide.

name: A Quantitative Proteome Map of the Human Body (GTEx proteome)
description: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteome across 32 normal human tissue types using GTEx-project samples, enabling protein-vs-mRNA comparison across the body. Protein-level normal-tissue abundance reference tied to GTEx donors.
scale: 32 normal tissue types, ~12,627 genes quantified, 201 samples (GTEx donors)

relevance.why: Protein-level normal abundance across 32 tissues in the GTEx framework — directly checks whether a candidate antigen's protein is present (and at what level) in normal tissues, complementing transcript baselines.

agent_access: Bulk raw + processed files via PRIDE (PXD016999) over FTP/Aspera/Globus; MassIVE mirror (MSV000086387). No auth. Raw MS files are large.
caveats: Raw MS requires reprocessing for peptide/protein tables (processed supplements in the paper). Deposit-level terms, not a named CC license.

name: Draft map of the human proteome — raw deposit (Kim 2014)
description: Raw mass-spectrometry deposit underlying the Human Proteome Map: 30 histologically normal adult and fetal human tissues/primary cells profiled by high-resolution FT-MS. The raw-data accession behind the HPM portal (cataloged separately in domain-5).
scale: 30 normal tissues/cell types; proteomic evidence for ~17,000 genes

relevance.why: Raw-data provenance for the Human Proteome Map normal-tissue protein evidence; reprocessable for custom peptide-level self references.

agent_access: Bulk raw via PRIDE (PXD000561) / MassIVE (MSV000079514) FTP/Aspera. No auth. Large.
caveats: Commercial-use contact request attaches to the HPM resource (see domain-5 human-proteome-map). Raw only — reprocessing required. Overlaps Wilhelm/ProteomicsDB draft (dedup by peptide).

name: Marcu 2021 HLA Ligand Atlas raw data (PXD019643)
description: The raw MS deposition behind the HLA Ligand Atlas benign-tissue reference, plus a companion glioblastoma deposition that used the atlas as reference. The primary-data layer under the atlas portal cataloged in domain-1.
scale: 90,428 HLA-I + 142,625 HLA-II ligands; ~227 samples; 51 HLA-I / 86 HLA-II allotypes

provenance.maintainer: University of Tübingen (Marcu/Rammensee); PRIDE (MassIVE mirror MSV000096271)

relevance.why: Raw benign-tissue reference for building a self-peptide subtraction baseline from spectra rather than trusting the portal's processed lists.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD019643 (+ MassIVE MSV000096271); companion glioblastoma set PXD020186. Bulk-downloadable, no auth.
caveats: Companion glioblastoma samples are a SEPARATE accession (PXD020186). Human only; no canine benign reference exists anywhere (key gap).

name: Monaco immune cell RNA-seq reference (29 PBMC cell types)
description: RNA-seq profiles of 29 sorted immune cell types from healthy-donor PBMCs, with matched flow cytometry, designed as an absolute-deconvolution reference (ABIS). Clean normal immune-subset transcriptome reference.
scale: 29 immune cell types; 4 donors (S4 cohort) + PBMCs (S13 cohort)

relevance.why: Well-defined normal immune-subset expression signatures; a compact self reference to flag candidate targets expressed in resting/activated immune cells.

agent_access: Download count matrices from GEO (GSE107011) over HTTPS/FTP; no auth. Signatures via ABIS repo.
caveats: Blood immune cells only; small donor number. GEO deposit terms (effectively open, cite paper).

name: PanglaoDB
description: Secondary database of uniformly reprocessed public scRNA-seq samples (mostly from SRA) with cell clusters and cell-type annotations, plus a large curated cell-type marker gene resource. Useful reference for cell-type marker calibration and baseline composition.
scale: ~1,368 samples (1,063 mouse / 305 human), ~5.6M cells (site, 2026)

relevance.why: Marker-gene reference and reprocessed baseline samples for cell-type annotation QC in tumor-immune pipelines.

agent_access: Bulk download of all samples as a single tar archive + per-sample RData; marker gene table downloadable. rPanglaoDB R package (GPL-3) programmatically lists/downloads samples keyed by SRA (SRS) accession. No REST API.
caveats: License listed as CC BY 4.0 by a third-party catalog but not clearly stated on-site — mark license as reported, confirm with maintainer before redistribution. Static/largely unmaintained since ~2020; derived (reprocessed) data.

name: PeptideAtlas
description: Compendium of peptides identified by tandem MS across many experiments, reprocessed through a uniform pipeline into annotated builds (incl. a comprehensive Human build and Human Plasma), mapped to the genome. Provides observed-peptide evidence of the normal proteome and of which protein regions are reliably detectable by MS.
scale: Human build (2026-01) at very low PSM FDR; millions of PSMs; multi-GB files

provenance.maintainer: Institute for Systems Biology (Moritz lab) + collaborators

relevance.why: Observed-peptide atlas of the normal proteome helps judge MS detectability of a candidate antigen region and provides a self peptide/SRM reference; SRMAtlas aids targeted validation.

agent_access: Per-build bulk download (FASTA, TSV, MySQL dumps, coordinate files) over HTTPS; also query interfaces/APIs. No auth. Files can be large (coordinate file ~17 GB).
caveats: CC BY-NC 4.0 — NON-COMMERCIAL license; a flag for a commercial entity (check whether internal research use qualifies / seek permission for commercial use). Build-versioned; not all files carry all fields. Overlaps Human Proteome Map / ProteomicsDB.

name: ProteomicsDB
description: Mass-spectrometry-based protein expression resource quantifying protein abundance across human tissues, cell lines, and body fluids, with a draft human proteome, drug-sensitivity and kinobead data, and expression visualizations. Useful as a protein-level normal-tissue expression baseline complementing transcriptomics.
scale: >15,000 human proteins; tissues, fluids, cell lines; multi-omics layers

provenance.maintainer: Technical University of Munich (Kuster lab) with SAP

relevance.why: Protein-abundance-across-normal-tissues view to cross-check transcript-based expression and assess whether a target protein is present in normal tissues — specificity/safety evidence.

agent_access: OData v2 API (apiv2) returning JSON/XML via GET, no registration; legacy v1.1 API also public. Scriptable record-level access.
caveats: LICENSE AMBIGUOUS — some sources cite CC BY-NC 4.0 (no commercial use), others CC BY 4.0; confirm current terms on proteomicsdb.org before any commercial pipeline. API is per-query (not a single bulk dump). Overlaps HPM/HPA.

name: Tabula Sapiens (v1)
description: Multi-organ single-cell transcriptomic atlas built from individual human donors, spanning 24 tissues/organs with harmonized cell-type annotations. A benchmark normal reference for which cell types across the body express a given gene.
scale: v1: ~483k cells, 24 tissues/donors; v2 (2026): ~2x cells, 28 tissues, 24 donors

provenance.maintainer: Chan Zuckerberg Biohub / Tabula Sapiens Consortium

relevance.why: Cell-type-resolved normal expression lets you ask not just whether a target is expressed in a tissue but in which cell types (e.g. essential vs. regenerable), sharpening on-target/ off-tumor safety assessment beyond bulk GTEx averages.

agent_access: Processed H5AD via figshare (direct download) and CELLxGENE collection (Census/API accessible); also GEO (GSE306755) and AWS Open Data. No auth for processed data. Raw sequence data requires a data sharing agreement.
caveats: Processed/annotated objects (not raw reads) are the easy download. Donor count small; not every tissue equally deep. Dedup against Tabula Sapiens 2.0 (supersedes for many tissues).

name: Deep proteome & transcriptome abundance atlas of 29 healthy human tissues
description: Paired label-free quantitative proteomics + RNA-seq across 29 histologically healthy human tissues (from HPA project material), reporting protein and transcript abundance per gene. Protein-level normal-tissue reference with matched transcriptome.
scale: 29 healthy tissues; 13,640 proteins; 18,072 transcripts

provenance.maintainer: Küster lab, Technical University of Munich

relevance.why: Matched protein+mRNA normal baselines across 29 tissues — protein-presence self check and a resource to calibrate mRNA-to-protein inference for target prioritization.

agent_access: Bulk via PRIDE (PXD010154) / MassIVE (MSV000083508) FTP; data underlies ProteomicsDB. No auth.
caveats: MassIVE copy labels CC0 (very permissive) — confirm the PRIDE record's terms. Feeds ProteomicsDB (dedup). Raw needs reprocessing.

name: Mass-spectrometry-based draft of the human proteome — raw deposit (Wilhelm 2014)
description: Raw MS deposit behind the ProteomicsDB human draft proteome: a "human body map" of 36 tissues and body fluids plus a "missing proteins" collection, from 16,857 LC-MS/MS experiments. The raw accession behind ProteomicsDB (cataloged separately in domain-5).
scale: 36 tissues/body fluids; >16,800 LC-MS/MS experiments

provenance.maintainer: Küster lab, Technical University of Munich (with SAP/ProteomicsDB)

relevance.why: Raw-data provenance for ProteomicsDB normal-tissue protein evidence; reprocessable for self-proteome peptide sets.

agent_access: Bulk raw via PRIDE (PXD000865) / MassIVE (MSV000079526) FTP. No auth. Large.
caveats: Terms tie to ProteomicsDB (license ambiguous — see domain-5). Raw only. Overlaps Kim draft map.

name: Anthem (HLA-I binding predictor + curated set)
description: An HLA class I presentation/binding predictor and web server that also supports training custom models on user data. Its curated training set aggregates binders from IEDB, EPIMHC, MHCBN, and SYFPEITHI.
scale: Curated class I binder set aggregated from IEDB + legacy DBs

relevance.why: A benchmark predictor; mainly of interest as a comparison point rather than a data source (its corpus is largely re-derived from IEDB et al.).

agent_access: Web server; no documented bulk training-data download or API. Low agent utility as a data source.
caveats: No clear standalone training-data download or license - unknown. Underlying data overlaps heavily with IEDB; limited independent value.

name: BigMHC training & evaluation data
description: Training/evaluation splits for BigMHC (deep-learning HLA-I eluted-ligand and immunogenicity predictor), including el_train / im_train sets and MANAFEST immunogenicity data.
scale: EL + immunogenicity training/eval CSVs
license: CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley); code MIT + Zenodo archive

provenance.maintainer: Johns Hopkins (Karchin/Griffith labs); Mendeley + Zenodo + GitHub

relevance.why: Combines EL presentation with immunogenicity labels - useful for the presentation->immunogenicity step and as a modern DL benchmark.

agent_access: Mendeley (DOI 10.17632/dvmz6pkzvb.4) CSVs; code github.com/KarchinLab/bigmhc (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8023523). Bulk-downloadable, no auth.
caveats: Verify current Mendeley version. Human only. Derived from public EL data (dedup).

name: Canine DLA-88 NGS Genotyping / Novel-Allele Discovery
description: Sequence-based / next-generation DLA-88 typing studies reporting high rates of new-allele discovery and gene duplication (incl. 13 novel DLA-88 alleles), feeding IPD-MHC curation. Population-level DLA-88 allele content for dogs.
scale: dozens of DLA-88 alleles (ongoing discovery)
license: custom (EMBL-EBI/IPD terms; article refs CC BY)

relevance.why: Defines which DLA-88 alleles actually circulate in dogs — essential for prioritizing alleles for immunopeptidomics and for population-aware presentation prediction.

agent_access: Allele FASTA via IPD-MHC; study tables in article supplements. Small, bulk-downloadable.
caveats: GAP: DLA-88 gene duplication/copy-number complicates typing; no breed allele-frequency database; non-DLA-88 class I and all class II far less characterized.

name: High-throughput class-I pMHC binding via yeast surface display (Holec 2025)
description: Supplement for a yeast-surface-display platform that measures class-I peptide-MHC binding at scale: NNK benchmark libraries (quantitative enrichment/binding readouts across selected HLA-I alleles) plus pathogen peptide libraries (M. tuberculosis T7SS substrates, Dengue, Zika, SARS-CoV-2). Release includes raw + processed read counts, enrichment/rank tables, NetMHC predictions, oligo pools, and figures; raw sequencing at NIH SRA.
scale: NNK benchmark libraries across multiple HLA-I alleles + 4 pathogen libraries; archive 384.7 MB (page lists ~29.6 GB total)

provenance.maintainer: Holec et al. (Birnbaum lab, MIT); Zenodo + NIH SRA

relevance.why: A large, recent, CC BY quantitative pMHC-I binding screen (yeast display) — exactly the kind of high-throughput experimental binding set third-pass gap-filling targets; clean license makes it directly usable for model training.

agent_access: Zenodo anonymous HTTPS download (single 384.7 MB zip of processed data); raw reads via SRA. CC BY 4.0 permits reuse with attribution.
caveats: Zenodo statistics report ~29.6 GB total vs a 384.7 MB archive — the discrepancy is unexplained; verify whether additional files exist. Paper DOI not yet on the record.

name: IEDB MHC-I quantitative binding retraining & reliability benchmark (Kim 2014; BD2009/BD2013)
description: The curated quantitative peptide-MHC-I binding-affinity datasets used to retrain the IEDB prediction tools and to build the reliability benchmark of Kim et al. BD2009 (~137,654 measurements) and BD2013 (~179,692 measurements) span human HLA plus mouse H-2, macaque and chimpanzee alleles; a "Blind" set (BD2013 minus BD2009, similarity- reduced) and cross-validation partitions (cv_rnd/cv_sr/cv_gs) are included. Same page hosts the Wang 2008 MHC-II affinity set and Peters 2006 benchmark predictions.
scale: BD2009 ~137,654; BD2013 ~179,692 quantitative affinity measurements; multi-species HLA + H-2

relevance.why: The reference quantitative IC50 training corpus behind a generation of pMHC-I predictors; includes mouse H-2 affinities, giving a rare multi-species quantitative binding set for cross-species presentation modelling and benchmark reproduction.

agent_access: Direct HTTPS downloads of the zip/tar.gz; no auth. Note link text on the page differs from the real path (benchmark_mhci_reliability.tar.gz).
caveats: No explicit license stated on the IEDB datasets page; IEDB content is NIAID-funded and freely usable but lacks an SPDX tag here — confirm terms before redistribution. Overlaps with netmhcpan training sets and the stability set — dedup on peptide/allele.

name: IPD-MHC Dog (DLA) Section + ISAG DLA Nomenclature
description: The official curated repository and nomenclature authority for canine MHC (DLA) sequences, hosted at EMBL-EBI. Loci include DLA-88, DLA-12, DLA-64, DLA-79 (class I) and DLA-DRA, DLA-DRB1, DLA-DQA1, DLA-DQB1 (class II). Allele names assigned by the ISAG/Comparative MHC committee.
scale: class I: DLA-88 ~130+ alleles; class II loci tens-to-low-hundreds each (dog-specific counts not published as a single figure)
license: custom (EMBL-EBI terms of use; free for research)

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI (IPD) + ISAG/IUIS Comparative MHC Nomenclature Committee

relevance.why: THE canonical DLA allele reference — the backbone for any canine MHC-binding predictor, immunopeptidome allele assignment, and vaccine/epitope design. Central to Veritope's work.

agent_access: FASTA/flat-file downloads + EBI API; no auth. Small, fully bulk-downloadable.
caveats: GAP ALERT: DLA allele set is orders of magnitude smaller and less population-characterized than HLA/IMGT; DLA-88 dominates class I curation while other loci are thin. No allele frequencies by breed, and binding data are near-absent (see immunopeptidome entries). This sparsity is a core constraint for canine presentation prediction.

name: Legacy MHC databases (MHCBN, EPIMHC, dbMHC)
description: Historical MHC-binding/epitope databases that predate IEDB's dominance. MHCBN (binders/non-binders), EPIMHC (MHC-binding peptides/epitopes in real proteins), and NCBI dbMHC (HLA typing/allele + anthropology data). Catalogued for provenance and because older predictors trained on them.
scale: MHCBN: ~19,777 entries (17,129 binders + 2,648 non-binders), >400 MHC molecules; EPIMHC: thousands

provenance.maintainer: MHCBN: IMTECH (Raghava); EPIMHC: academic; dbMHC: NCBI (retired)

relevance.why: Mostly superseded by IEDB; relevant only for understanding legacy predictor training provenance and avoiding double-counting the same source peptides.

agent_access: Largely unavailable: NCBI dbMHC was retired; MHCBN/EPIMHC URLs may be dead or unmaintained. Not reliable for automated fetch - treat as historical.
caveats: Several of these are DEFUNCT or unmaintained (dbMHC retired by NCBI; MHCBN/EPIMHC frequently offline). No clear licenses. Content now subsumed by IEDB; verify each URL resolves before relying on any of them.

name: MHC Motif Atlas (binding specificities & ligands)
description: Curated database of MHC-I and MHC-II binding motifs, peptide length distributions, phospho-ligand motifs, multiple specificities, and links to X-ray structures, plus downloadable curated MHC ligand datasets. Derived largely from mono-allelic/deconvolved immunopeptidomics. Mix of curated experimental ligands and motif models.
scale: Thousands of class I and class II MHC molecules; curated ligand lists + motifs + PDB links

provenance.maintainer: David Gfeller lab, University of Lausanne / Ludwig Institute, Switzerland

relevance.why: Clean per-allele motifs and curated ligand lists (human, mouse, cattle, chicken) useful for benchmarking presentation models and sanity-checking allele motifs.

agent_access: Direct text/CSV downloads of all_peptides.txt and sequence files (paths observed via third-party tooling; confirm on site). No auth; bulk-downloadable.
caveats: CC BY-NC (non-commercial) per the Lausanne repository record - RED FLAG for a commercial company: non-commercial clause likely restricts commercial ML use. Confirm exact license text before training production models. No canine.

name: MHCflurry 2.0 (OpenVax) + training data
description: Open-source MHC class I binding-affinity and antigen-processing/presentation predictor. Unlike DTU tools, both the code and the full training data (BA, presentation, and antigen-processing CSVs) are openly released, making it the most agent-friendly trainable baseline.
scale: Training CSVs: ~hundreds of thousands of BA measurements + large MS presentation set
license: code: Apache-2.0; data: CC BY 4.0 (verify current Mendeley version)

relevance.why: Permissively licensed code + data: the cleanest starting point for a reproducible in-house presentation model and the easiest legal baseline to build on commercially.

agent_access: `mhcflurry-downloads fetch` pulls models/data; data also on Mendeley (direct CSV download) and GitHub. Fully bulk-downloadable, no auth. Most agent-friendly entry in this domain.
caveats: Class I only. Confirm the current Mendeley version's license field (v2 shows CC BY 4.0). Underlying MS data ultimately derives from public immunopeptidomics studies.

name: MHCflurry 2.0 training & evaluation data (Mendeley)
description: The openly-licensed CSV training data behind MHCflurry 2.0: separate binding-affinity, antigen-processing, and presentation-score training sets plus benchmark sets. The most permissively licensed ready-to-train HLA-I corpus.
scale: BA + AP + PS training CSVs (hundreds of thousands of measurements) + benchmarks

provenance.maintainer: OpenVax / Mount Sinai (O'Donnell, Hammerbacher); Mendeley Data

relevance.why: CC BY data + Apache-2.0 code = the cleanest legal foundation for a commercial in-house HLA-I presentation model.

agent_access: Direct CSV download from Mendeley (DOI 10.17632/zx3kjzc3yx.3) or `mhcflurry-downloads fetch`. Bulk-downloadable, no auth.
caveats: Class I only. Confirm current Mendeley version's license field. Underlying MS data derives from public immunopeptidomics studies.

name: MixMHCpred / MixMHC2pred (+ bundled data)
description: Motif-based MHC-I (MixMHCpred) and MHC-II (MixMHC2pred) predictors from the Gfeller lab, shipping with allele motif/definition files and an expanded multi-species training set bundled in the releases.
scale: MixMHC2pred built from >600,000 curated MHC-II ligands; bundled allele definition files
license: custom (free for academic; for-profit use requires a separate license)

provenance.maintainer: David Gfeller lab, University of Lausanne, Switzerland

relevance.why: Strong class II motif modeling and multi-species data; a useful benchmark and motif source for presentation/design.

agent_access: Code + bundled data downloadable from GitHub releases (no auth); bulk-fetchable.
caveats: RED FLAG: license explicitly states for-profit use of the tool OR "any data provided with the script" requires a SEPARATE license from the authors. A commercial entity should not use the bundled data in production without that license. The curated ligand training set proper is not clearly offered as a standalone download.

name: NetMHCIIpan-4.0 training set — MHC-II binding affinity + eluted ligand (incl. mouse H-2)
description: The combined quantitative binding-affinity (BA) and mass-spec eluted-ligand (EL) training corpus for NetMHCIIpan-4.0: >500,000 measurements covering human HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP AND mouse H-2 (I-A/I-E) class-II molecules. Distributed as a single tar archive with 5-fold cross-validation partitions (train/test BA and EL files) and an MHC pseudo-sequence file. Companion to the NetMHCpan-4.1 release.
scale: >500,000 BA+EL measurements; HLA-DR/DQ/DP + mouse H-2 class II

provenance.maintainer: Reynisson, Alvarez, Nielsen et al. (DTU Health Tech)

relevance.why: The largest public quantitative + EL class-II training set and one of the few that includes MOUSE H-2 class II — directly fills the preclinical CD4/MHC-II gap for presentation prediction and cross-species transfer.

agent_access: Download the tar archive over HTTPS from the DTU supplementary page (cat/untar). No auth. Distinct archive from the already-catalogued NetMHCpan-4.1 class-I training set.
caveats: No explicit license on the DTU page (academic/non-profit free; commercial needs a license). BA values are log-transformed; file layout documentation is inconsistent across DTU pages — inspect the extracted folder before parsing.

name: NetMHCpan / NetMHCIIpan (DTU) + training data
description: The most widely used pan-allele MHC-I (NetMHCpan) and MHC-II (NetMHCIIpan) binding/eluted-ligand predictors from DTU. Critically, DTU publishes the partitioned training datasets (binding affinity + eluted ligand, with CV folds), which are a reusable curated corpus in their own right.
scale: Training sets: millions of peptide-allele BA+EL measurements, cross-validation partitioned

relevance.why: The de-facto benchmark predictors and, more usefully, their curated BA+EL training partitions are a high-quality labeled corpus for our own presentation models and for apples-to-apples benchmarking.

agent_access: Training-data tar.gz archives are directly downloadable from the suppl/ URL (no login). The SOFTWARE itself requires an academic download form; non-academic users must email health-software@dtu.dk. Data archive: bulk-fetchable; software: gated.
caveats: Software license is non-commercial/academic - RED FLAG for a for-profit: running the DTU binaries commercially requires a separate license (contact DTU). The training DATA tables are downloadable but their re-use/redistribution terms are not clearly licensed - treat cautiously and attribute. NetMHCIIpan training archive on the suppl page is labeled v4.0.

name: NetMHCpan-4.1 / NetMHCIIpan-4.0 training sets (DTU)
description: The partitioned (cross-validation-ready) training corpora released with the DTU predictors: combined binding-affinity (BA) and eluted-ligand (EL) measurements for MHC-I and MHC-II, aggregated from the public domain + IEDB. A ready-made labeled benchmark substrate.
scale: MHC-I: 13,245,212 data points / 250 molecules; MHC-II: 4,086,230 / 116 molecules (BA+EL)

provenance.maintainer: DTU Health Tech (Nielsen lab); supplementary data site

relevance.why: Pre-partitioned BA+EL labels (incl. MHC pseudo-sequences) are the standard benchmark split; reusing their folds gives directly comparable model numbers.

agent_access: Direct download of NetMHCpan_train.tar.gz and NetMHCIIpan_train.tar.gz (no auth, old unix 'compress' format - decompress with `cat x | uncompress | tar xvf -`). Evaluation sets (CD8_benchmark, per-allele MS ligand files) also hosted. The SOFTWARE is separately gated (academic form; commercial needs DTU license).
caveats: The training-data tables carry no explicit license on the suppl page - marked unknown; attribute and confirm reuse terms. Includes some non-human alleles (e.g. BoLA integrated in 4.1). Dedup vs IEDB/SysteMHC needed (overlapping sources).

name: NetMHCstabpan peptide-MHC-I complex stability dataset (Rasmussen/Harndahl 2016)
description: Quantitative peptide-MHC class I complex STABILITY measurements (half-life of the pMHC complex, a correlate of immunogenicity distinct from affinity), generated by the Buus lab and used to train NetMHCstabpan. >25,000 stability data points across 75 HLA molecules; the publication-level file is released as HLA/peptide/Thalf tuples, with the stand-alone training archive (data.tar.gz) and a counts table.
scale: >25,000 stability measurements; 75 HLA-I molecules (publication reports up to ~136k stability+affinity points)

provenance.maintainer: Rasmussen, Fenoy, Harndahl, Nielsen, Buus (DTU Health Tech / U. Copenhagen)

relevance.why: Stability (off-rate) is a stronger correlate of CTL immunogenicity than affinity; this is the primary public quantitative stability set for training/validating stability predictors and immunogenicity filters.

agent_access: Direct HTTPS download of Stability.txt (HLA/peptide/Thalf) and data.tar.gz from DTU; counts.xls describes the training table. No auth; small files.
caveats: No explicit license on the DTU page; DTU tools are free for academic/non-profit use, commercial use needs a license — treat the data as academic-use, cite Rasmussen 2016. Quantitative binding inputs were drawn from IEDB (overlap with IEDB sets below).

name: SYFPEITHI
description: One of the oldest curated databases of MHC class I and II ligands and peptide motifs, drawn exclusively from published reports, with anchor positions, MHC restriction, source protein, and a classic motif-matrix prediction method.
scale: >7,000 peptide entries; many class I and II alleles

provenance.maintainer: Rammensee group, University of Tübingen, Germany

relevance.why: A clean, literature-curated motif/ligand reference useful for cross-checking motifs and historical epitope recall; small but high-confidence.

agent_access: Query-driven HTML interface only; no bulk download or API - scrape-only and low-throughput. Largely superseded by IEDB for bulk needs.
caveats: No explicit license surfaced - marked unknown; confirm before any redistribution. Not designed for bulk programmatic access. Dated but still cited.

name: Tadros/Racle/Gfeller 2025 MixMHCpred 3.0 multi-species MHC-I corpus
description: The aggregated MHC-I ligand corpus behind MixMHCpred 3.0, spanning >250 samples across human, mouse, cattle, CANID (dog), and non-human primate - the key benchmark assessing how far cross-species MHC-I prediction can go, explicitly including canine.
scale: >250 immunopeptidomics samples across human, mouse, cattle, canid, non-human primate
license: custom (free academic; for-profit use of tool or bundled data needs separate license)

provenance.maintainer: Gfeller lab, UNIL Lausanne; GitHub + Genome Medicine supplement

relevance.why: Directly answers Veritope's core question (cross-species, incl. canine, MHC-I prediction) and aggregates the multi-species training data, including canid, in one place - a shortcut to the canine-relevant literature and data.

agent_access: Tool + bundled data on GitHub (GfellerLab/MixMHCpred); per-source accessions in the paper supplement (aggregates public PXD/MSV datasets). Bulk via git clone / releases.
caveats: RED FLAG: Gfeller for-profit-license clause covers the tool AND "any data provided with the script" - a commercial entity must license before using bundled data in production. Canid coverage present but modest. Re-fetch per-source accessions from the Genome Medicine supplementary (the preprint PDF, 10.1101/2024.05.08.593183, was rate-limited/erroring at catalog time - verify the full source table there).

name: TransPHLA-AOMP peptide-HLA binding dataset
description: Training, independent, and external test sets for TransPHLA (transformer pHLA-I binding predictor) plus 112 common HLA sequences; released via GitHub and a Zenodo archive.
scale: ~ training + independent + external + neoantigen pHLA-I test sets (~1.1 GB archive)

provenance.maintainer: Chu et al.; GitHub a96123155/TransPHLA-AOMP + Zenodo

relevance.why: A modern transformer baseline with a packaged pHLA-I dataset for benchmarking; includes a neoantigen test set.

agent_access: GitHub Dataset folder + Zenodo archive (record 5715479) + a lab download page. Bulk-downloadable, no auth.
caveats: License not explicit on the archive - mark unknown; confirm before reuse. Source DOI to verify. Dataset largely re-derived from IEDB/public EL (dedup needed). Do not confuse with TransHLA (different, later model). Human only.

name: Experimental HLA-B*2705 peptide-binding affinity dataset (Walshe 2014)
description: A focused "data paper" releasing experimentally measured binding affinities for 223 peptides to HLA-B*2705, determined with an in-house FACS-based MHC stabilization assay — a clean, fully experimental single-allele quantitative binding set published with the data as the primary object (Dataset Papers in Science).
scale: 223 peptides, single allele HLA-B*2705; experimental affinities

provenance.maintainer: Walshe et al.; Dataset Papers in Science (Hindawi, open access)

relevance.why: Small but fully experimental, well-documented single-allele affinity set useful as an independent held-out test for HLA-B27 binding predictors (B27 is clinically important and often under-represented in training data).

agent_access: Open-access article + supplementary data table via the Wiley/Hindawi page; CC BY 3.0.
caveats: Small scale and single allele; stabilization-assay affinities are not directly IC50 and should be normalized before merging with competitive-binding sets.

name: Wang 2008 quantitative MHC class II peptide-binding affinity dataset (IEDB)
description: Curated quantitative MHC class II peptide-binding affinity dataset assembled by Wang et al. for a systematic MHC-II prediction benchmark, released via the IEDB datasets page. Includes the peptide-affinity table, a non-redundant PDB core-peptide/allele reference, and an LCMV T-cell activation table.
scale: quantitative IC50 affinities across human HLA class II + mouse H-2; thousands of peptides

relevance.why: A clean legacy quantitative MHC-II affinity benchmark (human + mouse H-2) still used to compare class-II predictors; complements the much larger NetMHCIIpan-4.0 corpus.

agent_access: Direct HTTPS download of the zip/txt from IEDB; no auth; small files.
caveats: No explicit license on the IEDB page. Older curation; expect overlap with BD2013 and NetMHCIIpan sets — dedup on peptide/allele/measurement.

name: MHC-II neoantigens in mouse T3 sarcoma (Alspach 2019)
description: Characterization of the MHC class II-restricted neoantigen landscape of the T3 MCA sarcoma, defining mITGB1 (N710Y Itgb1) as a major I-A(b)-restricted CD4 neoantigen and showing MHC-II neoantigens are required for optimal checkpoint-blockade response. Processed mutation/neoepitope data and immunogenicity readouts are in the paper's extended-data and supplementary tables.
scale: T3 sarcoma; defined MHC-II (mITGB1) and MHC-I neoantigens; CD4/CD8 reactivity data

relevance.why: One of the few well-defined mouse MHC-II (CD4) tumour neoantigen datasets; essential for CD4 neoantigen prediction and for modelling the CD4/CD8 interplay underlying vaccine and checkpoint responses, where class-II data are scarce.

agent_access: Extended-data / supplementary tables from the Nature article page (no auth for SI).
caveats: No deposited raw-sequence accession confirmed; processed data only in SI under Springer Nature terms (no explicit open license). Confirm any GEO ID in the paper.

name: Bassani-Sternberg 2016 native melanoma immunopeptidome + neoepitopes
description: HLA-I immunopeptidomes directly from native human melanoma tissue, including mutation-derived (neoepitope) ligands validated as T-cell targets - a benchmark for tissue-level and neoantigen presentation.
scale: ~95,500 patient-presented peptides across ~25 melanoma patients; 11 mutated ligands (4 immunogenic)

relevance.why: Native-tissue (not cell-line) presentation plus validated neoepitopes - directly relevant to real tumor target discovery and presentation-model realism.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD004894 via API/FTP; bulk-downloadable, no auth.
caveats: Tumor tissue immunopeptidomes are noisier/lower-yield than cell lines. Neoepitope calling needs matched patient genomics. Human only.

name: CAD v1.0 (Cancer Antigens Database)
description: Cancer antigen database platform aimed at supporting cancer-antigen algorithm development and information exploration — aggregates cancer antigen/peptide information for benchmarking and tool development. Listed as a supplementary/aggregator resource; validation status mixed (curated + predicted).
scale: unknown

relevance.why: Potential aggregator for algorithm-development benchmarking; low priority until site/URL and counts are confirmed. Catalogued for completeness.

agent_access: UNVERIFIED: landing URL not resolved at catalog time — needs a site check before any automated access.
caveats: LOW CONFIDENCE ENTRY: discovered via search only; landing URL, counts, DOI and license all unverified (marked unknown). Confirm the resource resolves and is distinct from TumorAgDB/Neodb before ingesting — do not rely on it until verified.

name: CAPED — Cancer Antigenic Peptide Database (T cell-defined tumor antigens)
description: The de Vigneron/Van den Eynde (Ludwig Institute, UCLouvain) database of human antigenic peptides recognized by T cells that meet strict tumor/tissue-specificity criteria — the long-standing "T cell-defined human tumor antigens" resource (formerly at cancerimmunity.org/peptide). Entries are experimentally VALIDATED T-cell epitopes with HLA restriction, antigen/gene, and references. High-purity, low-volume gold-standard set.
scale: ~403 tumor antigenic peptides (2013 update baseline); CAPED web version adds curation

provenance.maintainer: de Duve Institute / Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, UCLouvain (van der Bruggen, Vigneron, Van den Eynde)

relevance.why: Gold-standard, strictly-curated set of genuinely T-cell-defined human tumor antigens — high-precision positive controls for recognition/immunogenicity work and vaccine/TCR design validation.

agent_access: AT RISK for automation: caped.icp.ucl.ac.be returned connection failure (000) via curl and 403 via WebFetch — the site is up for browsers but blocks automated/headless requests. No API. Expect to need a real browser session; bulk download not confirmed.
caveats: Bot-blocked (403/000 to automated clients) — resolves for humans, not scrapers; flag for manual export. Old location cancerimmunity.org/peptide also 403s. No data license stated — license: unknown. Small (~hundreds) but very high quality; attribution expected.

name: CEDAR (Cancer Epitope Database and Analysis Resource)
description: Cancer-focused sibling of the IEDB, built and curated by the IEDB/LJI team. Comprehensive manual curation of experimentally characterized cancer epitopes from the literature — T-cell assays, B-cell assays, MHC ligand-elution/binding, and a dedicated neoantigen-assay class. Includes germline/tumor-associated antigens and neoantigens, with receptor (TCR/BCR) data. Same query/analysis tooling as IEDB.
scale: ~445,931 epitopes, ~1.5M assays, ~60,104 receptors, 26 cancer types, ~6,203 publications (2026 paper); ~45,132 neoantigen assays. Launch (2022): ~224,355 epitopes / ~317k assays
license: CC BY 4.0 (per IEDB/CEDAR data policy; confirm on export page)

provenance.maintainer: La Jolla Institute for Immunology (IEDB team; NIH/NIAID-funded)

relevance.why: Highest-quality, continuously curated cancer-epitope source with explicit neoantigen assays and receptor data, shared infrastructure/API with IEDB. A backbone reference for both presentation and recognition programs.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200), bulk export page, and the shared IEDB query REST API (query-api.iedb.org) with rate limits. No auth for public data. Best automated-access profile of any resource in this domain.
caveats: Data license not separately stated on-page distinct from IEDB's CC BY 4.0 policy — treat as CC BY (attribution) but confirm on the export page before redistribution. Cancer-restricted subset of the broader IEDB universe; dedup against IEDB tumor subset needed if both are ingested.

name: dbPepNeo2.0 (incl. dbPepNeo v1)
description: Manually curated human tumor neoantigen peptide database. v2.0 adds mass-spectrometry immunopeptidome evidence and neoantigen-reactive TCRβ sequences. Entries are stratified by confidence: high-confidence (HC) validated neoantigens vs low-confidence (LC) MS-derived HLA immunopeptidomes. Fields include mutant/wild-type peptide, length, mutation position, HLA allele, gene, cancer type, verification method, PubMed ID.
scale: v2.0: ~801 class-I HC neoantigens + ~842,289 LC HLA immunopeptidomes + ~55 class-II HC + ~630 neoantigen-reactive TCRβ. v1 (2020): 295 HC / 247 MC / ~407,794 LC

provenance.maintainer: Guangzhou Medical University / collaborators (Lu et al.)

relevance.why: Couples MS-validated HLA immunopeptidomes (LC) with HC validated neoantigens and reactive TCRs — spans presentation evidence and recognition in one curated resource with explicit confidence tiers.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200). v1 offered CSV/Excel/PDF export via a Download button; v2.0 download options not individually verified but portal is live. Expect per-table export rather than one API. No login.
caveats: No explicit data license found — license: unknown. Hosted on biostatistics.online (small academic host) — at-risk for longevity. HC/LC confidence tiers must not be conflated: LC = MS immunopeptidome, not validated neoantigens.

name: GNIFdb (glioma neoantigen intrinsic feature database)
description: Glioma-focused database of computationally PREDICTED HLA class-I neoantigens with intrinsic features (associated mutations, gene expression, HLA binding affinity) plus tooling for feature calculation and survival prediction. Also covers four other cancer types (lung, melanoma, bladder, HNSCC). Predicted, not T-cell-validated.
scale: unknown

provenance.maintainer: Beihang University / collaborators (Li, Sun et al.)

relevance.why: Disease-specific (glioma) predicted-neoantigen set with intrinsic-feature annotation — narrow but useful for a glioma-focused presentation/target program; otherwise predicted-only supplementary data.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200 at oncoimmunobank.cn/index.php; apex https:// fails, use the index.php URL). Search/browse with stated download capability; no API. Expect table export/scrape.
caveats: No data license found — license: unknown. Entirely predicted neoantigens (no T-cell validation). Single-host (.cn) site on only the index.php path — fragile. Glioma-centric; limited breadth.

name: Checkpoint-blockade mouse sarcoma mutant-antigen landscape (Gubin 2014; GSE62771 / phs001005)
description: Whole-exome + transcriptome characterization of MCA-induced mouse sarcomas (e.g. d42m1-T3) defining tumour-specific mutant antigens (incl. the mLAMA4 and mALG8 neoepitopes) that are the targets of CD8 T-cell responses driving regression after anti-PD-1 / anti-CTLA-4. RNA-seq in GEO; raw exome/transcriptome reads in SRA/dbGaP.
scale: MCA sarcoma lines; exome + RNA-seq; defined H2-Kb/Db mutant neoepitopes

relevance.why: Foundational syngeneic neoantigen dataset linking mutation discovery to checkpoint response; mLAMA4/mALG8 are reference immunogenic mouse neoepitopes for benchmarking neoantigen ranking and TCR-recognition models.

agent_access: GSE62771 processed RNA-seq is open on GEO (anonymous HTTP). Raw reads under dbGaP phs001005 need an approved Data Use Certification (controlled access).
caveats: Raw sequence is controlled-access (dbGaP DUA) — catalog but note the gate. GEO processed matrices are open but carry no explicit redistribution license.

name: IEDB — tumor/cancer subset
description: The Immune Epitope Database filtered to cancer/tumor disease context. Experimentally measured epitopes: T-cell assays, B-cell assays, and MHC ligand-elution/binding. Overlaps heavily with CEDAR (same team) but IEDB is the broader superset; the cancer slice is reachable via disease filters and bulk export.
scale: IEDB overall ~1.6M+ epitopes / ~1M+ assays; tumor subset is a filtered fraction (see CEDAR for the curated cancer counts)

relevance.why: Canonical, well-licensed epitope reference; the tumor slice anchors validated cancer epitopes and feeds dedup/cross-referencing for every other neoantigen DB here.

agent_access: Bulk CSV/JSON export + REST query API (rate-limited), no auth. Fully automatable. Filter on disease = cancer/neoplasm to isolate the tumor subset.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 — redistribution OK with attribution (good). Heavy overlap with CEDAR; ingest one as canonical and treat the other as supplement to avoid double-counting. Tumor subset requires disease-field filtering, not a prebuilt file.

name: TCGA pan-cancer alternative-splicing neoepitopes (Kahles et al. 2018, PCAWG/SplAdder)
description: Comprehensive alternative-splicing analysis across 8,705 TCGA patients (32 cancer types) with SplAdder, cataloguing tumor-specific splicing events and deriving predicted splicing-derived MHC neoepitopes. The deposited-data table releases the predicted neoepitope set and the tumor variant set via Synapse, with the splicing event catalogue mirrored at the NCI GDC (PanCanAtlas-Splicing-2018).
scale: 8,705 patients, 32 cancer types; genome-wide splicing event + neoepitope catalogues

provenance.maintainer: TCGA PanCanAtlas splicing working group (Ratsch/Robinson labs; MSKCC/ETH Zurich)

relevance.why: Largest pan-cancer map of splicing-derived antigen candidates; the released neoepitope table is a direct prioritisation input for alternative-splicing antigen programs.

agent_access: Synapse requires a (free) registered account + accepting governance terms for download; programmatic access via synapseclient. GDC splicing catalogue is openly downloadable.
caveats: Synapse data governance: registration + terms acceptance required (not fully "open"); some upstream TCGA variant/HLA inputs are controlled-access. Neoepitopes are predicted, not MS-validated. Human only.

name: Tumour-wide splicing-derived public neoantigens (Kwok et al. 2025, SSNIP)
description: Spatially-mapped tumor RNA-seq (gliomas and other tumor types) used to identify recurrent, tumour-wide RNA-splicing aberrations that generate shared ("public") neoantigens, with the SSNIP pipeline and HLA-presentation validation. The study's own spatially-mapped glioma biopsy RNA-seq is deposited in EGA (controlled) plus a NODE mirror for other RNA-seq.
scale: Spatially-mapped multi-region biopsies; recurrent public splicing neoantigens

provenance.maintainer: University of California San Francisco (Okada lab; Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy)

relevance.why: "Public" splicing neoantigens shared across patients and across tumor regions are prime shared-target candidates; SSNIP (github.com/dakwok/SSNIP) is reusable for discovery.

agent_access: Own glioma biopsy RNA-seq is EGA controlled-access (DAC approval + DUA). NODE OEP002956 is openly downloadable. Code on GitHub.
caveats: Core patient RNA-seq is controlled-access (EGA). Immunopeptidome relied on reused CPTAC/PIDB data (no new MS accession). Human only.

name: Aberrantly-expressed TSA immunopeptidome (Laumont et al. 2018, Perreault/Thibault)
description: Proteogenomic datasets underpinning the finding that non-coding/aberrantly-expressed genomic regions (endogenous retroelements, non-coding RNAs, intergenic/UTR regions) are the main source of targetable tumor-specific antigens (aeTSAs). The study built tumor-specific protein databases by subtracting the mature medullary thymic epithelial cell (mTEC) transcriptome, then validated MHC-I-eluted peptides by MS across murine lines (CT26, EL4) and human B-ALL and lung tumor samples. Multiple PRIDE/ProteomeXchange immunopeptidome deposits.
scale: Multiple MHC-I elution datasets across mouse lines + human tumors

provenance.maintainer: Institute for Research in Immunology and Cancer (IRIC), Universite de Montreal (Perreault & Thibault labs)

relevance.why: Primary evidence and data for the "dark matter" / non-coding source of shared tumor antigens. Mouse + human elution data are reusable for training/benchmarking non-canonical ligand detection and for the know/believe/prove separation on aeTSAs.

agent_access: PRIDE bulk FTP/Aspera download, no auth; related accessions cross-linked within each project.
caveats: No explicit dataset reuse license beyond PRIDE/EBI terms — confirm before redistribution. Species metadata on individual PRIDE records can mislabel mixed mouse/human submissions.

name: Noncoding-derived tumour-specific antigens in mouse models (Laumont 2018; GSE111092 / PXD009064)
description: Proteogenomic discovery of tumour-specific antigens (TSAs) in two murine lines (CT26 BALB/c colon carcinoma; EL4 C57BL/6 lymphoma) plus 7 human primary tumours, showing ~90% of TSAs arise from allegedly noncoding regions. Pairs RNA-seq / exome (GEO GSE111092, mouse + human sub-series) with MHC-I immunopeptidomics MS (PRIDE, EL4/CT26 ligandomes).
scale: 21 mouse + 30 human TSAs; CT26 & EL4 lines; RNA-seq + immunopeptidome MS

provenance.maintainer: Laumont/Perreault lab (IRIC, U. Montréal); GEO + PRIDE

relevance.why: Key evidence that noncoding/aberrant translation drives the mouse (and human) TSA repertoire; immunopeptidome + RNA pairing is a direct proteogenomics training set for non-canonical antigen discovery, with matched syngeneic models (CT26/EL4).

agent_access: GSE111092 open on GEO (anonymous HTTP); PXD009064 raw MS via anonymous PRIDE FTP.
caveats: No explicit SPDX license on either GEO or PRIDE. PXD009750 linkage to this study is inferred from co-deposition dates — verify in the paper's data-availability text.

name: Exon-TE splice-junction neoantigens in lung cancer (Merlotti/Burbage 2023, Institut Curie)
