description: HLA-I immunopeptidomics and matched transcriptomics identifying immunogenic, patient-shared neoantigens encoded by non-canonical splice junctions between coding exons and transposable elements in non-small-cell lung cancer and lung tumor lines. Companion study (Burbage et al.) shows these junction antigens are epigenetically (DNA-methylation) controlled. The PRIDE deposit is released under CC0.
scale: NSCLC primary samples + lung tumor cell lines; recurrent junction-derived peptides

provenance.maintainer: Institut Curie, Paris (Amigorena lab; submitter Y. Arribas)

relevance.why: Recurrent exon-TE junction antigens are candidate shared targets; CC0 licensing makes the immunopeptidome fully reusable for training and for proving recurrence across patients.

agent_access: PRIDE bulk download, no auth. CC0 permits unrestricted reuse including ML training.
caveats: Companion Burbage (abm6360) deposit accession not individually verified here — cite the Merlotti PXD034820 for the released immunopeptidome. Human lung cancer only.

name: Neodb (comprehensive neoantigen database & discovery platform)
description: R/Shiny platform combining a curated VALIDATED-neoantigen module, a driver-mutation candidate module (Driver-Neo), prediction tools, and an immunogenicity GNN (Immuno-GNN). Validated set curated from literature with assay types (ELISpot, multimer staining, etc.) and HLA-I/II restriction; Driver-Neo is predicted candidates.
scale: ~1,463 validated neoantigen instances (1,277 HLA-I, 186 HLA-II); Driver-Neo ~20,971 candidate neoantigens

relevance.why: Validated set with assay-type metadata plus a driver-mutation-focused candidate set and an immunogenicity model — good for recognition training and driver-neoantigen target prioritization.

agent_access: AT RISK: web host liuxslab.com/Neodb failed to connect (000) at check time. However code + validated-neoantigen data are on GitHub (XSLiuLab/Neodb) under MIT — the robust automated route is the repo, not the Shiny app. Example inputs (VCF/MAF/PEP) and validated data documented on the About page.
caveats: Live web platform appears down (000) — rely on the GitHub repo instead. MIT applies to the code per bio.tools; confirm whether curated data inherit MIT or carry source-paper terms. Driver-Neo is predicted, not validated.

name: NeoPeptide (immunoinformatic database of T-cell-defined neoantigens)
description: Web database of literature-curated neoantigens with mutation site, subunit sequence and MHC restriction, drawn from published papers and other immunological resources, with links out for further characterization. Focus on T-cell-defined (validated) neoantigens.
scale: unknown

relevance.why: Additional literature-curated T-cell-defined neoantigen set for cross-referencing/dedup against NEPdb, dbPepNeo and CAPED; small supplementary source.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200). Browse/search UI; code mirror on GitHub (lyotvincent/NeoPeptide) which may contain the underlying data for bulk access. No documented API.
caveats: No explicit data license — license: unknown. Last updated 2019 (stale). Heavily overlaps other curated sets; low incremental volume. Check the GitHub repo for a bulk data copy before scraping the site.

name: NeoTCR — neoantigen-specific functional TCR database
description: Curated database of experimentally-supported, functional neoantigen-specific TCR sequences, each linked to its neoantigen/neoepitope, HLA restriction, tissue of origin and source publication. Focused specifically on tumor neoantigen reactivity.
scale: ~988 entries from 52 publications, 17-18 cancer types

relevance.why: The most directly on-target TCR label set for tumor neoantigen recognition — high-value despite small size for neoantigen-focused design/recognition.

agent_access: Web interface with downloadable curated table. No documented REST API; scripted table fetch. Small dataset, easily ingested.
caveats: Data license not located — treat as unknown, confirm before reuse. Small (hundreds of entries) but functionally validated. Verify landing URL resolves (newer .cn host).

name: NEPdb (NEoPeptide database)
description: Manually curated database of T-cell-experimentally-validated neoantigens plus pan-cancer predicted neoepitopes. Both IMMUNOGENIC ('P') and non-immunogenic/ineffective ('N') human neopeptides are recorded with HLA class I/II alleles, T-cell activation data, TCR sequences and clinical outcome where available — the negative set is a notable feature for training. A separate module provides predicted HLA-I neoepitopes from shared somatic mutations.
scale: ~17,549 validated entries (site reports ~173 immunogenic + ~17,376 non-immunogenic from 41 papers); predicted set from ~16,745 shared somatic mutations

relevance.why: One of few sources with explicit negative (non-immunogenic) neoantigen data alongside positives plus TCRs — directly useful for immunogenicity/recognition classifier training and benchmarking.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200). Browse/search UI; no documented REST API or clearly-labeled bulk file found — expect scraping of result tables. No login.
caveats: No explicit data license found — license: unknown. Headline count (~17.5k) is dominated by negatives; true immunogenic count is small (~173). Last updated 2021 — stale. Single-institution host; monitor for drift.

name: nuORFdb v1.0 + Ribo-seq/MHC-I immunopeptidome (Ouspenskaia et al. 2022)
description: Ribosome-profiling-derived database of ~230k+ translated non-canonical/unannotated ORFs (nuORFs: uORFs, out-of-frame, lncRNA, 5'UTR, 3'UTR, pseudogene ORFs) built across human cell lines and tissues, plus the matched MHC-I immunopeptidomics used to show ~3,555 nuORF-derived peptides are presented on HLA class I in cancer. The deposited bundle includes the Ribo-seq raw data, transcript quantifications, and the nuORFdb_v1.0.bed database itself (via GEO), with the mass-spectrometry raw files on MassIVE. This is a foundational resource for cryptic/ non-canonical tumor antigen discovery.
scale: ~237k nuORFs in nuORFdb v1.0; 3,555 translated nuORFs detected in MHC-I MS

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Dana-Farber (Clauser/Carr/Regev labs)

relevance.why: The canonical reference for expanding the presentable antigen space beyond annotated coding genes. nuORFdb is directly usable as a search space for immunopeptidome re-analysis and for training presentation models on non-canonical ligands.

agent_access: GEO (nuORFdb_v1.0.bed + Ribo-seq) and MassIVE (MS) are bulk-downloadable without auth; code at github.com/klarman-cell-observatory/Riboseq-nuORFs. Patient-derived raw data are under dbGaP controlled access (DUA + eRA/approval required).
caveats: Patient-sample raw sequencing is dbGaP controlled-access, not open. No explicit reuse license is attached to the GEO/MassIVE deposits (repository terms only) — flag before redistribution. nuORFdb is human-only.

name: RNA-source (editing/variant) tumor-agnostic neoantigen immunopeptidome (2023)
description: Proteogenomic study showing RNA-level variants — notably A-to-I RNA-editing events (detected as A>G) — are a major, tumor-agnostic source of HLA-presented neoantigens, with many neoantigens derived only from RNA (not DNA) variants. Mass spectrometry immunopeptidome data deposited at PRIDE.
scale: Patient cohort; high fraction of RNA-only / RNA-editing-derived neoantigens

relevance.why: Directly demonstrates RNA-editing neoantigens on HLA — a non-mutational, potentially shared antigen class; the MS data support proving editing-derived targets.

agent_access: PRIDE bulk download, no auth. Article CC BY 4.0.
caveats: Immunopeptidome MS deposited; upstream patient sequencing access varies. A>G calls require careful SNP/editing discrimination. Human only.

name: Non-canonical proteome & immunopeptidome of DLBCL (Ruiz Cuevas et al. 2021)
description: Integrated Ribo-seq (translation initiation + elongation), RNA-seq and MHC-I immunopeptidome MS for three human diffuse large B-cell lymphoma lines (HBL-1, DoHH2, SU-DHL-4), used to catalogue 2,503 new non-canonical proteins (1,842 cryptic proteins + 661 novel isoforms) and assess how few reach the immunopeptidome. Primary data + the custom proteogenomic databases are deposited (PRIDE + SRA).
scale: 3 DLBCL lines; 2,503 non-canonical proteins catalogued

provenance.maintainer: IRIC, Universite de Montreal (Perreault lab) with Yewdell (NIAID)

relevance.why: Quantifies the gap between non-canonical translation and actual HLA presentation — directly relevant to prioritising which cryptic ORFs are worth proving as antigens. Code: lemieux-lab/Ribo-db.

agent_access: PRIDE + SRA bulk download, no auth; analysis code on GitHub (lemieux-lab/Ribo-db).
caveats: Article is CC BY-NC-ND (no derivatives / non-commercial) — note for any derived redistribution. Human lymphoma cell lines only.

name: Pan-cancer transposable-element-derived tumor antigens (Shah et al. 2023, TEProf2)
description: Pan-cancer (33 TCGA tumor types) identification of 1,068 transposable-element-chimeric transcripts (exon-TE splice products) predicted to yield shared tumor-specific TE antigens (TS-TEAs), with HLA-pulldown and whole-lysate mass spectrometry confirming TE-derived peptides (e.g. four L1PA2-derived ligands in DMS53). New sequencing and MS data were deposited; the TEProf2 pipeline is released.
scale: 1,068 TE-chimeric candidate transcripts across 33 tumor types

provenance.maintainer: Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis (Ting Wang lab)

relevance.why: Shared, tumor-specific TE antigens are attractive off-the-shelf targets; the new GEO/PRIDE deposits plus TEProf2 (github.com/twlab/TEProf2Paper) let us re-derive and prove candidates.

agent_access: GEO + PRIDE bulk download, no auth. Note some upstream inputs (EGAD00001000725 cell lines) are EGA controlled-access; TCGA/GTEx/CPTAC used as references.
caveats: No explicit reuse license on GEO/PRIDE deposits (repository terms). Antigen calls are prediction-heavy; only a handful MS-validated. Human only.

name: Intron-retention neoepitopes in cancer (Smart et al. 2018)
description: In-silico framework (plus MS evidence on MHC-I in cancer cell lines) establishing intron retention as a source of tumor neoepitopes, applied to melanoma immunotherapy cohorts. No new primary sequencing was deposited; the work re-analysed public cohorts (Snyder 2014; Hugo 2016) whose raw data are at dbGaP/SRA, and released its pipeline and predictions.
scale: Melanoma ICB cohorts re-analysed; intron-retention neoepitope predictions

relevance.why: Establishes intron retention as an antigen class to test; useful as a method reference and for benchmarking splicing-antigen pipelines against ICB outcomes.

agent_access: SRP070710 openly downloadable from SRA; Snyder cohort (phs001038) is dbGaP controlled-access. No new deposit — a reanalysis/method paper.
caveats: Reuses external cohorts rather than depositing new primary data; one cohort is controlled. Neoepitopes are predicted with limited MS validation. Human only.

name: TANTIGEN 2.0
description: A curated knowledge base of tumor T-cell antigens, including HLA ligands, T-cell epitopes, neoantigens, naturally processed (MS-eluted) peptides, cognate TCR sequences, and expression data. Bridges presentation and tumor-antigen target lists.
scale: ~4,296 antigen variants from 403 tumor antigens; >1,500 epitopes/HLA ligands

relevance.why: A ready list of known tumor antigens/epitopes with presentation and TCR annotations - useful for target triage and positive-control construction.

agent_access: Web interface with downloadable tables; small enough to fetch fully. No formal API.
caveats: No explicit data license found - unknown; confirm before reuse. Smaller, curated (not comprehensive). Human only.

name: TANTIGEN 2.0 (Tumor T-cell Antigen database)
description: Knowledge base of tumor T-cell antigens and epitopes: tumor antigen proteins and their sequence variants, experimentally validated T-cell epitopes and HLA ligands, and validated TCR sequences for cognate epitopes. Mix of validated epitopes/ligands and antigen-variant annotation. Update of the original Dana-Farber TANTIGEN.
scale: ~4,296 antigen variants from 403 unique tumor antigens; >1,500 T-cell epitopes and HLA ligands; plus validated TCRs
license: open-access (stated 'interactive open-access database'; no SPDX license found)

provenance.maintainer: Met-hilab (Olsen/Brusic; Keskin, Dana-Farber co-author). Legacy host: cvc.dfci.harvard.edu/tadb

relevance.why: Antigen-variant-centric view (403 tumor antigens, thousands of variants) plus validated epitopes/TCRs — useful for antigen-level target mapping and recognition datasets.

agent_access: AT RISK: projects.met-hilab.org/tadb returns HTTP 503 (service unavailable) at check time — may be transient or decommissioned. Legacy Dana-Farber host (cvc.dfci.harvard.edu/tadb) also unreliable. No API. Monitor/retry.
caveats: Host down (503) at catalog time — verify before relying on it; single-lab hosting is fragile. License called "open-access" in the paper but no formal SPDX terms found. Dana-Farber is a co-author affiliation, not the current host.

name: The Cancer Immunome Atlas (TCIA) / Immunophenoscore
description: Pan-cancer immunogenomic portal (Charoentong et al. 2017) providing, per TCGA tumor, predicted neoantigens, cancer-germline antigens, HLA types, immune-cell deconvolution and the Immunophenoscore (IPS) as a predictor of checkpoint-blockade response.
scale: ~20 TCGA solid-tumor types (pan-cancer, ~8,000+ samples)
license: unknown (portal terms not stated; data derived from TCGA)

provenance.maintainer: Institute of Bioinformatics, Medical University of Innsbruck

relevance.why: Pre-computed neoantigen and cancer-germline-antigen predictions plus HLA calls across TCGA — a direct shortcut to candidate shared/private antigen lists and an IPS response prior.

agent_access: Normally a web portal with downloadable per-tumor tables (no auth). As of 2026 the portal is paused for redesign; urgent dataset/validation-file requests go to icbi@i-med.ac.at. Supplementary data also distributed with the Cell Reports paper.
caveats: Portal currently offline — availability intermittent; cannot be relied on for an automated pipeline until restored. License/terms not explicitly stated (mark unknown). Predictions are tool-dependent; re-derive with current callers for production use.

name: TESLA — Tumor nEoantigen SeLection Alliance benchmark
description: Consortium benchmark (Wells et al. 2020) in which many teams predicted neoantigens from shared WES+RNA-seq of 6 tumors (3 melanoma, 3 NSCLC); 608 peptides were then experimentally tested for MHC binding and T-cell recognition, yielding validated immunogenicity labels and key parameters of epitope immunogenicity.
scale: 6 tumors; 608 peptides with experimental immunogenicity readouts

provenance.maintainer: Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy / Sage Bionetworks

relevance.why: The gold-standard labeled benchmark for neoantigen prediction — validated positives and negatives for training/evaluating presentation and immunogenicity models end to end.

agent_access: Downloadable from Synapse (syn21048999) via the synapseclient Python/R API with a free account + token — scriptable. Open benchmark intended for reuse.
caveats: Tiny number of tumors (depth, not breadth). Synapse registration + terms acceptance required. Immunogenicity assays have their own sensitivity limits (document assay type).

name: TSNAdb v1.0 (legacy)
description: Original 2018 TSNAdb: predicted tumor-specific neoantigens from TCGA and ICGC SNVs using NetMHCpan v2.8/v4.0 across common HLA alleles. Superseded by v2.0. Catalogued only to note the dead legacy host.
scale: ~3.7M predicted (NetMHCpan 2.8) / ~1.15M (NetMHCpan 4.0) shared-neoantigen predictions (ICGC/TCGA)

relevance.why: Historical reference only; v2.0 supersedes it. Listed so the broken legacy URL is documented, not re-chased.

agent_access: DEAD: biopharm.zju.edu.cn/tsnadb returns HTTP 502. Not fetchable. Use TSNAdb v2.0 instead.
caveats: Legacy host down (502). Entirely predicted data. Redundant with v2 — kept for provenance/dead-link tracking.

name: TSNAdb v2.0 (Tumor-Specific NeoAntigen database)
description: Updated version of TSNAdb from the Zhan Zhou group (Zhejiang University). Predominantly a PREDICTED neoantigen resource derived from TCGA: predictions now cover SNVs, INDELs and gene fusions (v1 was SNV-only). It also curates a smaller set of literature-collected neoantigens graded by evidence tier (tier 1 = validated immunogenic AND presented; tier 2 = immunogenic only; tier 3 = presented only). Predictions use NetMHCpan / MHCflurry-class tools. Browsable by cancer type and HLA.
scale: Predicted: ~372,273 SNV-derived + ~137,130 INDEL-derived + ~11,093 fusion-derived (TCGA). Curated/validated: ~1,557-1,856 neoantigens (source counts vary)

provenance.maintainer: Zhan Zhou group, College of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Zhejiang University

relevance.why: Large pan-cancer predicted-neoantigen set tied to TCGA mutations, plus a tiered validated set, useful as a predicted-vs-validated contrast for presentation modeling and shared-neoantigen target triage.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200). Per-cancer-type and per-HLA tables downloadable from the Download page; no documented API or single bulk dump. Automated retrieval likely needs page/table scraping. No login.
caveats: No explicit data license found on the site — license: unknown; do not assume reuse/ML-training rights. v1.0 host (biopharm.zju.edu.cn/tsnadb) returns 502 and should be treated as dead/superseded — use v2 at pgx.zju.edu.cn. Validated-neoantigen count differs between the preprint and published abstracts (1,557 vs 1,856); verify on-site. Overwhelmingly predicted data — do not read predictions as validated.

name: TumorAgDB (tumor neoantigen database platform, v1/v2)
description: Recent (2025) tumor neoantigen platform aggregating published literature and public resources (NCI database, IEDB, TESLA alliance ~608 sequences) plus simulated/affinity-derived neoantigen data; v2.0 integrates two more years of public data across human and mouse. Includes immunogenicity-prediction tooling. Mixes validated, mouse-model-validated, and simulated/predicted data.
scale: v2.0: ~187,223 total entries across 15 cancer types/cell lines; ~1,106 experimentally validated neoantigens

relevance.why: Newest/largest aggregate with human+mouse coverage and a modest validated core — useful as a recency sweep and for mouse-model cross-species comparison, but heavily predicted/simulated.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200). Browse/search; no documented API or confirmed bulk file — expect scraping. No login.
caveats: No data license found — license: unknown. Large total count (~187k) is mostly predicted/simulated/mouse-model data; validated core is ~1,106 — separate carefully. Chinese single-host site; longevity unproven. Count discrepancies between v1/v2 in sources — verify on-site.

name: MC38 & TRAMP-C1 MS-validated mouse neoantigens (Yadav 2014)
description: Combined whole-exome + transcriptome sequencing and MHC-I immunopeptidomics in two widely used syngeneic lines (MC38 colon carcinoma, TRAMP-C1 prostate) to identify MS-confirmed, MHC-I-presented mutant peptides — including the reference H2-Db neoepitope Adpgk (ASMTNMELM, ~2 nM). Variant peptides, LC-MS identifications, RNA-seq expression, and MHC-I-presented variants are released as Supplementary Tables 1-5.
scale: 2 syngeneic lines; thousands of nonsynonymous variants; handful of MS-confirmed neoepitopes

provenance.maintainer: Yadav, Jhunjhunwala et al. (Genentech); data in journal supplementary tables

relevance.why: Adpgk/Reps1/Dpagt1 (MC38) are among the most-used mouse neoantigen benchmarks for vaccine and TCR work; the paper's MS-validated presented variants are a clean positive set for immunogenicity/presentation modelling in syngeneic systems.

agent_access: Supplementary Excel tables downloadable from the Nature article page (no auth for SI). No raw-read repository accession was deposited.
caveats: Data live only as journal supplementary tables (no GEO/SRA/PRIDE accession); governed by Springer Nature SI terms, not an open license — redistribution not clearly granted.

name: Gene-fusion-derived neoantigens (Yang et al. 2019, MSKCC)
description: Whole-exome and RNA-seq of patient tumors used to detect tumor-specific gene fusions and demonstrate that fusion-junction neoantigens are strongly immunogenic and can drive immunotherapy responses (incl. a complete responder with a fusion neoantigen). Pan-cancer TCGA analysis estimated fusion neoantigens in ~24% of fusion-positive tumors. New sequencing deposited under one BioProject.
scale: TCGA pan-cancer fusion survey (1,404/5,825 fusion+ tumors with predicted neoantigen) + patient cohort

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (Chan & Morris labs); sequencing at New York Genome Center

relevance.why: Fusion-junction neoantigens are a distinct, often clonal antigen class; the deposited WES/ RNA-seq supports fusion-caller benchmarking and antigen recurrence analysis.

agent_access: PRJNA527992 bulk-downloadable from SRA, no auth; some TCGA inputs via cBioPortal/controlled TCGA.
caveats: No explicit reuse license on the SRA deposit (NCBI policy only). Human only.

name: Systematic A-to-I RNA-editing neoantigen catalogue (Zhou et al. 2020, PREP)
description: Systematic in-silico characterization of A-to-I RNA-editing-derived neoantigens across TCGA cancer types, with the PREP pipeline and MS validation of an editing-derived peptide (OSBPL9) in ovarian tumors. The released resource is a set of supplementary neoantigen tables plus the open pipeline; it re-analyses public RNA-editing, RNA-seq and MS data rather than depositing new MS.
scale: Pan-cancer TCGA RNA-editing neoantigen predictions; 1 MS-validated editope

provenance.maintainer: Tongji University / ShanghaiTech / USTC (Qi Liu lab)

relevance.why: Complements the RNA-source immunopeptidome: provides a pan-cancer predicted editope catalogue and an open pipeline (PREP, github.com/bm2-lab/PREP) for editing-antigen discovery.

agent_access: Neoantigen tables are open article supplements; PREP on GitHub. Underlying editing data via Synapse (registration) and some controlled TCGA (phs000178) inputs.
caveats: Predictions (reanalysis), not a new primary deposit; only one editope MS-validated. TCGA HLA/ neoantigen inputs partly controlled. Human only.

name: Abelin 2017 mono-allelic HLA-I immunopeptidome (MassIVE MSV000080527)
description: Earlier mono-allelic HLA class I immunopeptidome (16 datasets) establishing the mono-allelic profiling approach and improving neoepitope prediction. Experimentally measured eluted ligands; a predecessor/companion to the Sarkizova 2020 expansion.
scale: 16 mono-allelic HLA-I datasets

provenance.maintainer: Abelin/Carr et al., Broad Institute; MassIVE/ProteomeXchange

relevance.why: Foundational mono-allelic training data for HLA-I presentation prediction; combine with Sarkizova 2020 for a broader allele panel.

agent_access: MassIVE open download, no auth. Automatable.
caveats: license: unknown (MassIVE open policy). Smaller/older than Sarkizova 2020; dedup allele overlap if merging.

name: Abelin 2017 mono-allelic HLA-I immunopeptidome
description: The foundational mono-allelic HLA class I immunopeptidomics dataset: peptides eluted from single-HLA-allele cell lines, which established mono-allelic profiling as the gold standard for clean per-allele motifs and launched MS-trained predictors.
scale: ~24,000 peptides across 16 HLA class I alleles

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute (Carr/Wu labs); deposited in MassIVE

relevance.why: Clean mono-allelic positives for HLA-I presentation model training/benchmarking; the dataset that showed MS-trained predictors beat affinity-trained ones.

agent_access: MassIVE FTP (MSV000080527) + GEO GSE93315; bulk-downloadable, no auth, CC0. Raw files are large (Q Exactive). Use ppx/pridepy or direct FTP.
caveats: Raw MS requires reprocessing (search engine + FDR) to get peptide lists. Only 16 alleles. Human only.

name: Abelin 2019 mono-allelic HLA-II immunopeptidome
description: Mono-allelic HLA class II immunopeptidomics defining HLA-II ligand processing and binding rules - the class II analogue of the 2017 mono-allelic work, enabling cleaner HLA-II presentation prediction.
scale: >200,000 unique peptides across 41 HLA-II heterodimers

relevance.why: Core mono-allelic HLA-II training/benchmark set; class II is historically data-poor, so this is disproportionately valuable.

agent_access: MassIVE MSV000083991 / ProteomeXchange PXD014293; bulk-downloadable, CC0, no auth.
caveats: Raw MS needs reprocessing. Class II deconvolution is harder (open binding register). Human only.

name: Bassani-Sternberg 2015 HLA-I peptidome (abundance/turnover)
description: Deep multi-allelic HLA class I immunopeptidome across seven cell lines plus primary cells, showing presentation tracks protein abundance and turnover. An early large-scale, widely-reused HLA-I ligand set.
scale: 22,244 unique HLA-I peptides at 1% FDR; 7 cell lines + primary cells

provenance.maintainer: Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry (Mann lab); PRIDE (MSV000079539 mirror)

relevance.why: Classic multi-allelic positive set; the abundance/turnover findings inform processing features used in presentation models.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD000394 (REST API + FTP) and MassIVE mirror MSV000079539; bulk-downloadable.
caveats: Multi-allelic (needs deconvolution to assign alleles). Older acquisition. Human only.

name: Bassani-Sternberg 2016 melanoma neoepitope immunopeptidome (PXD004894)
description: Direct MS identification of HLA-presented peptides (incl. neoepitopes) from native human melanoma tissue — one of the foundational tumor immunopeptidome datasets. Experimentally measured eluted ligands across a melanoma cohort; frequently reused to train/benchmark presentation and neoepitope prediction.
scale: Melanoma-associated immunopeptidome to ~95,500 peptides; tumor tissue from 25 melanoma patients

relevance.why: Gold-standard tumor-tissue ligandome with directly-detected neoepitopes — direct presentation evidence for melanoma neoantigens and a core training/benchmark set.

agent_access: PRIDE bulk download, no auth (~176 GB). Automatable.
caveats: license: unknown (ProteomeXchange open policy). MS presentation evidence; immunogenicity not established here. Large raw volume; most reuse starts from the paper's peptide tables, not raw.

name: caAtlas (immunopeptidome atlas of human cancer)
description: MS-based immunopeptidome atlas (Zhang lab) reprocessing 43 published HLA immunopeptidomic datasets with an open (modification-tolerant) search engine over ~81.6M MS/MS spectra. Records HLA-presented peptides with cancer type, dataset/spectrum IDs, HLA allele, predicted binding affinity and annotated spectra. Presentation evidence (MS-eluted ligands), including some neoantigen/aberrant-peptide annotation — not T-cell-validated.
scale: ~81.6M MS/MS spectra; 311 cancer samples (9 cancer types) + 707 non-cancer samples (43 datasets)

provenance.maintainer: Bing Zhang lab (Baylor College of Medicine)

relevance.why: Large harmonized MS immunopeptidome across cancers — direct experimental presentation evidence (ligandome) for training/benchmarking presentation predictors; complements binding-only predictions.

agent_access: Web portal (HTTP 200) with on-site download. No documented API; expect bulk file(s)/table export. No login.
caveats: No explicit data license found — license: unknown; underlying 43 source datasets each carry their own terms (check PRIDE/MassIVE originals before redistribution/ML use). MS-presentation evidence only — not immunogenicity-validated.

name: DLA-88*50101 Peptide-Binding Motif Dataset
description: Early immunoaffinity MS characterization of the DLA-88*50101 peptide-binding motif (and later DLA-88*508:01 self + canine-distemper-virus peptides), the first experimental canine MHC-I ligand sets published.
scale: ~3,720 DLA-88*50101 peptides (plus DLA-88*508:01 self/viral peptides)

provenance.maintainer: academic (PLOS ONE); structural follow-ups in J Immunol/PMC

relevance.why: Historical anchor points / positive controls for DLA-88 motif modeling; combine with the 2026 atlas for allele coverage.

agent_access: Peptide lists in article supplements (CC BY); downloadable.
caveats: DLA-88*50101 data were generated in transfected human cells (not native dog cells). Few alleles.

name: Monoallelic Canine DLA-88 Immunopeptidome Atlas
description: Monoallelic LC-MS/MS immunopeptidomics atlas across 10 prevalent canine DLA-88 alleles — the first systematic, allele-resolved map of naturally processed canine MHC-I ligands and their binding motifs. Directly addresses the canine presentation data void.
scale: ~32,702 naturally processed peptides (7-15 aa) across 10 DLA-88 alleles
license: preprint content CC BY; PRIDE data CC0/public (verify on PRIDE record)

relevance.why: The single most valuable public resource for canine MHC-I presentation: enough mono-allelic ligands to train/benchmark DLA-88 binding/presentation predictors. This is exactly the data type Veritope needs and that almost nothing else supplies.

agent_access: Peptide tables from supp.; raw MS from PRIDE/ProteomeXchange (FTP, no auth). Confirm association with PXD074485 vs a separate PXD on the PRIDE record.
caveats: PREPRINT, not yet peer-reviewed. Covers only DLA-88 class I (10 alleles) — other class I loci (DLA-12/64/79) and all class II remain uncharacterized. Still tiny vs human MS atlases.

name: Canine PeptideAtlas (build 573, 2024-01; Kusebauch Sci Data 2026)
description: Community canine proteome build in PeptideAtlas: 149,546 peptides across 18 samples (528,272 PSM counts), ~1,009,420 peptide-to-protein locations, 17,795 protein identifications (16,959 map 1:1 to Ensembl 110). A tryptic PROTEOME reference (not an MHC-ligand immunopeptidome), but the backbone for canine proteogenomics and for mapping eluted ligands to proteins.
scale: 149,546 peptides; 18 samples; ~1.01M peptide-protein locations; 17,795 proteins

provenance.maintainer: Institute for Systems Biology (PeptideAtlas; Kusebauch et al.)

relevance.why: Essential protein-level reference to annotate canine eluted peptides and run proteogenomic neoantigen validation; complements the DLA-88 ligand atlases.

agent_access: PeptideAtlas web export + bulk build download; openvax/orfdata builds it locally (`peptideatlas-dog-peptides`) rather than redistributing (no stated license).
caveats: NO explicit license — flagged for redistribution/ML-training. Tryptic proteome, NOT HLA/DLA-ligand data. DOI VERIFY.

name: Chong 2020 non-canonical tumor immunopeptidome (NewAnce)
description: Proteogenomic immunopeptidomics of melanoma and lung cancer identifying non-canonical (non-coding-derived) HLA-I peptides, with the NewAnce FDR pipeline. Includes matched sequencing under controlled access.
scale: 7 melanoma cell lines + 2 lung tumor/normal pairs; canonical + non-canonical HLA-I peptides

provenance.maintainer: Ludwig Institute / UNIL (Bassani-Sternberg); PRIDE + EGA + GitHub

relevance.why: Non-canonical antigens are a frontier target class; NewAnce is a reusable noncanonical-HLAp discovery pipeline.

agent_access: MS + NewAnce jar: PRIDE PXD013649 (open, bulk). Code: github.com/bassanilab/NewAnce. Matched sequence data: EGA EGAS00001003723 / EGAS00001003724 - CONTROLLED (requires Data Access Committee approval; not agent-fetchable without a DUA).
caveats: RED FLAG (access): the paired sequencing is EGA controlled-access (DUA, human subjects). The immunopeptidomics (PXD013649) itself is open CC0. Human only.

name: Monoallelic DLA-88 Immunopeptidome Atlas (10 alleles, preprint)
description: Monoallelic LC-MS/MS atlas across 10 prevalent canine DLA-88 alleles using melanoma-derived cell lines each expressing one functional DLA-88 allele; ~32,702 naturally processed peptides (7-15 aa); reports allele binding motifs and ligand sharing vs binding-site distance.
scale: ~32,702 peptides; 10 DLA-88 alleles
license: preprint CC BY; data accession per preprint (VERIFY)

relevance.why: The single largest allele-resolved canine MHC-I ligand set — enough to train/benchmark DLA-88 presentation predictors. Core to closing the canine presentation gap.

agent_access: Peptide tables in supplement; raw MS via PRIDE/ProteomeXchange — confirm the PXD accession in the preprint's data-availability (NOT independently verified; may differ from PXD074485).
caveats: PREPRINT, not peer-reviewed. DLA-88 class I only (10 alleles); other loci + all class II absent. Data accession UNVERIFIED here.

name: Cis/trans spliced HLA-I peptide immunopeptidome (Faridi et al. 2018, Purcell lab)
description: LC-MS/MS immunopeptidomics dataset ("Trans-splicing of class I HLA bound peptides diversifies the immunopeptidome") supporting the claim that a subset of HLA-I ligands are not genomically templated but arise from proteasome-catalysed cis-/trans-peptide splicing. A contested but heavily re-analysed resource for post-translationally generated (spliced) antigens.
scale: HLA-I elution across cell lines/alleles; spliced-peptide fraction estimates

relevance.why: Spliced peptides, if real at scale, expand the presentable antigen space and complicate genome-anchored prediction; essential data for the "believe vs prove" line on spliced antigens.

agent_access: PRIDE bulk download, no auth.
caveats: SCIENTIFIC DISPUTE: later Science Immunology comment (10.1126/sciimmunol.aaw1622) argues the spliced-peptide fraction is overestimated (<1% at 1% FDR) and that only 8 result files were shared. Treat spliced-peptide counts as contested. No explicit reuse license beyond PRIDE terms.

name: Gfeller 2018 meningioma HLA-I peptidome (length/multiple specificity)
description: Newly generated HLA-I immunopeptidomes from human meningioma samples used to study peptide length distributions and multiple specificity, extending MixMHCp/MixMHCpred.
scale: 31,896 unique peptides across 84 HLA-I alleles (12 peptidomes)

relevance.why: Length-distribution modeling feeds MixMHCpred allele coverage; useful HLA-I positives from a tissue type under-represented elsewhere.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD009925 via API/FTP; bulk-downloadable.
caveats: Source-paper DOI (10.4049/jimmunol.1800504) inferred from search, not opened at catalog time - verify. Human only.

name: HLA Ligand Atlas (DDA main deposition, PXD019643)
description: Benign (non-tumor) human HLA class I and II immunopeptidome — a negative/self reference for picking truly tumor-restricted targets. Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) LC-MS/MS of HLA-eluted peptides from paired autopsy tissues. Experimentally MEASURED presented ligands (not predicted). Portal: hla-ligand-atlas.org.
scale: ~227 ligandomes (198 HLA-I + 220 HLA-II) across 29 benign tissue types from 21 subjects; raw+processed MS

provenance.maintainer: Rammensee/Walz groups, University of Tübingen (deposited to PRIDE/ProteomeXchange)

relevance.why: The key benign-tissue "what NOT to target" reference: subtracting self-ligands presented on normal tissue is essential for safe tumor-antigen/neoantigen target selection and for calibrating presentation models.

agent_access: Fully automatable via PRIDE/ProteomeXchange: HTTP/FTP/Aspera bulk download, no auth. Very large (~1.4 TB) — plan storage/bandwidth. Portal also serves a queryable peptide table.
caveats: PRIDE attaches no SPDX license (license: unknown) but ProteomeXchange policy is open download/reuse — confirm before redistribution. Massive volume. Benign reference, not cancer peptides — use as negative set/filter.

name: HLA Ligand Atlas — DIA-SWATH benign immunopeptidome extension
description: Data-independent acquisition (DIA-SWATH) extension of the HLA Ligand Atlas: matched DIA LC-MS/MS runs over the same benign tissues/subjects as the original DDA atlas, increasing sensitivity and depth of the normal-tissue HLA-I/II presentation reference. (Cross-references presentation agent.)
scale: Extends to ~30 benign tissues, 51 HLA-I and 86 HLA-II alleles; 1,274 DDA runs referenced, DIA runs here

relevance.why: Deeper, more sensitive normal-tissue presentation reference than DDA alone — strengthens the self-presentation filter (removing candidate epitopes presented on benign tissue).

agent_access: Bulk DIA raw + results via PRIDE (PXD024837) FTP/Globus; query/download via hla-ligand-atlas.org. No auth.
caveats: Accession attribution between DDA/DIA records is inconsistent across the paper's text — verify PXD024837 vs PXD020186/PXD019643 on PRIDE before use. OVERLAPS presentation agent and the domain-5 hla-ligand-atlas-normal entry — cross-reference, do not deep-duplicate. Confirm the DIA paper's exact DOI.
accessions: related DDA: PXD020186, PXD019643; dynamic-range: PXD024809

name: HLA Ligand Atlas — glioblastoma use-case subset (PXD020186)
description: Companion PRIDE deposition under the HLA Ligand Atlas title, focused on glioblastoma samples used to illustrate tumor-associated target prioritization against the benign reference. Measured HLA-eluted ligands.
scale: 3 glioblastoma samples (illustrative subset); 43 files

relevance.why: Concrete tumor-vs-benign target-prioritization example (GBM) directly relevant to presentation-based target nomination workflows.

agent_access: PRIDE bulk download, no auth, modest size (~18 GB). Fully automatable.
caveats: license: unknown (PRIDE open policy). Small illustrative subset, not a cohort.

name: Immune Epitope Database (IEDB)
description: The largest curated resource of experimentally characterized immune epitopes (B-cell, T-cell, MHC binding, and MHC-ligand elution), manually extracted from the published literature plus direct submissions. Covers class I and class II, infectious disease, allergy, autoimmunity, and cancer. Includes the full assay context (host, MHC restriction, assay type, qualitative/quantitative result).
scale: ~1.6M-2.2M epitopes, ~6.8M assays from >25,000 publications (2024/2025 update)

provenance.maintainer: La Jolla Institute for Immunology (NIH/NIAID funded, contract 75N93019C00001)

relevance.why: Foundational training/validation corpus for both presentation (MHC-ligand elution, binding) and recognition (TCR-epitope) models. The benchmark most MHC predictors cite.

agent_access: Full weekly bulk exports (XML/MySQL/CSV/TSV/XLSX/JSON), no auth, directly wget-able from database_export_v3.php. Public REST query API at query-api.iedb.org (PostgREST-style) for subset pulls. Fully bulk-downloadable by an automated agent.
caveats: License statements conflict across IEDB pages: the citation page states CC BY 4.0 while the older terms_of_use_v3 page describes NIAID/government data as effectively public domain, and a third-party data.gov record lists ODbL. Treat as CC BY 4.0 and attribute both IEDB and original data authors. Heavy dedup/normalization needed (same epitope across many assays/papers; mixed qualitative + quantitative). Canine (DLA) coverage is sparse.

name: In vivo autochthonous tumour immunopeptidome via KbStrep GEMM (PXD033232)
description: MHC-I immunopeptidomics from autochthonous mouse tumours using a genetically engineered KbStrep allele (StrepTag knocked into H2-K1) enabling StrepTactin affinity purification of MHC-I peptides directly from KP pancreatic (PDAC) and lung (LUAD) adenocarcinoma in vivo. Identified 438 tumour-specific peptides, 192 of which were missed by conventional antibody immunoprecipitation; several LUAD peptides derive from genes with minimal cognate mRNA.
scale: 438 tumour-specific peptides (192 unique to StrepTactin purification); PDAC + LUAD GEMMs

provenance.maintainer: Jaeger, Stopfer, White et al. (MIT/Koch Institute); PRIDE deposit

relevance.why: Rare in vivo (not cultured-line) mouse tumour ligandome; gold standard for what is actually presented by autochthonous tumours, incl. non-canonical / low-mRNA antigens that cell-line immunopeptidomics and RNA-based prediction miss.

agent_access: Anonymous PRIDE FTP; bulk per-file download. Verify exact subfolder path under the 2022 archive via the ProteomeXchange landing page.
caveats: No explicit per-dataset SPDX license on PRIDE. Two accessions exist (peer-reviewed PXD033232 vs preprint PXD026337) — dedup to PXD033232.

name: Tissue-based draft map of the murine MHC class I immunopeptidome (PXD008733 / SYSMHC00018)
description: Mass-spectrometry immunopeptidome of H2-Db/H2-Kb-eluted peptides across 19 normal C57BL/6 tissues plus mouse tumour cell lines (EL4, LLC1/LL2, B16F10). ~30,000 high-confidence H2-Db/Kb ligands identified and annotated, built as a reference "draft map" of the steady-state mouse MHC-I ligandome. Raw files on PRIDE; curated identifications mirrored in the SysteMHC Atlas (SYSMHC00018) and SWATH Atlas, with a figshare collection of supplementary tables.
scale: ~30,000 high-confidence H2-Db/Kb peptides; 19 normal tissues + 3-4 tumour lines

provenance.maintainer: Schuster/Caron et al.; deposited at PRIDE (EMBL-EBI); mirrored at SysteMHC Atlas

relevance.why: The canonical normal-tissue mouse H2-Db/Kb ligandome needed to subtract self from tumour-specific signal in syngeneic models; direct training/validation data for murine presentation prediction and for cross-species transfer to human.

agent_access: Anonymous PRIDE FTP, per-file wget/rsync. SysteMHC Atlas offers parsed peptide tables via its web UI. No auth; raw files are large (GB-scale).
caveats: PRIDE does not attach an explicit per-dataset license; data are "freely available" but no SPDX license is stated — confirm before redistribution. Raw .raw files need reprocessing to reach peptide lists; use the SysteMHC/figshare tables for ready IDs.

name: Pearson 2016 MHC-I-associated peptides (MAPs) from B-LCLs
description: HLA-I MAPs from B lymphocytes of 18 individuals with paired RNA-seq, used to model which genomic regions generate presented peptides. Pairs immunopeptidome with transcriptome.
scale: 25,270 MAPs; 18 individuals; 27 HLA-A/B allotypes
license: CC0 1.0 (PRIDE default); RNA-seq via SRA BioProject terms

provenance.maintainer: IRIC / Université de Montréal (Perreault lab); PRIDE + SRA + IEDB

relevance.why: Paired peptidome + transcriptome supports expression-aware presentation features; MAP list also submitted to IEDB (ref 1000704).

agent_access: MS: PRIDE PXD004023 (API/FTP). RNA-seq: SRA BioProject PRJNA286122. Peptide list also in IEDB (reference 1000704). Bulk-downloadable.
caveats: RNA-seq is controlled only by SRA/BioProject norms (open). Human only.

name: ProteomeXchange (PRIDE / MassIVE / jPOST / iProX)
description: The federated primary repositories for raw mass-spec proteomics, including the bulk of raw immunopeptidomics (HLA-elution) datasets underlying every reprocessed atlas. ProteomeXchange assigns PXD accessions; PRIDE and MassIVE host the files. The source layer if you want to reprocess raw spectra yourself.
scale: Tens of thousands of PXD datasets; hundreds are immunopeptidomics; TB-scale raw files
license: CC0 1.0 (PX default since 2020; Panorama Public / iProX default CC BY)

provenance.maintainer: ProteomeXchange consortium (EBI-PRIDE, UCSD-MassIVE, jPOST, iProX, Panorama)

relevance.why: The ground-truth raw-data source for building our own uniformly reprocessed immunopeptidome. Reprocessing raw files (vs. trusting others' peptide lists) controls FDR and label quality end-to-end.

agent_access: PRIDE REST API (ws/archive/v2) + pridepy client; MassIVE FTP; the `ppx` Python package resolves PXD accessions across repositories and downloads files. Fully bulk-downloadable but TB-scale - plan storage/compute. No auth for public datasets.
caveats: CC0 is the default but PER-DATASET terms vary (some older sets, Panorama/iProX use CC BY; a few are embargoed/private until publication) - check each PXD record. Finding immunopeptidomics subsets requires keyword/metadata filtering. Canine sets exist but are rare (e.g. PXD074485, canine tumor antigen presentation).

name: PXD074485 — Identical Tumor Antigen Peptides by Canine & Human MHC-I (Kaabinejadian, iScience 2026)
description: ProteomeXchange/PRIDE immunopeptidomics: DLA-bound peptides purified from 4 dog tumors (osteosarcoma, two anal sac adenocarcinomas, oral melanoma) and 3 human HCT116 lines each transduced with one DLA-88 allele (DLA-88*012:01 named). Shows 30-55% of canine tumor peptides are identical to human HLA-I peptides in IEDB. Instruments TripleTOF 5600 / ZenoTOF 7600. PEAKS tables = 76,550 rows.
scale: 4 dog tumors + 3 monoallelic human lines; 76,550 PEAKS rows

relevance.why: THE empirical dog<->human presentation-overlap dataset and native canine tumor MHC-I ligands. Top-priority raw data for Veritope's canine presentation models.

agent_access: PRIDE REST API v2 + FTP bulk (RAW + result files); no auth. Derived PEAKS tables also packaged in openvax/orfdata (`kaabinejadian-dog-dla-ligands`, CC0).
caveats: submissionType=PARTIAL (not all raw runs deposited; ~1,695 rows lack deposited RAW). Only DLA-88; small allele set. Unique 8-14mer monoallelic counts ~591 and ~1,465 per line.

name: Identical Tumor Antigen Peptides by Canine & Human MHC-I (PXD074485)
description: Immunopeptidomics purifying DLA-bound peptides from canine tumors and DLA-transduced monoallelic cell lines (e.g., DLA-88*003:02, *012:01 in HCT116), showing 30-55% of canine tumor peptides are identical to human HLA-I peptides reported in IEDB — direct evidence for cross-species shared presentation.
scale: canine tumor + monoallelic cell-line runs (ProteomeXchange deposit)

relevance.why: Quantifies dog<->human presentation overlap — the empirical basis for transferring human immunology knowledge to the dog. High-priority raw data for our presentation models.

agent_access: PRIDE REST API + FTP bulk download of RAW/result files; no auth.
caveats: Small and tumor/line-specific; may be from the same group as the DLA-88 atlas (possible overlap). Verify exact allele coverage and dedup against the atlas.

name: Racle 2019 HLA-II immunopeptidome (MixMHC2pred)
description: HLA class II immunopeptidomes with motif deconvolution used to build MixMHC2pred, one of the leading class II predictors.
scale: 99,265 unique HLA-II ligands

relevance.why: Class II positive set + deconvolved motifs; benchmark for HLA-II presentation.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD012308 (API/FTP) + Supplementary Data peptide tables. Bulk-downloadable.
caveats: Associated MixMHC2pred tool carries the Gfeller for-profit-license restriction (see domain-1 mixmhcpred); the deposited raw data itself is CC0 via PRIDE. Human only.

name: Racle 2023 pan-species MHC-II ligandome (627K)
description: A large curated MHC class II ligand dataset across human, mouse, cattle and chicken, with motifs for 88 alleles and an alternative class II binding mode - the largest MHC-II immunopeptidome corpus to date.
scale: 627,013 unique MHC-II ligands; motifs for 88 alleles

relevance.why: Largest HLA-II positive set AND multi-species (cattle, chicken) - directly useful for cross-species presentation modeling, a stepping stone toward canine.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD034773 (API/FTP) + supplementary tables. Bulk-downloadable, CC0.
caveats: Underpins MixMHC2pred 2.0 (tool has for-profit-license clause); raw data CC0. No dog.

name: Sarkizova/HLAthena mono-allelic immunopeptidome (MassIVE MSV000084172 + MSV000084442)
description: Large mono-allelic HLA class I immunopeptidome generated by expressing single HLA alleles in cell lines and eluting/sequencing their ligands — the training data behind the HLAthena presentation predictor. Experimentally measured ligands; mono-allelic design gives clean per-allele motifs. Patient-sample data in a companion accession.
scale: >185,000 peptides from 95 mono-allelic HLA-A/-B/-C/-G cell lines

provenance.maintainer: Keskin/Carr/Wu labs, Broad Institute & DFCI; MassIVE/ProteomeXchange

relevance.why: Per-allele mono-allelic ligand data is the cleanest substrate for training HLA-I presentation/binding models (powering HLAthena) — high-value for a presentation program.

agent_access: MassIVE open download (MSV000084172 cell lines; MSV000084442 patient samples), no auth. Automatable via FTP.
caveats: license: unknown (MassIVE/ProteomeXchange open). Companion mono-allelic sets in MSV000080527 (see abelin-2017). Cell-line mono-allelic motifs may not fully capture tissue co-regulation.

name: Sarkizova 2020 95-allele mono-allelic HLA-I (HLAthena)
description: The largest mono-allelic HLA class I immunopeptidome at publication: peptides from 95 HLA-A/B/C/G mono-allelic cell lines, underpinning the HLAthena predictor. The reference mono-allelic corpus for pan-allele HLA-I presentation modeling.
scale: ~185,000 peptides across 95 HLA-A/B/C/G alleles (raw spectra for 79/95 deposited)

relevance.why: Broad allele coverage makes it the backbone positive set for pan-allele presentation predictors and for validating allele-specific motifs.

agent_access: MassIVE MSV000084172 (PSM tables for all 95 alleles + raw spectra for 79) and a companion MSV000084442; GEO GSE131267. HLAthena predictions via hlathena.tools. Bulk-downloadable, CC0.
caveats: Raw spectra incomplete (79/95); PSM tables cover all 95. Confirm which accession (MSV000084172 vs MSV000084442) holds the files you need. Human only.

name: Schuster 2017 ovarian carcinoma immunopeptidome
description: HLA class I/II ligandome of epithelial ovarian carcinomas compared to benign tissue to nominate tumor-associated antigens - a tumor-vs-normal presentation dataset.
scale: Large-scale HLA ligandome across ovarian tumor and benign tissues

relevance.why: Tumor-vs-benign comparison is the exact triage logic for target nomination; complements the HLA Ligand Atlas benign reference.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD007635 via API/FTP; bulk-downloadable.
caveats: Multi-allelic tissue data (deconvolution needed). Human only.

name: SysteMHC Atlas (v2.0)
description: Curated repository of mass-spectrometry immunopeptidomics datasets reprocessed through a uniform pipeline into HLA/MHC peptide spectral libraries across many allotypes and studies (incl. normal and non-normal sources). A one-stop harmonized immunopeptidome resource; filter for normal-tissue datasets. (Cross-references presentation agent.)
scale: v2.0: ~1.0M unique class I + ~1.1M class II peptides; 7,190 MS files; 303 allotypes; 471K modified peptides

provenance.maintainer: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (formerly ETH Zurich / Aebersold lab); current host systemhc.sjtu.edu.cn

relevance.why: Harmonized immunopeptidome libraries let you check whether a peptide has been observed as an HLA ligand (and in what context); normal-source subsets contribute to the self-presentation filter.

agent_access: Bulk download of spectral libraries + reprocessed files from the portal (HTTPS); pipeline on Zenodo. No auth. (Original systemhcatlas.org superseded by systemhc.sjtu.edu.cn.)
caveats: No explicit data license found on the site (v1.0 paper CC BY-NC covers the article only, not the data) - marked unknown; confirm terms before redistribution/ML use. Built from public raw data so re-use may inherit per-dataset ProteomeXchange terms. Canine coverage: none known.

name: SysteMHC Atlas — murine MHC-I draft map (SYSMHC00018 / PXD008733)
description: Tissue-based draft map of the murine MHC class I immunopeptidome, a flagship SysteMHC Atlas deposition. Experimentally measured eluted ligands, reprocessed through the SysteMHC pipeline. The broader SysteMHC Atlas v2.0 portal (systemhc.sjtu.edu.cn) aggregates 7,190 MS files / 303 allotypes with allele- and PTM-specific spectral libraries; pipeline on Zenodo (record 10011925).
scale: Murine MHC-I draft map; SysteMHC v2.0 overall: 7,190 MS files, 303 allotypes, +280,126 peptides in 2024-06 release

provenance.maintainer: Shao/Aebersold et al.; portal at Shanghai Jiao Tong University

relevance.why: Harmonized MS immunopeptidome spectral libraries (incl. mouse) for training/benchmarking presentation predictors; mouse data support cross-species comparative work.

agent_access: Portal Download section (allele/PTM spectral libraries); raw in PRIDE (PXD008733, ~251 GB) + repo; pipeline on Zenodo (10011925). Automatable; no auth.
caveats: license: unknown across portal/PRIDE (ProteomeXchange open policy). This entry's size_bytes is the murine deposition only, not the whole v2.0 atlas. Reprocessed data carry source-study provenance.

name: NetMHCIIpan-4.3 targeted HLA-DP/DQ immunopeptidome (PXD044810)
description: Targeted HLA class II immunopeptidomics (notably HLA-DP) generated to close the cross-loci prediction gap for NetMHCIIpan 4.3, improving DR/DQ/DP coverage.
scale: New targeted DP/DQ/DR eluted-ligand data (multi-sample)

provenance.maintainer: University of Oklahoma HSC (Hildebrand/Yari) + DTU (NetMHCIIpan); PRIDE

relevance.why: HLA-DP/DQ are under-modeled relative to DR; this fills a real class II gap for presentation prediction.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD044810 via API/FTP; bulk-downloadable, no auth.
caveats: Exact 4.3 publication DOI not confirmed at catalog time (dataset predates/accompanies the method update) - verify. Human only.

name: Allele Frequency Net Database (AFND)
description: A repository of HLA (and KIR, MIC, cytokine) allele, genotype, and haplotype frequencies across worldwide populations, with a gold-standard data classification. Used to weight/prioritize alleles by population prevalence.
scale: Thousands of population samples across 8 HLA genes (+KIR/MIC/cytokine); millions of typings

provenance.maintainer: University of Liverpool (Andrew R. Jones et al.)

relevance.why: Population allele frequencies decide which HLA alleles to prioritize for population coverage in presentation/design (shared-antigen vaccine or TCR design).

agent_access: Native access is paginated HTML tables (scrape-only, no clean bulk API) - a real friction point for agents. Community mirrors exist: slowkow/allelefrequencies (single afnd.tsv, MIT-licensed repo) and the HLAfreq Python package automate download/combination. Prefer those for bulk pulls.
caveats: AFND's own site has "Licensing" and "Disclaimer" pages that were not retrievable at catalog time - data license marked unknown; confirm before redistribution. AFND asks you to also cite the ORIGINAL publication of each dataset used. Community mirror's MIT license covers the repo/code, not the underlying frequencies.

name: BarkBase — Canine Epigenomic Annotation
description: Epigenomic reference for the dog: RNA-seq, WGS and ATAC-seq across 27 adult tissues (with replicates) plus staged embryonic timepoints, with a download portal. Foundational for regulatory annotation of the canine genome.
scale: 27 adult tissues + embryonic timepoints; 37/46 ATAC-seq libraries passed QC
license: unknown (portal download; SRA raw reads public-domain norms)

relevance.why: Tissue-level regulatory annotation helps interpret expression context of tumor antigens; a baseline for "self" expression used in neoantigen filtering.

agent_access: Portal downloads + SRA raw reads (project IDs in supp. Table S1); no auth.
caveats: ATAC-seq quality limited (many samples FRiP <0.3, below ENCODE threshold); not ENCODE-depth. No MHC/immune-specific layer. License not explicitly stated.

name: CAID (Critical Assessment of Intrinsic Disorder)
description: CASP-style blind benchmark for intrinsic disorder and disordered-binding-region prediction, built on community-curated DisProt annotations (plus DisProt-PDB / DisProt-Binding reference sets). Defines where a sequence does NOT adopt a single stable 3D structure — an important complement/caveat to folding models.
scale: CAID1: 646 proteins, 43 methods; CAID2: expanded DisProt-based sets (e.g. 210-protein NOX subset)

relevance.why: Disorder labels mark regions where sequence->single-structure assumptions break down (low-pLDDT regions in AFDB often coincide); useful for masking/ confidence modelling and for antigen-flexibility reasoning.

agent_access: Reference datasets and predictions downloadable from the CAID portal / OpenEBench; DisProt has a REST API and flat-file downloads. No auth.
caveats: Tangential to 3D coordinate learning (disorder, not folds) — included as a boundary/negative-signal resource. Datasets are small (benchmark scale). Cite DisProt/CAID.

name: CAMEO (Continuous Automated Model EvaluatiOn)
description: Weekly, fully automated blind benchmark that evaluates structure (and other) prediction servers on soon-to-be-released PDB targets. Provides continuous, ongoing held-out assessment data complementing the biennial CASP.
scale: Weekly targets since 2012 (rolling archive of predictions + scores)

relevance.why: Continuous, low-leakage evaluation stream for monitoring folding-model performance on fresh structures — useful for tracking model drift between CASP rounds.

agent_access: Per-window "Raw Data" downloads over HTTPS; no auth. Some older category pages frozen. Agent can fetch snapshots.
caveats: RED FLAG: CC BY-SA 4.0 share-alike — derivatives inherit the license. Primarily an evaluation resource, not a bulk training corpus; download layout can change.

name: CanFam3.1 Reference Assembly (Boxer "Tasha")
description: The long-standing Boxer-derived dog reference genome (Sep 2011, Broad). Still the most widely used coordinate system for legacy canine GEO/SRA studies and most published tumor variant calls.
scale: ~2.4 Gb; 39 chromosomes (38 autosomes + X)
license: public (INSDC / Ensembl — no restriction on use)

relevance.why: Default coordinate space for historical canine cancer datasets; needed for liftover and to interpret legacy mutation calls.

agent_access: Bulk FASTA/GTF from Ensembl/UCSC/NCBI FTP; no auth. UCSC canFam3.
caveats: Fragmented vs newer long-read assemblies; coordinate mismatch with CanFam4/ROS/Tasha1.0 — liftover required. Aging annotation.

name: CATH / CATH-Gene3D
description: Hierarchical structural classification of protein domains (Class, Architecture, Topology/fold, Homologous superfamily) derived from PDB, extended to sequence space via Gene3D (HMM-based assignment to UniProt). Provides domain boundaries, fold labels and representative/non-redundant sets used to build leakage-free ML train/test splits.
scale: v4.3.0: 500,238 classified structural domains, 5,481 superfamilies; ~151M predicted sequence domains (Gene3D)
license: custom (Gene3D copyright; research use, no resale, attribution)

provenance.maintainer: Orengo group, UCL (Global Biodata Core Resource)

relevance.why: Standard source of fold/superfamily labels and non-redundant domain sets for structure-aware pretraining and for defining clustered data splits that prevent homology leakage between train and test.

agent_access: Open FTP/HTTPS bulk download and FunFam/sequence search APIs; no auth. Agent-mirrorable.
caveats: RED FLAG: data files are Gene3D copyright with a research-use policy that forbids resale and requires acknowledgement — NOT a CC licence. Confirm terms before redistribution or commercial product use. Classification lags PDB.

name: Cell Ontology (CL)
description: Structured, species-neutral ontology of cell types (including immune cell types) used as the controlled vocabulary for annotating single-cell datasets (e.g. CELLxGENE, Tabula Sapiens). The backbone for harmonizing cell-type labels across sources.
scale: thousands of cell-type classes

relevance.why: Required controlled vocabulary to merge cell-type annotations across atlases and to query cells by type programmatically (e.g. in the Census).

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: download OWL/OBO/JSON from persistent PURLs (versioned for reproducibility); query via EBI OLS API; GitHub source. Fully automatable, no auth.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 (attribution). One name annotation imported from OBO Foundry is CC0 — negligible. Do not confuse CL with CLO (Cell Line Ontology), which has its own (disputed) license.

name: COSMIC (Catalogue Of Somatic Mutations In Cancer)
description: The largest expert-curated catalogue of somatic mutations in human cancer, aggregating point mutations, CNVs, fusions, drug-resistance variants and the Cancer Gene Census from literature and large screens. Core reference for annotating which tumor variants are recurrent/driver and for mutational-signature analysis.
scale: tens of millions of coding mutations; v104+ (May 2026)
license: Custom — free for academic/non-profit (registration); commercial via QIAGEN; redistribution prohibited

relevance.why: Recurrence and driver annotation for candidate neoantigens — distinguishing recurrent hotspot mutations (shared-antigen opportunities) from private passengers, and sourcing curated fusion/resistance variants.

agent_access: Bulk downloads require a registered COSMIC account; files are fetched via authenticated HTTPS (email+password → download token/URL). Scriptable with stored credentials but NOT anonymous. Commercial automated use needs a QIAGEN license.
caveats: REDISTRIBUTION FORBIDDEN — COSMIC data may not be re-packaged or passed to third parties without a commercial licence; flag for any product that would ship derived COSMIC content. Academic licence is royalty-free but still a contract. Commercial pipelines need paid QIAGEN licensing.

name: CTdatabase — cancer-testis antigen knowledge base
description: Curated knowledge base of cancer-testis antigens (CTAs): gene aliases, RefSeq accessions, genomic locations, splice variants and family members, plus manually curated mRNA/protein expression and antigen-specific immune-response data in cancer patients. The reference catalogue for the classic shared tumor-antigen class (MAGE, NY-ESO-1, SSX, etc.).
scale: Hundreds of curated CTA genes/families with expression + immunogenicity annotation

provenance.maintainer: Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research / LNCC (Brazil)

relevance.why: The canonical CTA reference for shared tumor antigens — a baseline antigen list to cross- check non-canonical/TE/ERV candidates against established cancer-germline antigens.

agent_access: Web interface (cta.lncc.br); no documented bulk-download API — may require scraping. Verify the site resolves before relying on it.
caveats: NO explicit license stated (flag before redistribution/ML training). Site is legacy (core content ~2009) and availability can be intermittent. Human only.

name: Darwin's Ark — Companion-Animal Citizen-Science Genomics
description: Open citizen-science cohort (co-founded by E. Karlsson) linking owner-reported phenotype questionnaires to low-pass WGS in tens of thousands of dogs. Phenotype + genotype data released openly (e.g., Dryad) alongside behavior-genetics publications.
scale: ~48,500+ dogs registered; sequenced subset in the thousands

relevance.why: Large open germline + phenotype resource; breed-structure and germline background useful for population-aware variant interpretation. Minimal direct oncology/immune content.

agent_access: Dryad bulk downloads (CC0); surveys as CSV. No auth.
caveats: Behavior/morphology focus, not cancer; low-pass depth limits somatic/immune uses.

name: Dog10K / CanFam canine reference genome & variation
description: Canine reference genome assemblies and a large multi-omics variation resource for dogs and wild canids. Centers on the UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0 (canFam4, German Shepherd) assembly with GFF annotation, plus the Dog10K consortium SNV/structural-variant panel from ~2000 canids. The primary dog reference for the comparative-oncology program.
scale: SNPs from ~2,075 individuals; VCF from 1,987 samples (phase-1 from 1,929)
license: unknown (freely available online; no explicit license posted)

provenance.maintainer: Dog10K Consortium (incl. Kunming Inst. Zoology CAS; Kidd lab, U Michigan; iDog/NGDC)

relevance.why: The canine reference genome + variation baseline needed to translate human target/antigen concepts into dog (naturally occurring canine cancers as comparative-oncology models) and to distinguish germline canine variation from tumor-specific changes.

agent_access: Genome FASTA (GCF_011100685.1_UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0), GFF, aliases, and SNV VCFs download from the Dog10K site; variant files/annotations mirrored on the Kidd lab share (kiddlabshare.med.umich.edu/dog10K/) and Zenodo (record 8084059). UCSC canFam4 and NCBI Datasets also serve the assembly. No auth.
caveats: Dog10K portal does not state an explicit license — treat as unknown and rely on the NCBI/UCSC assembly (unrestricted) + cite the papers; verify terms for the variant panel before redistribution. Multiple canine assemblies in circulation (canFam3.1/4/5/6, ROS_Cfam_1.0) — fix one and be consistent. Canine gene annotation is less mature than human.

name: Dog10K_Boxer_Tasha_1.0 (Long-read Boxer assembly)
description: Long-read (PacBio) reassembly of the original Boxer "Tasha", scaffolded against CanFam3.1. NCBI GCF_000002285.5; UCSC canFam6. Higher contiguity on the historical Boxer background.
scale: chromosome-level; ~2.4 Gb

relevance.why: Bridges legacy Boxer-based (CanFam3.1) resources with long-read quality; useful for DLA-region assembly comparisons.

agent_access: NCBI Datasets / FTP; no auth. UCSC canFam6.
caveats: A third coordinate system — adds to the dog-reference fragmentation problem. Note: ROS_Cfam_1.0 (GCF_014441545.1, canFam5) is the current NCBI RefSeq reference for Canis lupus familiaris.

name: DoGA — Dog Genome Annotation (Integrative Epigenome Map)
description: Integrative dog epigenome reference annotation (RNA-seq + regulatory marks) across many tissues for comparative inter-tissue and cross-species studies; complements BarkBase.
scale: multi-tissue epigenome (dozens of tissues/samples)
license: CC BY 4.0 (article); data via SRA/GEO public norms

provenance.maintainer: DoGA consortium (incl. University of Helsinki / Lohi, Broad)

relevance.why: Stronger regulatory/expression annotation than BarkBase; supports gene-model and self-expression references for the dog.

agent_access: Processed tracks + raw reads via GEO/SRA/EGA (check paper data-availability for exact accession and any controlled-access splits); no auth for public parts.
caveats: Not tied to Darwin's Ark/Karlsson despite overlap of people; confirm exact accessions. ENCODE-level canine functional data still does not exist.

name: ECOD (Evolutionary Classification of protein Domains)
description: Classification of PDB domains emphasising distant evolutionary (homologous) relationships, with an automatically updated hierarchy (X/H/T/F groups). Recent releases extend classification to AlphaFold DB models (AFDB-ECOD), giving domain labels over predicted structures too.
scale: >500,000 PDB domains (~3,400 homologous groups); plus AFDB-derived domains

relevance.why: Evolution-aware domain boundaries and remote-homology groupings help define challenging, leakage-controlled splits and augment fold-label coverage, including over predicted (AFDB) structures.

agent_access: Flat-file distributions downloadable over HTTP; no auth. Agent-mirrorable. No documented bulk API.
caveats: RED FLAG: no explicit license found on the site — treat as unknown and confirm reuse terms before redistribution. Served over plain HTTP; verify integrity.

name: Ensembl (genomes, gene models, comparative genomics)
description: Reference genome assemblies with automated + manually integrated gene annotation, variation, regulation, and comparative genomics for vertebrates. Provides human (GRCh38, with GENCODE as the human gene set) and multiple dog assemblies (incl. ROS_Cfam_1.0, UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0/canFam4, Boxer Tasha), with cross-species orthology.
scale: Hundreds of vertebrate genomes; human GRCh38 + GRCh37; multiple dog assemblies

relevance.why: Supplies the human and dog reference genomes + gene models underpinning transcript/protein references and variant interpretation. Cross-species orthology directly serves the comparative-oncology (canine) program (mapping human targets to the dog genome).

agent_access: REST API (rest.ensembl.org; GRCh37 mirror grch37.rest.ensembl.org), Perl API, BioMart, and FTP for FASTA/GTF/GFF3/VCF. No auth. Highly scriptable; per-release archive hosts for pinning.
caveats: Multiple dog assemblies exist — pick one deliberately (ROS_Cfam_1.0 vs UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0/canFam4) and keep human/dog coordinate systems consistent. Release-versioned; pin releases for reproducibility.

name: GENCODE (reference gene annotation)
description: The reference gene annotation for the human (and mouse) genome: comprehensive, manually curated + computationally supported models of protein-coding genes, lncRNAs, pseudogenes, and alternative splicing on GRCh38. Adopted as the human gene set in Ensembl and (via MANE) aligned with RefSeq.
scale: Human ~63,000 genes, ~20,000 protein-coding, ~250,000 transcripts (recent releases)

provenance.maintainer: GENCODE consortium (EMBL-EBI/HAVANA + collaborators), part of ENCODE

relevance.why: The authoritative transcript/ORF catalog defining the canonical human proteome coordinate space. Alternative-splice and ORF annotation is the substrate for enumerating normal protein products vs. candidate tumor-specific transcripts/ORFs.

agent_access: Direct HTTPS/FTP download of GTF/GFF3 and transcript/translation FASTA per release; small, scriptable, versioned. No auth, no API needed (static files).
caveats: No explicit standalone license document — data is free/open but cite the GENCODE paper; verify terms if redistributing. Human + mouse only (no dog — use Ensembl/RefSeq for canine annotation). Pin release number (annotation changes between releases).

name: IMGT Dog (Canis lupus familiaris) IG/TR Germline Reference
description: IMGT's curated germline annotation of the canine immunoglobulin (IGH, IGK, IGL) and T-cell-receptor (TRA/TRB/TRG/TRD) loci — gene tables, allele sequences, locus maps and gene order — the canine analogue of the human IMGT germline sets used for V(D)J assignment. Underlying comprehensive annotation from Martin et al. (Immunogenetics 2017).
scale: canine IG + TR germline V/D/J/C gene tables and alleles

provenance.maintainer: IMGT, the international ImMunoGeneTics information system (Montpellier/CNRS)

relevance.why: The germline backbone for canine TCR/BCR repertoire analysis (V(D)J assignment, CDR3 calling) — essential canine-specific infrastructure where human IMGT cannot substitute. Enables canine recognition-arm work analogous to human IMGT pipelines.

agent_access: IMGT/GENE-DB and IMGT/V-QUEST provide canine reference sets; web and FASTA export. No bulk API; scraping is restricted by terms of use — prefer the provided export tools.
caveats: IMGT terms of use are restrictive (academic use, mandatory citation, redistribution limited) — verify license_url before redistributing or using for ML training. Canine TRA/TRD and light-chain annotation historically lagged; coverage still improving.

name: IMGT Canine IGK Locus Annotation (NAR Genom Bioinform 2026)
description: Dedicated IMGT annotation of the canine immunoglobulin kappa (IGK) light-chain locus on chromosome 17 (~317-349 kb; 31 genes: 25 V, 5 J, 1 C), built from Boxer (CanFam3.1) and Basenji assemblies with cross-breed insights. Fills a long-standing light-chain gap in canine immunogenetics.
scale: canine IGK locus — 31 genes (25V/5J/1C)

relevance.why: Completes the canine light-chain germline reference needed for full BCR (IGK) V(D)J analysis in the recognition program.

caveats: IMGT terms of use apply (see license_url). Breed-specific allele variation noted — confirm which reference breed matches the study samples.

name: IMGT/GENE-DB (IG & TR reference genes)
description: The international reference for immunoglobulin (IG) and T-cell receptor (TR) gene and allele nomenclature and germline reference sequences; supplies the reference directories used by IMGT/V-QUEST and most AIRR annotation tools.
scale: ~8,500 IG/TR genes across species (human + mouse core)
license: conflicting: site states CC BY 4.0; NAR 2025 states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

relevance.why: Canonical germline reference for TCR/IG gene naming and sequences — required to standardize V/D/J gene calls across all recognition datasets.

agent_access: Germline FASTA reference sets downloadable from the site; query interface for genes. No open REST API — fetch reference directories as files. IMGT/V-QUEST has a web API but with usage terms (contact IMGT).
caveats: LICENSE CONFLICT: imgt.org states CC BY 4.0 while the NAR 2025 overview states academic CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 with commercial use requiring a CNRS financial arrangement — resolve with IMGT (contact-imgt@igh.cnrs.fr) before any commercial use. Scraping discouraged; prefer the provided reference files.

name: InterPro
description: Integrative classification of proteins into families, domains and sites by combining 13+ member databases (Pfam, CATH-Gene3D, PANTHER, PROSITE, SMART, SUPERFAMILY, NCBIfam, CDD, etc.). Provides domain architectures and residue annotations across 200M+ UniProt sequences, with structural member databases (CATH-Gene3D, SUPERFAMILY) linking families to folds.
scale: Release 10x.0: 45,899 InterPro entries from 84,588 member signatures; >200M sequences
license: CC0 1.0 for InterPro-produced data; InterProScan Apache-2.0; member DBs vary

relevance.why: Domain-architecture and structural-family labels across all of UniProt provide weak supervision and conditioning signals for sequence->structure models, and a route to propagate structural family labels onto unlabelled sequences.

agent_access: Open FTP bulk download and a comprehensive REST API; no auth. Agent-mirrorable. New releases every ~8 weeks.
caveats: Member databases carry their own licenses (e.g. CATH-Gene3D research-use/no- resale; PANTHER, SMART have terms). InterPro's own aggregation is CC0 but check a member DB's terms before redistributing that portion.

name: IPD-IMGT/HLA Database
description: The authoritative reference of human HLA allele sequences and official HLA nomenclature. Provides genomic/cDNA/protein sequences, alignments, and a flat-file database. The canonical source for HLA allele definitions used by every typing and prediction pipeline.
scale: ~43,758 HLA alleles (release 3.63, Jan 2026); 47 genes; 44,876 total sequences

provenance.maintainer: Anthony Nolan Research Institute + EMBL-EBI (IPD), UK

relevance.why: Required reference to standardize HLA alleles when joining pMHC/presentation data with TCR-recognition datasets. Cross-ref the presentation agent for MHC/HLA depth — do not duplicate deeply.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: EBI FTP/HTTP file download (latest release) and GitHub (ANHIG/IMGTHLA) with a branch per release + compressed archives — ideal for version-pinned ingestion. No auth.
caveats: CC BY-ND - RED FLAG: NoDerivs means you may redistribute verbatim with attribution (commercial OK) but distributing a MODIFIED version requires prior written permission. Deriving and re-publishing altered sequence sets, or shipping a reformatted subset, needs permission. Internal use/derived features generally fine; redistribution of derivatives is the constraint. Human only.

name: IPD-MHC Database (non-human, incl. canine DLA)
description: The inter-species sister database to IPD-IMGT/HLA: curated MHC allele sequences and nomenclature for non-human species, including canine DLA. The authoritative source for DLA allele definitions (DLA-88, DLA-DRB1, etc.).
scale: >7,000 alleles across ~70 species; canine (DLA) subset is comparatively small

relevance.why: The canine DLA reference needed for any dog immuno-oncology work: pseudo-sequences and allele definitions for DLA-restricted presentation modeling. Core to Veritope's comparative-oncology angle.

agent_access: Downloadable per-species flat files + GitHub. No auth; bulk-fetchable.
caveats: CC BY-ND (same NoDerivs constraint as IPD-IMGT/HLA). Canine coverage is SPARSE relative to human - few alleles, and sequence-only (no binding/elution data here). This is the central canine gap for Veritope.

name: neXtProt
description: Human-centric protein knowledgebase built on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot and enriched with curated expression, PTM, variant, proteotypic-peptide and subcellular-localization data. Tracks the "missing proteins" / protein-existence (PE) evidence for the Human Proteome Project. A deeply annotated human "self" protein reference with peptide-level evidence.
scale: ~20,400 human protein entries; curated isoforms, PTMs, variants, peptides

provenance.maintainer: SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics (CALIPHO group)

relevance.why: Human-only, peptide-and-PTM-rich self reference; proteotypic-peptide and protein-existence annotation supports deciding whether a candidate antigen maps to a well-evidenced normal protein vs. an uncertain/missing one.

agent_access: REST API (api.nextprot.org) and SPARQL endpoint; bulk download of all annotations as XML/PEFF, plus per-entry XML/JSON/FASTA. No auth.
caveats: Data is CC BY 4.0 since 2018 (earlier releases were CC BY-ND; ignore journal-article CC BY-NC labels). Human only (no dog). Overlaps UniProt (it is built on Swiss-Prot) — use for the extra curation layer, dedup against UniProt by accession.

name: Pfam (protein families)
description: Library of protein families represented by curated multiple sequence alignments and profile HMMs, now delivered through InterPro. Many families carry structural mappings (to PDB/CATH via InterPro/SIFTS), making Pfam a bridge between sequence family space and structure.
scale: Pfam 37.x/38.0: ~20,000+ families

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI (formerly Wellcome Sanger); integrated into InterPro

relevance.why: Curated family MSAs and HMMs are standard conditioning/pretraining inputs for evolutionary-coupling and folding models; seed alignments give high-quality sequence groupings tied to structural families.

agent_access: Open FTP bulk download (full Pfam-A.hmm, seed/full alignments). No auth. Agent-mirrorable. Interactive access via the InterPro site/API.
caveats: Standalone pfam.xfam.org was decommissioned; access is now via InterPro and the EBI FTP. Pfam-produced data is CC0, but downstream UniProt sequence content has its own (CC BY 4.0) terms.

name: NCBI RefSeq (Reference Sequence Collection)
description: Curated, non-redundant reference sequences for genomes, transcripts (NM_/XM_), and proteins (NP_/XP_) across organisms, with the RefSeq Select / MANE (jointly with Ensembl) representative transcript set for human. The NCBI counterpart reference for human and dog genomes/proteomes.
scale: >400M sequences across all RefSeq organisms; human + dog fully annotated

provenance.maintainer: NCBI / U.S. National Library of Medicine (NIH)

relevance.why: Alternative/complementary reference proteome and transcriptome for human and especially dog (NCBI is the primary annotator for several canine assemblies). MANE gives a stable, agreed human transcript per gene for consistent variant and antigen coordinates.

agent_access: Bulk via NCBI FTP (per-organism and per-assembly FASTA/GFF3/GBFF). NCBI Datasets v2 REST API + CLI (dehydrated "bags" for large sets). E-utilities for record-level fetch. No auth; API key raises E-utils rate limits.
caveats: NCBI states RefSeq is "available without restriction" (U.S. gov work, effectively public domain); no single SPDX license — a few registries mislabel it (e.g. ODbL). Watch RefSeq vs GenBank accession semantics; keep assembly/annotation-release versions consistent across human and dog.

name: SCOPe (Structural Classification of Proteins - extended)
description: Manually/semi-automatically curated classification of protein domains into a class/fold/superfamily/family hierarchy, continuing SCOP. ASTRAL compendium provides sequence/structure subsets at defined identity cutoffs (e.g. 40%) widely used as non-redundant benchmark sets for fold recognition.
