scale: v2.08: 344,851 domains from 106,976 PDB entries
license: custom (freely available; no explicit SPDX license stated)

relevance.why: ASTRAL non-redundant domain subsets are a classic basis for fold-level ML benchmarks and for building clustered train/test splits; curated fold labels complement CATH.

agent_access: Open download of parseable flat files and a ~2 GB MySQL dump; also archived on Zenodo. No auth; agent-mirrorable.
caveats: License not stated as a standard SPDX id — "freely available" but confirm reuse terms before redistribution (mark license as custom/unknown). Curation lags the PDB; large fraction of recent entries unclassified.

name: Sequence Ontology (SO)
description: Standardized ontology of biological sequence features and variant/annotation terms (genes, transcripts, variants, feature types), used to normalize feature and variant vocabulary in genomics pipelines.
scale: ~2,500+ sequence-feature terms

relevance.why: Normalizes sequence-feature and variant terminology when integrating cancer-genomics and annotation data into a common schema.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: download OWL/OBO from PURL; query via EBI OLS API; GitHub source. Automatable.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 (attribution). Peripheral to single-cell/antigen data proper — included as the standard vocabulary for the genomics-feature layer of an ingestion schema.

name: UniProt / UniProtKB (Universal Protein Knowledgebase)
description: Central reference for protein sequences and functional annotation. UniProtKB combines curated Swiss-Prot and computationally annotated TrEMBL; Reference Proteomes provide one representative, non-redundant proteome per species (human UP000005640; dog present). The canonical "self" protein sequence set for immunopeptidomics search and antigen mapping.
scale: ~25,000 reference proteomes; human proteome ~20,400 canonical proteins

provenance.maintainer: UniProt Consortium (EMBL-EBI, SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics, PIR)

relevance.why: The reference "self" proteome for both human and dog — the search database against which MS immunopeptidomes are identified and the self-filter for candidate neoantigens/epitopes. Isoform and PTM annotation supports distinguishing variant vs. canonical sequence.

agent_access: REST API at rest.uniprot.org (no auth) with proteomes, uniprotkb, and ID-mapping endpoints, content negotiation to FASTA/JSON/TSV; bulk reference-proteome FASTA via FTP. Fully scriptable.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 (ignore stale "NoDerivs" claims on third-party pages). TrEMBL is unreviewed — prefer Swiss-Prot + canonical for a clean self set. Canine proteome is less deeply curated than human; many entries are TrEMBL-level.

name: UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0 / CanFam4 (German Shepherd "Mischka")
description: Uppsala University German Shepherd Dog assembly, more contiguous than CanFam3.1; the build on which Dog10K variant calls are made. NCBI GCF_011100685.1.
scale: chromosome-level; ~2.4 Gb

relevance.why: Current Dog10K coordinate system; preferred modern reference for new canine WGS/WES analysis.

agent_access: NCBI Datasets CLI / FTP; no auth. UCSC canFam4.
caveats: Not the same coordinates as CanFam3.1 or Tasha1.0 — standardize a reference across the program.

name: 10x Genomics TCR-pMHC dextramer datasets ("A New Way of Exploring Immunity")
description: Single-cell 5' immune profiling of CD8+ T cells from four healthy donors, each labeled with ~44-50 dCODE Dextramer (pMHC) reagents plus TotalSeq-C surface-protein antibodies, giving paired alpha/beta TCR sequences with per-cell pMHC binding calls and gene expression.
scale: ~62,858 cells, ~14,320 distinct pMHC-specific paired TCRs (application note); 4 donors

relevance.why: The canonical paired-chain, single-cell pMHC-binding dataset underpinning modern TCR specificity models and most published negative/positive splits (NetTCR, pMTnet).

agent_access: Per-donor dataset pages host binarized CSV matrices and Cell Ranger outputs behind a short registration/EULA click-through; direct file URLs are fetchable once accepted.
caveats: Dextramer binding has nonspecific background; standard practice applies UMI>10 and >5x negative-control filters and drops cells with >4 specificities. CC BY 4.0 is ML/redistribution friendly (cite). Human only.

name: Transcriptomic atlas of the adult human brain (Siletti/Linnarsson)
description: Deep single-nucleus transcriptomic census of the adult human brain across ~100+ dissections spanning forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain, defining hundreds of cell-type clusters. The reference normal human brain cellular baseline.
scale: ~3.37M nuclei, ~105 dissections, 3 donors, 461 clusters

provenance.maintainer: Linnarsson lab / BRAIN Initiative Cell Census Network (BICCN)

relevance.why: Brain/neuronal expression is a severe off-tumor toxicity concern (non-regenerable tissue); a deep normal brain cell-type atlas is essential for neuro-safety screening of targets.

agent_access: Raw from NeMO Archive (HTTPS, BICCN data-use terms); processed .h5ad via CZ CELLxGENE. No auth for open files.
caveats: Only 3 donors (deep but not population-scale). NeMO/BICCN has its own data-use/attribution terms (not a standard CC license) — review before redistribution.

name: Ali/Jackson et al. 2020 — METABRIC imaging mass cytometry breast cancer
description: Imaging mass cytometry quantifying 37 proteins at subcellular resolution across 483 breast tumors from the METABRIC genomic cohort, linking spatial single-cell phenotypes to the extensively characterized METABRIC genomic/clinical data. Hosted at the Image Data Resource (IDR) as idr0076 with cell masks and multichannel images.
scale: 483 METABRIC tumors, 37-protein panel, IMC single-cell + masks

relevance.why: Couples spatial single-cell proteomics with deep genomics on the same tumors, a rare multi-modal anchor for relating antigenic/immune spatial context to genomic drivers.

agent_access: IDR download via Globus/Aspera for full images; processed single-cell data also on Zenodo (5850952) for the 2022 follow-up. Genomics/clinical via cBioPortal (METABRIC).
caveats: Full image transfer is large and Globus-based (not plain HTTPS). Linked METABRIC genomics governed separately. 2020 vs 2022 deposits differ (reanalysis/new structures).

name: Barkley et al. 2022 — Recurrent cancer cell states (pan-cancer scRNA + spatial)
description: Pan-cancer single-cell RNA-seq across 15 cancer types combined with sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics of tumor sections, defining recurrent cancer cell "states" and their specific interactions with the tumor microenvironment across tumor types.
scale: scRNA across 15 cancer types + spatial transcriptomics of multiple tumor sections

relevance.why: Cross-tumor recurrent cancer-cell states plus their spatial TME partners give a pan-cancer frame for which tumor states co-occur with immune niches.

agent_access: GEO open bulk download; matrices + spatial data. No auth. Scriptable over HTTPS/FTP.
caveats: Spatial component is a subset of tumors; combines human and mouse. Confirm per-sample platform (sequencing-based ST) before assuming Visium specifics.

name: Bi et al. 2021 — Tumor/immune reprogramming during ICB in advanced RCC (scRNA)
description: Single-cell RNA-seq of metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma sampled before or after immune checkpoint blockade (alone or with TKI), profiling how ICB remodels cancer and immune cell states and their interactions. Processed data on the Broad Single Cell Portal; raw scRNA + bulk exome under dbGaP controlled access.
scale: ~34,326 cells, 8 patients (5 ICB-treated), 10x scRNA-seq
license: custom (Broad Single Cell Portal terms); raw under dbGaP DUA

provenance.maintainer: Dana-Farber / Broad Institute; Single Cell Portal SCP1288

relevance.why: On-treatment single-cell view of ICB remodeling in an immunotherapy-responsive tumor; direct signal on how immune recognition states shift with checkpoint blockade.

agent_access: Processed matrices downloadable from Single Cell Portal after Google-account sign-in. Raw scRNA + exome require dbGaP (phs002065) controlled-access approval (DUA).
caveats: CONTROLLED ACCESS for raw (dbGaP DUA). Processed layer gated behind SCP login terms. Small patient cohort.

name: Broad Institute Single Cell Portal (SCP)
description: Hosting and interactive-visualization portal for single-cell studies, many with tumor/immune content. Each study carries expression matrices, cluster/metadata files and per-study access controls set by the submitter. A host for primary author-deposited single-cell data rather than a reprocessed atlas.
scale: >1000 public studies, ~90M cells (portal homepage, 2026)

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard

relevance.why: A large pool of primary tumor-immune single-cell studies with accession-level download, useful as raw inputs for reprocessing pipelines.

agent_access: REST API (v1) with OpenAPI docs; bulk download via portal or scripted. Some studies require sign-in / Terra authorization; download requires a Google-linked account token for protected studies. Per-study access gating must be handled programmatically.
caveats: No single data license — each study sets its own terms (some restrict redistribution). Must check each study's terms before ML training/redistribution. Code is BSD-3-Clause, not the data.

name: CancerSEA — Cancer Single-cell State Atlas
description: Atlas of 14 manually curated functional states (e.g. proliferation, invasion, stemness, hypoxia, EMT, angiogenesis) scored at single-cell resolution across cancer scRNA-seq datasets, with per-gene state-association queries and downloadable functional-state profiles and 14 state signature gene sets.
scale: ~41,900 cancer single cells, 25 cancer types, 14 functional states

provenance.maintainer: Harbin Medical University (Xia Li / Juan Xu labs)

relevance.why: Functional-state signatures provide an interpretable axis (stemness, EMT, hypoxia) to stratify tumor cells and correlate antigen-presentation state with malignant cell programs.

agent_access: Bulk download of state profiles, expression matrices and signatures via HTTP, no auth. No REST API. Signature gene sets are small and script-ingestible.
caveats: Site Help page states CC BY-NC (non-commercial); an NBDC catalog record lists CC0 but that applies to the catalog metadata, not the data — treat CC BY-NC as governing. Successor CancerSEA-X (http://biocc.hrbmu.edu.cn/CancerState, 2025) is broader but its license was not located; verify before use.

name: Additional Canine Immune scRNA Datasets (leishmaniosis, lung, canFam4, TNBC)
description: Cluster of further canine immune single-cell datasets: progressive-leishmaniosis PBMC atlas (~68,323 cells, 47 populations, iScience 2026), healthy-lung scRNA atlas, canFam4-based healthy-dog immune-subset atlas with checkpoint programs (2025 preprint), and triple-negative canine breast cancer scRNA (immune-suppressive interactions).
scale: multiple studies; tens of thousands of cells each
license: articles CC BY; data GEO/SRA public norms

relevance.why: Expands canine immune cell-type references across tissues/diseases for infiltrate annotation.

agent_access: Per-paper GEO/SRA accessions in data-availability; no auth. Some preprints.
caveats: Fragmented (no unified canine immune atlas); some preprints; accessions VERIFY per paper. No DLA typing or antigen specificity.

name: Canine Immune / PBMC Single-cell Atlases
description: Reference single-cell transcriptomic atlases of canine immune cells: circulating leukocytes in healthy and osteosarcoma dogs (~36 populations), a peripheral-blood TCRab+ T-cell atlas (incl. MAIT-like cells), a healthy-lung atlas, and a progressive-leishmaniosis PBMC atlas (~68,323 cells, 47 populations).
scale: multiple studies; tens of thousands of cells each
license: articles CC BY; data via GEO/SRA public norms

relevance.why: Cell-type references for annotating canine tumor immune infiltrates and deconvolving bulk RNA-seq; building blocks for mapping the dog immune system.

agent_access: GEO/SRA/ArrayExpress bulk downloads; no auth. Accessions in each paper's data-availability.
caveats: Fragmented across papers/accessions (no unified canine immune cell atlas); donor numbers small; DLA typing and antigen specificity absent.

name: Caushi et al. 2021 — Neoantigen-specific TIL in anti-PD-1 lung cancer (scRNA + TCR)
description: Single-cell RNA-seq and TCR-seq of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes from resectable NSCLC treated with neoadjuvant anti-PD-1, using MANA (mutation-associated neoantigen) functional expansion to identify and transcriptionally profile neoantigen-specific (vs viral- and cancer-testis-specific) T cells and their programs.
scale: NSCLC neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 cohort; MANA/viral/CT-antigen-specific TIL scRNA + TCR

provenance.maintainer: Smith/Pardoll/Anagnostou labs (Johns Hopkins) / GEO + EGA + immuneACCESS

relevance.why: Rare dataset of experimentally identified neoantigen-SPECIFIC TIL with paired transcriptome and TCR — ground truth for linking neoantigen recognition to T-cell state.

agent_access: Processed scRNA (GSE176021) and bulk TCR (GSE173351) open from GEO. Raw reads in EGA (EGAS00001005343) require controlled-access DAC approval. TCR also on Adaptive immuneACCESS (clients.adaptivebiotech.com/pub/caushi-2021-n).
caveats: CONTROLLED ACCESS for raw (EGA). Neoantigen specificity assignments are the key labeled layer; confirm which GEO subseries maps to which specificity.

name: Chevrier et al. 2017 — Immune atlas of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (CyTOF)
description: Mass cytometry immune atlas of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) using T-cell and myeloid/TAM antibody panels, profiling ~3.5 million cells across tumor, adjacent kidney, and blood to define tumor-associated immune cell states and an immune signature associated with outcome. Paired scRNA-seq in ArrayExpress.
scale: ~3.5M measured cells, ccRCC + adjacent + blood, two CyTOF panels

provenance.maintainer: Bodenmiller Lab (University of Zurich); seq in ArrayExpress E-MTAB-5640

relevance.why: Deep high-parameter immune phenotyping of a major immunotherapy-responsive tumor type (ccRCC); complements the Krishna/Bi ccRCC single-cell cohorts in this domain.

agent_access: Sequencing data (E-MTAB-5640) is open bulk download from ArrayExpress/BioStudies. CyTOF .fcs were released via the lab's project website; confirm current link.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — no explicit reuse license on the CyTOF deposit; ArrayExpress data under EBI terms. CyTOF project-site link may have moved; verify before scripting.

name: COMBAT COVID-19 Multi-Omic Blood Atlas (CITE-seq TCR)
description: Multi-omic blood atlas of COVID-19 including CITE-seq single-cell TCR chain composition alongside transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics and cytometry; served via COMBATdb with Zenodo deposits.
scale: 26 associated datasets; large CITE-seq cohort (COMBATdb)
license: mixed (Zenodo open deposits; genetic/clinical via EGA DUA)

relevance.why: Deep multi-omic immune repertoire context; CITE-seq TCR composition complements paired scTCR cohorts for disease-state modeling.

agent_access: Open processed datasets on Zenodo + COMBATdb portal; genetic data via EGA (EGAS00001005493, DUA), proteomics via PRIDE (PXD023175). Mixed open/controlled access.
caveats: Repertoire resolution is CITE-seq chain composition (not deep paired clonotypes). Controlled tiers need a DUA. Human only.

name: Canine Osteosarcoma Single-cell RNA-seq Reference
description: Treatment-naive primary canine osteosarcoma scRNA-seq reference (tumor + microenvironment / immune compartments) with processed data and an interactive cell browser; GEO GSE252470 plus a Zenodo code/data release.
scale: ~6 dogs; tens of thousands of cells

relevance.why: Resolves tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte / myeloid compartments in dog tumors — substrate for understanding the canine recognition landscape at single-cell resolution.

agent_access: GEO + Zenodo bulk downloads; no auth.
caveats: Small donor number; gene-expression TCR inference only (no paired VDJ unless separately noted).

name: Puram et al. 2017 — HNSCC scRNA-seq (GSE103322)
description: Smart-seq2 single-cell RNA-seq of ~5,902 cells from 18 oral-cavity head and neck squamous cell carcinoma patients, covering malignant, immune, fibroblast and endothelial compartments with a partial-EMT malignant program.
scale: ~5,902 cells, 18 HNSCC patients (Smart-seq2)

relevance.why: Reference HNSCC TME dataset; useful for malignant-program and stromal baselines in a comparative pipeline.

agent_access: Single supplementary matrix via GEO FTP; metadata via E-utilities. Automatable.
caveats: Smart-seq2, modest cell count. Matrix carries non-expression annotation header rows.

name: Azizi et al. 2018 — breast tumor immune scRNA-seq (GSE114725)
description: Single-cell RNA-seq map of ~45k immune cells (inDrop + 10x) across breast tumor, normal breast, blood and lymph node from 8 patients, describing a continuum of immune phenotypic states in the TME. Companion accession GSE114727 holds related samples.
scale: ~45,000 immune cells, 8 breast cancer patients (56 samples)

relevance.why: Breast TME immune reference emphasizing phenotypic continuity rather than discrete states — useful for immune-composition baselines.

agent_access: GEO supplementary matrices via FTP; mirrored in the MSKCC data catalog. Automatable. Companion accession GSE114727 should be fetched for full sample set.
caveats: Two related accessions (GSE114725 + GSE114727) — ingest both to avoid partial cohort. Mixed chemistries (inDrop/10x).

name: Jerby-Arnon et al. 2018 — melanoma ICI-resistance scRNA-seq (GSE115978)
description: Smart-seq2 single-cell RNA-seq of malignant and immune cells across melanoma tumors, used to define a malignant-cell immune-evasion / ICI-resistance program (and a T-cell exclusion signature). Includes CD4/CD8 T-cell annotations.
scale: ~7,186 cells, 31 melanoma tumors (Smart-seq2)

relevance.why: Malignant immune-evasion program directly relevant to antigen presentation and T-cell exclusion — high-value for presentation-focused analysis.

agent_access: GEO supplementary matrices via FTP; metadata via E-utilities. Automatable.
caveats: Smart-seq2. Overlaps/extends GSE72056 melanoma cohort — dedup if pooling melanoma cells.

name: Sade-Feldman et al. 2018 — melanoma checkpoint-response T cells (GSE120575)
description: Smart-seq2 single-cell RNA-seq of ~16,291 CD45+ immune cells from 48 melanoma biopsies (pre- and on-treatment, responder vs non-responder to checkpoint blockade), defining T-cell states associated with ICB response (TCF7+ CD8 memory-like vs dysfunctional).
scale: ~16,291 immune cells, 48 biopsies / 32 patients (Smart-seq2)

relevance.why: Rare public dataset linking single-cell T-cell states to checkpoint-blockade response — a key label source for immunotherapy-response modeling.

agent_access: TPM matrix + responder/pre-on-treatment metadata via GEO FTP. Automatable. Response labels per biopsy included.
caveats: Smart-seq2. Response labels at biopsy level; align carefully with cell barcodes.

name: Li et al. 2019 — melanoma dysfunctional CD8 T cells (GSE123139)
description: MARS-seq single-cell RNA-seq of T cells from ~25 melanoma patients, resolving a proliferative, dynamically regulated dysfunctional CD8 compartment (naive-like → transitional → dysfunctional trajectory) in the TME.
scale: T cells from ~25 melanoma patients (MARS-seq)

relevance.why: Defines the CD8 dysfunction trajectory central to antitumor T-cell biology and to recognition/engineering targets.

agent_access: GEO supplementary matrices via FTP. Automatable. Data-availability statement wording not directly verified in this pass — accession appears consistently across reuse.
caveats: MARS-seq (UMI, plate-based). Cell count not pinned here — confirm on series page.

name: Cheng et al. 2021 — pan-cancer myeloid atlas (GSE154763)
description: Pan-cancer single-cell transcriptional atlas of tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells across multiple cancer types, defining conserved macrophage/DC/monocyte states (incl. LAMP3+ DC, SPP1+/C1QC+ TAMs) relevant to antigen presentation.
scale: ~389k myeloid cells across 15+ cancer types

relevance.why: Myeloid/DC states are the professional antigen-presenting compartment — directly relevant to the presentation program across cancers.

agent_access: GEO normalized-expression CSVs via FTP; a Zenodo-derived h5 count matrix also exists. Raw data under GSA may be controlled — check. Automatable for processed data.
caveats: Processed matrices open on GEO; some raw data may sit in GSA (China) with its own access. Large; harmonize with other Zhang-lab pan-cancer atlases (T/NK/B/myeloid share design).

name: Wu et al. 2021 — breast cancer single-cell + spatial atlas (GSE176078)
description: Single-cell (10x) atlas of 26 primary breast tumors (ER+/HER2+/TNBC) with ~100k cells, plus companion spatial (Visium) data, defining gene modules and recurrent malignant/ stromal/immune states. Processed scRNA on GEO; raw reads controlled on EGA.
scale: ~99,876 cells, 26 primary tumors (10x 3' v2)
license: GEO terms (processed); EGA DAA for raw (controlled)

relevance.why: Deep breast-cancer single-cell+spatial reference across subtypes; strong for malignant and TME program discovery.

agent_access: Processed scRNA via GEO FTP; also on Broad SCP (SCP1039), CELLxGENE, and Zenodo (spatial, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4739739). Raw sequence reads require EGA DAC approval (EGAS00001005173) — not auto-ingestible.
caveats: Three deposits (GEO processed / EGA raw / Zenodo spatial) — pick the layer you need. Raw is controlled.

name: Tang et al. 2023 — pan-cancer NK-cell atlas (GSE212890)
description: Pan-cancer single-cell panorama of human natural killer cells across cancer types, defining conserved NK subsets and tumor-associated NK states. Part of the Zhang-lab pan-cancer immune atlas series.
scale: NK cells across many cancer types (pan-cancer)

relevance.why: NK compartment reference complementing T/myeloid/B pan-cancer atlases for full innate+adaptive immune baselines.

agent_access: GEO matrices via FTP. Some raw may be in GSA — check. Automatable for processed.
caveats: Accession from Zhang-lab atlas series; confirm tissue/cell counts on series page. Raw-data location may differ from processed.

name: GSE218355 — Canine Peripheral Blood TCRab T-cell Atlas (+ MAIT-like)
description: Combined scRNA + V(D)J atlas of peripheral-blood TCRab T cells from healthy dogs; first evidence of canine MAIT-like cells plus innate-effector and iNKT-like FCER1G+ CD8A+ populations (~19,796 T cells).
scale: ~19,796 T cells (healthy dogs)

relevance.why: Paired transcriptome + repertoire of canine T cells; MAIT/iNKT identification informs the canine recognition landscape.

agent_access: GEO FASTQ + processed; no auth.
caveats: Healthy blood only; no antigen-specific pairing.

name: GSE225599 — Canine Circulating Leukocyte scRNA Atlas (healthy + OSA)
description: scRNA-seq atlas of circulating leukocytes from 7 healthy and 10 osteosarcoma dogs; 36 cell populations with fine CD4 T-cell resolution. Processed data on UCSC Cell Browser (canine-leukocyte-atlas).
scale: 17 dogs; 36 populations

relevance.why: Reference for annotating canine immune infiltrates and deconvolving bulk RNA-seq.

agent_access: GEO FASTQ + UCSC Cell Browser; no auth.
caveats: Blood (not tumor) leukocytes; no antigen specificity.

name: Ma et al. 2024 — pan-cancer B-cell atlas (GSE233236)
description: Pan-cancer single-cell dissection of B-cell subtypes across cancers, defining phenotypically distinct B/plasma states and their tumor associations. Completes the Zhang-lab pan-cancer immune atlas quartet (T/myeloid/NK/B).
scale: B cells across many cancer types (pan-cancer)

relevance.why: B/plasma reference; relevant to tertiary lymphoid structures and humoral components of antitumor immunity.

agent_access: GEO matrices via FTP. Raw may be in GSA — check. Automatable for processed.
caveats: Accession from Zhang-lab series; verify counts on series page. Raw-data location may differ.

name: GSE252470 — Canine Osteosarcoma scRNA-seq (treatment-naive)
description: Single-cell RNA-seq reference of treatment-naive primary canine osteosarcoma (tumor + immune/stromal compartments), ~6 dogs; interactive cell browser; Zenodo code/processed-data companion.
scale: ~6 dogs; tens of thousands of cells

relevance.why: Resolves TILs/myeloid in dog OSA; single-cell substrate for recognition landscape.

agent_access: GEO + Zenodo bulk; no auth.
caveats: Small donor n; no paired VDJ.

name: Tirosh et al. 2016 — melanoma scRNA-seq (GSE72056)
description: Smart-seq2 single-cell RNA-seq of ~4,645 malignant, immune and stromal cells from 19 melanoma tumors; a foundational tumor scRNA-seq dataset with per-cell malignant/immune flags. One of the first to resolve malignant vs. microenvironment programs at single-cell resolution.
scale: ~4,645 cells, 19 melanoma patients (Smart-seq2)
license: GEO terms (submitter; no redistribution restriction stated)

relevance.why: Benchmark melanoma reference for malignant-vs-immune deconvolution and for testing presentation-machinery expression in tumor cells.

agent_access: Processed TPM matrix as a single GEO supplementary .txt (fetch via GEO FTP by accession). Metadata via Entrez E-utilities. Fully automatable, no auth.
caveats: Small by modern standards; Smart-seq2 (full-length, not UMI). Known gene-symbol/format quirks in the matrix (header rows for malignant/immune flags) — handle on ingest.

name: GTEx single-nucleus cross-tissue atlas (snRNA-seq)
description: Single-nucleus RNA-seq reference maps across multiple frozen GTEx tissues, linking cell-type composition to GTEx bulk expression and genetic regulation. Bridges GTEx bulk baselines to cell-type resolution in the same donor framework.
scale: 209,126 snRNA-seq profiles, 8 tissue types, 16 donors (25 samples)

provenance.maintainer: GTEx Consortium (Broad Institute; Regev/Aguet et al.)

relevance.why: Adds cell-type resolution to the GTEx normal baseline in the same donor/tissue framework, helping localize normal expression of a candidate target to specific cell types.

agent_access: Download .h5ad/loom from the GTEx portal and Broad Single Cell Portal (SCP1479); no auth for open files. A confirmed standalone GEO GSE was not located — use the portal downloads as the authoritative source.
caveats: Only 8 tissues / 16 donors (not whole-body). Frozen-nuclei (nuclear transcriptome) differs from whole-cell. Portal terms, not a CC license.

name: Gut Cell Atlas (Cells of the human intestinal tract)
description: Single-cell atlas of the human intestinal tract across space (regions) and developmental time, integrating fetal, pediatric and adult samples. Reference normal gastrointestinal cellular baseline.
scale: ~428,000 cells across intestinal regions and ages

relevance.why: GI epithelium is a frequent on-target/off-tumor toxicity site; normal intestinal cell-type expression helps assess target safety.

agent_access: Processed .h5ad from gutcellatlas.org and CELLxGENE (no auth); raw via ArrayExpress/BioStudies (E-MTAB-9543, E-MTAB-9536) over FTP.
caveats: Mixes developmental stages — filter to adult for a "self" reference. Processed objects easiest.

name: Heart Cell Atlas (Cells of the adult human heart)
description: Single-cell/single-nucleus atlas of the healthy adult human heart across six anatomical regions, with cell-type and spatial (Visium) data. Reference normal cardiac cellular baseline.
scale: ~486,000 cells, 6 cardiac regions, 14 donors

relevance.why: Heart is a critical off-tumor toxicity organ (cardiotoxicity); a normal cardiac cell-type reference flags targets expressed in cardiomyocytes/vasculature.

agent_access: Processed .h5ad open via heartcellatlas.org and CELLxGENE (no auth). Raw sequence via the HCA Data Coordination Platform under ERP123138.
caveats: Processed objects open; raw reads via HCA DCP (ERP123138). Confirm per-dataset license on CELLxGENE.

name: Human Lung Cell Atlas (HLCA, integrated)
description: Integrated single-cell reference of the human respiratory system combining 49 datasets, with a healthy "core" atlas and an extended health-and-disease atlas, harmonized cell types. The reference normal lung cellular baseline.
scale: ~2.4M cells, 486 individuals (full); core = 584,944 normal cells

provenance.maintainer: Human Cell Atlas Lung Biological Network (Theis/Teichmann et al.)

relevance.why: Lung is a common on-target/off-tumor toxicity site; a deep normal lung cell-type reference helps flag targets expressed in vulnerable respiratory epithelium/endothelium.

agent_access: .h5ad download from CZ CELLxGENE; programmatic via CELLxGENE Census. No auth. Use "core" (normal-only) subset for a clean self reference.
caveats: Full atlas mixes health + disease — select the normal core. Integrated embedding is batch-corrected; raw per-study counts also provided. Confirm CELLxGENE per-dataset license.

name: Human Cell Landscape (HCL)
description: Microwell-seq single-cell atlas covering adult and fetal human tissues and some cultured cell types, one of the first whole-body human single-cell references. Broad tissue coverage for normal cell-type expression.
scale: ~700,000 single cells; ~60 tissue types + cultured cells (adult + fetal)

relevance.why: Very broad (incl. many tissues not in Western atlases) normal cell-type reference; useful cross-check for target expression in cell types underrepresented elsewhere.

agent_access: Processed matrices from the HCL portal and GEO (GSE134355); raw sequence via CNGB (CNP0000325). HTTPS/FTP, no auth for open records.
caveats: No explicit data license found — cite the paper and verify terms before redistribution. Microwell-seq depth differs from 10x; mixes adult + fetal (filter for adult "self").

name: Jackson et al. 2020 — Single-cell pathology landscape of breast cancer (IMC)
description: Imaging mass cytometry (IMC) of breast cancer with a 35-marker antibody panel. 720 high-dimensional images from 352 patients (long-term survival data for 281), deposited as high-dimensional TIFFs, tumor/stroma and single-cell masks, plus single-cell and patient-level metadata. Defines recurrent single-cell phenotypes and spatial communities linked to clinical outcome.
scale: 720 IMC images, 352 patients, 35-marker panel, ~1.2M single cells

relevance.why: Large spatial-proteomic map of breast tumor cell phenotypes and their neighborhoods; a benchmark for relating immune infiltration structure to tumor biology at scale.

agent_access: Zenodo bulk download, no auth. Multi-GB TIFF archives plus compact single-cell CSVs. Companion processing code (ImcSegmentationPipeline) on GitHub.
caveats: Protein panel only (35 markers). Full image archive is large; single-cell tables are the practical layer for ML. Patient outcome subset (n=281) smaller than imaged cohort.

name: Ji et al. 2020 — Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (scRNA + spatial ST)
description: Multimodal single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics (ST/Visium-style) of human cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and matched normal skin, defining a tumor-specific keratinocyte state and spatially mapping tumor-immune niches at the leading edge.
scale: cSCC + matched normal; scRNA-seq + spatial transcriptomics sections

relevance.why: Spatially resolved tumor-immune boundary in an immunogenic skin cancer; informs how presentation and immune access vary across tumor architecture.

agent_access: GEO open download; superseries GSE144240 contains scRNA + ST subseries (incl. GSE144239). No auth; HTTPS/FTP.
caveats: Superseries layout: confirm which subseries holds the spatial vs scRNA layer. Paper had a 2020 figure correction (did not affect conclusions).

name: Keren et al. 2018 — Triple-negative breast cancer MIBI-TOF atlas
description: Multiplexed ion beam imaging by time-of-flight (MIBI-TOF) of triple-negative breast cancer: 36 labeled antibodies across 41 patients, revealing structured vs mixed tumor-immune architectures with prognostic value. Portal provides channel images, segmentation masks, and cell identities; patient metadata in the paper's supplement.
scale: ~1,763 images, 41 TNBC patients, 36-marker panel

relevance.why: Early, widely-reused spatial-proteomic benchmark for tumor-immune spatial organization; defines "structured" vs "mixed" immune architectures relevant to how T cells access tumor antigen in situ.

agent_access: Web portal with registration/login to browse and download; not a plain bulk HTTPS endpoint. Intermediate processed outputs mirrored on the authors' GitHub.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — explicit reuse/redistribution license not stated on the IonPath portal; treat terms as unknown and confirm before redistribution or ML training. Protein panel only; portal access may require account.

name: Krieg et al. 2018 — Anti-PD-1 response prediction in melanoma (CyTOF)
description: High-dimensional mass cytometry of peripheral blood from stage-IV melanoma patients before and during anti-PD-1 immunotherapy (plus healthy controls), identifying a baseline CD14+CD16-HLA-DRhi classical-monocyte frequency that predicts response and survival. Raw .fcs files in FlowRepository.
scale: ~40 patient blood samples pre/on anti-PD-1 + 10 controls, CyTOF panel

relevance.why: Links circulating high-parameter immune phenotypes to ICB outcome; a labeled responder/non-responder cytometry cohort for immune-correlate modeling.

agent_access: FlowRepository download; browsing/download typically needs a free account. A second deposit FR-FCM-ZYL8 is also associated (per Bioconductor HDCytoData).
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — FlowRepository deposits rarely carry an explicit reuse license; confirm terms. Peripheral blood (not intratumoral). Small cohort.

name: Krishna et al. 2021 — Multiregional ccRCC single-cell + TCR immune landscape
description: Paired single-cell RNA-seq and TCR-seq of clear cell renal cell carcinoma across tumor regions, tumor-normal interface, lymph node, normal kidney, and blood (including ICB-treated patients), linking tissue-resident/exhausted CD8 T-cell states and TCR clonality to tumor topology and therapy efficacy. ~167k cells.
scale: ~167,283 cells, multiregional ccRCC incl. 4 ICB-treated; paired scRNA + TCR
license: custom (CZ CELLxGENE processed; SRA raw public)

provenance.maintainer: Chan Lab (MSKCC) / SRA PRJNA705464; processed on CZ CELLxGENE Discover

relevance.why: Joint single-cell transcriptome + TCR in a checkpoint-responsive tumor; directly couples T-cell recognition (clonotypes) to functional states and spatial topology.

agent_access: Processed object downloadable from CZ CELLxGENE Discover (h5ad/RDS), no auth. Raw reads via SRA PRJNA705464 (open) — large FASTQ. Some secondary sources cite GSE121638 (unverified).
caveats: Confirm the raw accession (PRJNA705464 verified via SRA/CELLxGENE; GSE121638 citation is unconfirmed). Paired-TCR layer requires VDJ-aware parsing.

name: Lavin et al. 2017 — Innate immune landscape of early lung adenocarcinoma
description: Paired single-cell analyses (mass cytometry + MARS-seq scRNA-seq) of early-stage lung adenocarcinoma, tumor-adjacent normal lung, and blood, mapping tumor-remodeled innate/myeloid immune states very early in disease. scRNA-seq in GEO; CyTOF via the paper's data-availability section.
scale: Stage IA lung adenocarcinoma + adjacent + blood; CyTOF + MARS-seq scRNA
license: NCBI GEO terms (public domain-like, no explicit SPDX)

provenance.maintainer: Merad Lab (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai) / NCBI GEO

relevance.why: Multi-modal early-tumor immune map; myeloid/innate remodeling context that shapes the antigen-presenting milieu before adaptive responses dominate.

agent_access: GEO (GSE97168) open bulk download via FTP/HTTPS, no auth. CyTOF .fcs availability is stated in the paper; confirm deposit location for the cytometry layer.
caveats: GEO holds the scRNA layer cleanly; cytometry deposit path less explicit. Small patient numbers (early-stage discovery cohort).

name: Lowery et al. 2022 neoantigen-reactive TCR (NeoTCR) signatures
description: Molecular/transcriptomic signatures and sequences of neoantigen-specific TCR clonotypes isolated from metastatic human tumors, enabling prospective identification of neoTCRs.
scale: 55 neoantigen-specific TCR clonotypes mapped across 10 metastatic tumors

provenance.maintainer: Rosenberg lab, NCI Surgery Branch (Lowery et al.)

relevance.why: Directly defines what tumor-neoantigen-reactive TCRs look like transcriptionally — a template for recognition/design targeting private neoepitopes.

agent_access: NeoTCR sequences in supplementary materials; raw single-cell data under controlled access (dbGaP likely). Confirm accession in the Science data-and-materials-availability section.
caveats: Accession not confirmed in search — verify; raw data likely controlled. Small, high-value curated set. Human only.

name: Minervina et al. 2022 SARS-CoV-2 epitope-specific memory CD8 10x dataset
description: Aggregated CellRanger output from six 10x 5'GEX + paired abTCR + Feature-barcoding (dextramer) experiments profiling SARS-CoV-2 epitope-specific memory CD8 T cells across exposure histories.
scale: >4,000 epitope-specific paired TCRs; 6 10x experiments

provenance.maintainer: Thomas lab (St. Jude Children's Research Hospital)

relevance.why: High-quality paired-chain, dextramer-validated epitope-specific TCRs with phenotype — strong positives for recognition training/benchmarks.

agent_access: Single 224 MB zip on Zenodo, no auth; direct URL download. Processing scripts on linked GitHub.
caveats: CellRanger output needs parsing to extract clean TCR-epitope pairs. SARS-CoV-2 epitope-focused. No dog.

name: Nirmal et al. 2022 — Spatial landscape of primary melanoma (CyCIF, HTAN)
description: Tissue-cyclic-immunofluorescence (t-CyCIF) whole-slide multiplexed imaging of primary melanoma spanning precursor to invasive regions at single-cell resolution, mapping progression and immunoediting. Part of the Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN); releases whole-slide OME-TIFF images (~2.3 TB) with single-cell quantification tables.
scale: ~2.3 TB imaging, ~3.0e5 image tiles, single-cell CyCIF quantification

relevance.why: High-plex spatial map of how the immune compartment edits melanoma as it progresses; direct in-situ view of immune-tumor interfaces for recognition/presentation modeling.

agent_access: HTAN data via Synapse requires a (free) Synapse account and acceptance of HTAN terms; programmatic access via synapseclient. Whole-slide OME-TIFFs are very large.
caveats: Image volume is multi-TB — plan for the single-cell quantification layer, not raw images, for most ML. HTAN governance/registration applies.

name: Oliveira et al. 2021 melanoma antitumor CD8 TCR specificity/avidity
description: Single-cell linkage of TCR antigenic specificity (neoantigen/tumor) with phenotype and functional avidity in melanoma-infiltrating lymphocytes.
scale: melanoma TIL cohort; neoantigen- and tumor-reactive TCRs at single-cell resolution

relevance.why: Rare link of neoantigen specificity to avidity/phenotype — directly on-target for designing and ranking tumor-reactive TCRs.

agent_access: Neoantigen-reactive TCR sequences in supplementary tables (downloadable); raw sequencing under controlled access (dbGaP/EGA). Confirm accession in the article data-availability section.
caveats: Raw data controlled-access; exact accession to verify. Curated TCRs are in supplements. Human only.

name: Pozniak et al. 2024 — Melanoma ICB single-cell + spatial (TCF4 GRN)
description: Single-cell RNA-seq (with spatial profiling) of treatment-naive and immune-checkpoint- blockade-treated melanoma, mapping the cellular architecture and a TCF4-dependent gene regulatory network associated with resistance to immunotherapy. Released as Seurat objects (RDS) with raw counts and responder/non-responder clinical metadata.
scale: Treatment-naive + ICB-treated melanoma; scRNA-seq + spatial, responder/NR metadata

provenance.maintainer: Bechter/Marine labs (KU Leuven) / KU Leuven Research Data Repository (RDR)

relevance.why: Paired treatment-naive vs on-ICB melanoma single-cell + spatial with outcome labels; a resistance-focused complement to the Sade-Feldman/Jerby-Arnon melanoma ICB cohorts.

agent_access: KU Leuven RDR open download (RDS/Seurat objects), no controlled access. DOI-resolvable.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 forbids commercial use and imposes share-alike; problematic for commercial model training. Data shipped as R/Seurat objects (not raw FASTQ).

name: PRJEB86016 — Canine Insulinoma Single-Cell RNA-seq (2025)
description: Single-cell RNA-seq of 5,532 cells from three Boxer canine insulinoma samples (two primary insulinomas and one metastasis), resolving distinct sub-populations of insulin-expressing cancer cells (2025). Deposited in ENA as study ERP169389 under project PRJEB86016 (samples ERS23781655-57).
scale: 5,532 cells, 3 samples, 2 dogs

relevance.why: Only known single-cell view of a canine endocrine tumour; adds a neuroendocrine lineage to the canine single-cell atlas collection.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (ENA/INSDC open). Small cohort (2 dogs). Raw reads only — processed objects not noted; expect to run the scRNA pipeline from FASTQ.

name: Qian et al. 2020 — pan-cancer TME blueprint (Lambrechts lab)
description: Single-cell blueprint of the heterogeneous tumor microenvironment across breast, colorectal, ovarian and lung cancers (~230k cells), with a stromal/immune cell-type classifier and an interactive download portal.
scale: ~233,000 cells across 4 cancer types

relevance.why: Cross-cancer stromal+immune classifier and reference for TME cell-type assignment.

agent_access: Download via the Lambrechts-lab blueprint web portal. ArrayExpress accessions are cited in the paper's Data Availability (e.g. lung subsets from the 2018 Lambrechts NSCLC study) but the specific pan-cancer accession was NOT verified in this pass — confirm in the paper before scripting. Portal download is the confirmed route.
caveats: Explicit data license not stated — treat as unknown, verify before redistribution. Accession not pinned here (portal-first); read the paper's Data Availability for ArrayExpress E-MTAB IDs.

name: Schürch et al. 2020 — Colorectal cancer CODEX multiplexed imaging atlas
description: Highly multiplexed CODEX (co-detection by indexing) fluorescence imaging of advanced-stage colorectal carcinoma. 140 tissue-microarray spots from 35 patients stained with a 56-protein panel, segmented to single cells with spatial coordinates, enabling cellular-neighborhood analysis of the tumor-immune microenvironment. Includes raw multichannel images, segmentation masks, and single-cell feature tables.
scale: 140 CODEX images, 35 CRC patients, 56-protein panel, ~240k annotated cells

provenance.maintainer: Nolan Lab (Stanford) / hosted on The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA)

relevance.why: Spatially resolved tumor-immune niches at single-cell resolution give ground truth for where antigen-presenting and effector cells co-localize in a human solid tumor, informing models of in-situ immune recognition and presentation context.

agent_access: Bulk download from TCIA via DOI; no auth for the imaging collection. Large TIFF files; processed single-cell CSVs also mirrored on Mendeley Data. Scriptable over HTTPS.
caveats: Imaging is TMA-based (spots, not whole sections). Processed single-cell intensities/ coordinates are the most agent-friendly layer; raw images are multi-GB. Panel is protein markers, not transcriptome.

name: Stephenson et al. 2021 COVID-19 single-cell multi-omics atlas (E-MTAB-10026)
description: Single-cell transcriptome + surface proteome + paired TCR/BCR V(D)J of >780,000 PBMCs from 130 COVID-19 patients and controls; a very large paired scTCR immune-profiling release.
scale: >780,000 PBMCs; 130 patients (E-MTAB-10026)

relevance.why: Large paired scTCR/BCR immune-profiling cohort for background modeling, V/J priors and disease repertoire context.

agent_access: Processed data (incl. h5ad) open via ArrayExpress E-MTAB-10026 and covid19cellatlas.org portal; programmatically downloadable. VDJ tables bundled in the objects/portal.
caveats: Not antigen-labeled. Confirm VDJ-specific files within E-MTAB-10026 / portal. Human only.

name: STOmicsDB — Spatial Transcript Omics DataBase
description: Comprehensive aggregator database for spatial transcriptomics: a one-stop hub to search, visualize, archive, and analyze spatial datasets across many species and platforms (including numerous tumor spatial datasets). Hosts hundreds of curated spatial datasets with harmonized metadata and online analysis/visualization.
scale: ~400+ curated spatial transcriptomics datasets, 12+ species (growing)

relevance.why: Discovery/index layer to locate tumor spatial-transcriptomics datasets across platforms — useful for finding additional primary tumor atlases to catalog.

agent_access: Web portal with browse/search and dataset download; some datasets visualize in-browser. Not a single bulk endpoint — per-dataset access varies.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — licenses vary per contributed dataset; not uniformly open. It is an aggregator/index, not a single primary dataset — individual tumor datasets must be de-duplicated against GEO/other sources before cataloging.

name: Tabula Sapiens 2.0
description: Expanded, comprehensive transcriptomic atlas of human cell types extending Tabula Sapiens with many more cells, donors, and tissues and refined cell-type definitions. Current best single-donor-resolved pan-body normal reference from this consortium.
scale: Millions of cells across expanded tissue/donor panel (see paper)

provenance.maintainer: Chan Zuckerberg Biohub / Tabula Sapiens Consortium

relevance.why: Deeper, broader normal cell-type reference than v1 — the preferred pan-body self map for cell-type-level expression filtering of candidate targets.

agent_access: .h5ad via figshare/AWS Open Data; CZ CELLxGENE Census API for programmatic slicing. No auth.
caveats: Confirm the exact Cell DOI and final cell/donor counts against the published article (2026). Supersedes much of v1 — prefer for new work but note version in provenance.

name: 10x Genomics Xenium — Human breast cancer in-situ (public demo datasets)
description: Public 10x Genomics Xenium in-situ single-cell spatial transcriptomics datasets on human breast cancer FFPE tissue, including the Janesick et al. preprint data (Chromium + Visium + two Xenium replicates on consecutive sections) and newer Xenium Prime 5K pan-tissue + custom panels. Outputs include cell-feature matrices, transcript tables, cell boundaries, and registered H&E images.
scale: Breast cancer FFPE; ~hundreds of genes (base) to 5,000+ (Prime 5K) panels

provenance.maintainer: 10x Genomics (dataset program) / Zenodo mirror for preprint data

relevance.why: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics of a tumor with matched Chromium/Visium; a clean, openly-licensed benchmark for integrating single-cell and in-situ tumor data.

agent_access: Zenodo preprint bundle (~7.6 GB) open HTTPS download, CC BY 4.0. 10x dataset pages provide additional bundles with md5 checksums (CC BY 4.0); some newer sets need a form.
caveats: Preprint Zenodo bundle is a legacy pre-release (file/QC naming and image alignment differ from current outputs). Newer 10x demo datasets may require an email form.

name: TISCH2 — Tumor Immune Single-cell Hub 2
description: Curated, uniformly reprocessed collection of tumor single-cell RNA-seq datasets with a consistent immune-cell-type annotation layer across the tumor microenvironment. Supports gene-level visualization, per-dataset expression matrices, differential expression, transcription-factor and cell-cell interaction results. Built to compare immune cell states across cancer types rather than host primary raw data.
scale: ~6.3M cells, 190 datasets, 50 cancer types, 20 tissues

provenance.maintainer: Wang Lab, Tongji University / Shirley Liu Lab (originated)

relevance.why: A ready-made, harmonized pan-cancer immune single-cell reference for defining tumor T-cell/myeloid states and for benchmarking expression of presentation and recognition machinery across cancer types without reprocessing raw data.

agent_access: Per-dataset bulk downloads (expression matrices, metadata, DE tables) over HTTP, no auth. No documented REST API; ingestion is by scripted per-dataset file fetch. Landing returned a transient HTTP 503 at check time (2026-11-15) — retry; URL is the one cited in the NAR 2023 paper.
caveats: License is non-commercial (CC BY-NC 4.0) — flag for any commercial/for-profit use and clarify before building a product on it. Secondary resource: cells are reprocessed, so re-derive raw where provenance matters. No stable programmatic API.

name: Vizgen MERSCOPE — Human FFPE Immuno-oncology MERFISH data release
description: Vizgen MERSCOPE (MERFISH) in-situ spatial transcriptomics across multiple human FFPE tumor types including melanoma, lung, ovarian, colon, liver, prostate, breast, and uterine cancer. Measures ~500-gene panels (newer panels up to ~815/1,000 genes), releasing cell-by-gene matrices, per-transcript coordinates, and cell boundaries.
scale: ~16-26 tumor samples, 8+ cancer types, ~4-6B transcripts, ~9-10M cells

relevance.why: Multi-tumor-type MERFISH gives in-situ transcriptomic maps of tumor-immune spatial organization across cancers, complementing the Xenium/Visium entries.

agent_access: Download via Vizgen's Data Release Program page; participation/registration required. Not a plain anonymous bulk endpoint.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — vendor Data Release Program terms, not a standard open license; confirm redistribution/ML-training allowance. Gene-count figures differ across Vizgen pages (panel versions). Access is registration-gated.

name: Wagner et al. 2019 — Single-cell atlas of human breast cancer ecosystem (CyTOF)
description: Mass cytometry (CyTOF) atlas of the tumor and immune ecosystem of human breast cancer using tumor and immune antibody panels. Profiles ~26 million cells from 144 tumors, 46 juxta-tumoral samples, and four reduction mammoplasties, defining immune/stromal/tumor phenotype abundances across subtypes. Deposited as raw .fcs files plus IF images.
scale: ~26M cells, 144 tumors + 46 juxta-tumoral + 4 mammoplasties, two CyTOF panels

provenance.maintainer: Bodenmiller Lab (University of Zurich) / Mendeley Data

relevance.why: One of the largest single-tumor-type CyTOF immune atlases; high-parameter protein phenotyping of tumor-infiltrating immune cells to anchor immune-composition priors.

agent_access: Mendeley Data bulk download, no auth. Native .fcs (flow/mass cytometry) files; parse with flowCore / readfcs. CC BY 4.0 per Mendeley record.
caveats: Protein marker panel (no transcriptome). .fcs requires cytometry-specific parsing and arcsinh transform. Large number of files.

name: Weizmann 3CA — Curated Cancer Cell Atlas
description: Expertly curated collection of published tumor single-cell datasets with harmonized cell-type annotations, malignant-cell programs, copy-number calls and cell-cycle/state layers, downloadable per study. Focus on consistent re-annotation of malignant and TME cells across many studies.
scale: ~40+ studies, millions of cells across cancer types (growing)
license: unknown (site has no explicit data license; paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)

provenance.maintainer: Tirosh Lab, Weizmann Institute of Science

relevance.why: High-quality, consistently re-annotated malignant + TME single-cell data; a strong curated backbone for comparative tumor-immune analysis and program discovery.

agent_access: Per-study "download" links over HTTP, no auth; files are matrices + annotation tables. No REST API; scripted per-study fetch. Code at github.com/tiroshlab/3ca.
caveats: No explicit license on the download pages — associated paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial, no derivatives), which is restrictive; treat data license as unknown and confirm with the lab before redistribution/ML training. One dataset is EGA-only (controlled), not on the site.

name: Wu et al. 2020 peripheral/tumor T cell expansion scTCR (GSE139555)
description: Paired scRNA-seq + scTCR-seq of tumor, normal-adjacent tissue and blood across several cancer indications, characterizing clonotypic effector expansion linking periphery to tumor.
scale: multiple cancer indications; thousands of clonotypes (GSE139555)

relevance.why: Paired tumor/periphery scTCR with clonal tracking — directly relevant to tumor-reactive TCR identification and repertoire context.

agent_access: Open GEO series GSE139555 (matrices via FTP/HTTPS); a matched EGA set (EGAS00001003993) holds controlled raw data. GEO portion programmatically downloadable.
caveats: Not antigen-labeled. Raw reads partly on EGA (controlled). Human only.

name: Yost et al. 2019 BCC/SCC anti-PD-1 scTCR (GSE123813)
description: Paired 5' scRNA- and scTCR-seq from site-matched basal/squamous cell carcinoma tumors before and after anti-PD-1, demonstrating clonal replacement of tumor-specific T cells.
scale: 11 BCC patients (pre/post anti-PD-1); paired scRNA+scTCR (GSE123813)

relevance.why: Classic checkpoint-response tumor scTCR dataset; useful for tumor-reactive clonotype dynamics and as a recognition-context cohort.

agent_access: Open GEO series GSE123813 (bulk companion GSE123812); matrices via GEO FTP/HTTPS, automatable.
caveats: Not antigen-labeled. Small patient count. Human only.

name: Zenodo 10891255 — Canine OSA scRNA Reference (code + processed data)
description: Processed Seurat objects + analysis code for the canine osteosarcoma scRNA reference (companion to GSE252470).
scale: processed objects + scripts

relevance.why: Ready-to-use processed canine OSA single-cell objects.

agent_access: Zenodo direct download + REST API; no auth.
caveats: Derived/processed only.

name: Zheng et al. 2021 pan-cancer tumor-infiltrating T cell atlas (scRNA + scTCR)
description: Pan-cancer single-cell atlas of tumor-infiltrating T cells combining gene expression with paired TCR sequences across 21 cancer types; a very large tumor-context scTCR resource (new + pooled published data).
scale: 316 patients, 21 cancer types; ~397k T cells (meta-cohort larger)

relevance.why: The largest tumor-infiltrating paired scTCR atlas — essential tumor-context repertoire data for recognition and for clonal-expansion phenotyping.

agent_access: Processed data via lab portal (cancer-pku.cn); raw sequencing is under China GSA/HRA controlled access (data access agreement). Confirm exact accession (HRA/GSA) in the Science data-availability section before use.
caveats: Raw data controlled-access (GSA/HRA); exact accession to verify. Not antigen-labeled (tumor reactivity inferred). Human only.

name: ABodyBuilder2 predicted antibody structures + ImmuneBuilder weights
description: ImmuneBuilder (ABodyBuilder2/NanoBodyBuilder2/TCRBuilder2) data release: predicted structural models for a large set of paired antibody sequences from the Observed Antibody Space, bundled with all ImmuneBuilder model weights. Antibody-binder precedent for the pMHC design program.
scale: ~148k ABodyBuilder2 models of paired antibody sequences (from OAS) + ImmuneBuilder weights

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), University of Oxford

relevance.why: Open antibody/nanobody structure predictor + weights, the binder-design precedent most transferable to engineering antibody-like binders against peptide-MHC.

agent_access: Open Zenodo download (10.5281/zenodo.7258553); pip-installable code with bundled weights. Fully scriptable.
caveats: Models are predictions, not experiments. Antibody-centric (TCR via sibling TCRBuilder2). Attribution required (CC BY 4.0).

name: AFDB/Foldseek structural clusters (AFDB50/AFDBclusters)
description: Structural clustering of the entire AlphaFold DB with Foldseek, collapsing ~214M models into ~2.3M non-singleton structural clusters with representatives. Provides a non-redundant, structure-defined view of the predicted universe — ideal for building de-duplicated training sets and sampling diverse folds.
scale: ~2.3M clusters from ~214M AFDB models; ~2.27M cluster representatives

provenance.maintainer: Steinegger & van Kempen (Seoul National Univ. / groups)

relevance.why: Non-redundant structural representatives let you train/evaluate without drowning in near-duplicate AFDB models and enable balanced sampling across the fold space — key for representation learning.

agent_access: Downloadable cluster membership tables, representative sets and Foldseek databases over HTTPS; no auth. Agent-mirrorable.
caveats: Derived from AFDB predictions (same prediction caveats). Confirm current download mirror URLs. Inherits AFDB CC BY 4.0 terms.

name: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (AFDB)
description: DeepMind/EMBL-EBI database of AlphaFold2-predicted 3D structures covering essentially the whole of UniProt. Each model carries per-residue pLDDT confidence and PAE. The largest openly licensed predicted sequence->structure corpus with explicit commercial-use permission; widely used for distillation and structure-aware pretraining.
scale: >214M predicted structures (as of Sept 2023); redesigned interface/coverage in 2025
last_updated: 2025 (interface/coverage update); UniProt sync lagged for a period

relevance.why: Massive, commercially usable predicted-structure corpus for pretraining, distillation and augmenting experimental data; pLDDT/PAE enable confidence- weighted training. Directly ML-training-friendly by license.

agent_access: Bulk: Google Cloud public bucket (gs://public-datasets-deepmind-alphafold-v4) for the full set (~23 TB); EBI FTP (ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/alphafold) and per-organism + Swiss-Prot archives; REST API for single entries. No auth. Fully agent-downloadable; use gsutil/aws for the complete corpus.
caveats: Models are predictions, not experiments; low-pLDDT and disordered regions are unreliable. CC BY requires attribution; EMBL-EBI Terms of Use also apply. Heavy redundancy — cluster before training (see AFDB Foldseek clusters).

name: ATLAS (protein molecular-dynamics database)
description: Standardized all-atom MD of representative protein structures (3 x 100 ns replicas per chain) with precomputed analyses — RMSF, flexibility, secondary-structure dynamics, contacts. Covers a broad, non-redundant set of PDB chains plus curated subsets (Chameleon fold-switchers, DPF). NOT the TCR–pMHC affinity "ATLAS" in domain-6.
scale: 1,938 main ATLAS structures (+16 Chameleon, +100 DPF); 3 x 100 ns each

provenance.maintainer: DSIMB, INSERM / Université Paris Cité (Galochkina, Gelly et al.)

relevance.why: Broad, uniform MD coverage of diverse folds with ready-made flexibility metrics — strong supervision for sequence-to-dynamics/ensemble and B-factor/flexibility prediction.

agent_access: Bulk download script (download_ATLAS.py) and a /api/parsable REST endpoint; per- entry XTC+PDB+analysis bundles. No auth. Fully automatable.
caveats: CC BY-NC 4.0 — NON-COMMERCIAL. A computational-oncology company must treat this as restricted for commercial model training/redistribution; use for evaluation or seek a license. 3 x 100 ns is modest sampling for slow motions.

name: ATLAS (Altered TCR Ligand Affinities and Structures)
description: Manually curated database linking experimental binding affinities (and some kinetics) to 3D structures for wild-type and mutant TCR-pMHC complexes. Where a mutant has no crystal structure, a modeled structure is provided. The canonical affinity+structure resource for TCR-pMHC interactions.
scale: ~253 affinity values paired with TCR-pMHC complex structures (growing; original 2017 release + post-2017 literature)

relevance.why: Direct structure-to-affinity labels for TCR-pMHC, including mutational effects — essential for training/benchmarking affinity predictors and for validating peptide-MHC binder design against measured Kd.

agent_access: Data and build scripts on GitHub (weng-lab/ATLAS, piercelab fork); affinities also exposed through TCR3d. Clone the repo for programmatic access.
caveats: No explicit repository license found (marked unknown) — check before reuse. Small, manually curated set; mixes experimental and modeled mutant structures (flag the modeled ones). Overlaps TCR3d.

name: BFVD (Big Fantastic Virus Database)
description: Repository of ColabFold-predicted structures for viral protein sequence representatives of UniRef30 clusters — filling a gap (viral proteins are under-represented in AFDB). Complements general corpora with viral fold diversity; each model carries pLDDT.
scale: 351,242 predicted viral protein structures (median pLDDT 70.2)

relevance.why: Adds viral structural space absent from AFDB — useful for oncolytic-virus / viral-antigen modelling and for broadening fold coverage in pretraining.

agent_access: Zenodo tarball (bfvd.tar.gz ~9.1 GB) and Cloudflare mirror; Foldseek DB. No auth. Fully agent-downloadable.
caveats: Predicted structures (median medium confidence ~70 pLDDT); ~204k singletons. Verify current mirror. Viral-only scope.

name: Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank (BMRB)
description: The wwPDB NMR archive: assigned chemical shifts, coupling constants, relaxation data, residual dipolar couplings, restraints, and time-domain/raw NMR spectral data for proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, metabolites and other organics. NMR uniquely captures solution-state behavior and dynamics, not just a single static conformer.
scale: >14,000 entries with assigned shift data (archive >15,000 depositions); spectral peak lists and raw time-domain data for many entries
license: public domain (BMRB/wwPDB policy); some secondary sources cite CC BY 4.0 — see caveats

provenance.maintainer: UConn Health (prev. University of Wisconsin-Madison); NIGMS R24GM150793; wwPDB member; mirror BMRBj at PDBj

relevance.why: Chemical shifts and restraints encode local backbone/side-chain conformation and solution dynamics — directly useful for sequence-to-conformation and ensemble models, and for cross-checking predicted structures against experiment.

agent_access: Anonymous FTP/HTTPS bulk download of the full NMR-STAR archive; rsync and Globus endpoints for keeping a local mirror; REST API (api.bmrb.io) and CSV relational tables. PDBj BMRBj mirror serves NMR-STAR/XML/RDF/JSON over HTTP. Fully agent- downloadable.
caveats: License statements conflict: BMRB data are generally treated as public domain under wwPDB policy, but at least one book chapter cites CC BY 4.0 and Wikipedia lists "public domain." Treat as freely reusable but attribute. Raw time-domain (FID) data exist only for a subset. NMR-STAR requires parsing (PyNMRSTAR library).

name: CAPRI (Critical Assessment of PRedicted Interactions)
description: Community-wide blind assessment of protein-protein docking and complex structure prediction, run jointly with CASP for assembly rounds. Provides curated target complexes (incl. antibody-antigen and nanobody complexes) and score-set ensembles of submitted models for benchmarking docking/scoring.
scale: CASP15-CAPRI round = 37 targets (incl. 3 antibody-antigen); score-set benchmark ~15 published targets with large model ensembles

provenance.maintainer: CAPRI management (EBI/IGBMC and community), coordinated with CASP

relevance.why: Antibody-antigen and nanobody docking targets are the closest public blind benchmarks for interface prediction relevant to pMHC binder docking and scoring; score-sets give labeled good/bad models for scorer development.

agent_access: Targets and score-sets distributed via capri-docking.org / scoreset.org; manual/semi-automated download. No documented programmatic API.
caveats: Explicit reuse license not clearly posted (marked unknown). No pMHC-specific targets historically — antibody-antigen is the proxy. Some materials released only to registered participants during active rounds.

name: CASP (Critical Assessment of Structure Prediction) datasets
description: Biennial blind community experiment assessing protein (and complex/RNA) structure prediction. Releases target sequences, experimental reference structures, all participant predictions and numerical assessment results — the gold-standard held-out benchmark for sequence->structure methods.
scale: Per-round target + prediction archives (e.g. CASP15; CASP16 2024 ~300 targets across 5 categories)
license: custom (freely downloadable for research; cite Prediction Center)

provenance.maintainer: Protein Structure Prediction Center (UC Davis), NIGMS funded

last_updated: 2024 (CASP16); archives per round from CASP1 onward

relevance.why: Standardized targets with experimental references and large model ensembles provide a reusable accuracy benchmark for monomer/complex prediction methods feeding the structure-based design and recognition pipelines.

agent_access: Open download_area indexed by round and file type (targets, predictions, results) as tar.gz; directly fetchable/scriptable over HTTPS.
caveats: No single SPDX license — a research-use/citation convention; verify before redistribution. Targets are deliberately limited in number (benchmark, not a training corpus). Reference structures embargoed until each season ends.

name: CZ cryoET Data Portal
description: Open-access portal for cryo-electron tomography: tilt series, reconstructed tomograms, and dense expert/ML annotations (segmentations, particle picks) of cellular and in-situ structures. Built to accelerate ML-based annotation of cryo-ET, and interoperates with EMPIAR for raw-data hosting.
scale: 392 datasets, 60,512 tomograms, 179,902 annotations, 51 species (2026)

provenance.maintainer: Chan Zuckerberg Imaging Institute / CZ Biohub

relevance.why: In-situ 3D structure with annotations — training data for structure/particle identification in crowded cellular context, pushing sequence-and-context-to-3D beyond purified single particles.

agent_access: Dedicated Python client (pip install cryoet-data-portal) and GraphQL API over an S3 bucket; public, no account. napari plugin for inspection. Tomograms stored as multiscale Zarr/MRC — large but chunk-streamable, well-suited to scripted access.
caveats: Confirm license per dataset (portal applies CC BY 4.0 by default; contributors vary). Volumetric data are large; use the S3/Zarr chunked access rather than full downloads.

name: CycPeptMPDB (cyclic-peptide membrane-permeability database)
description: Database of cyclic peptides with measured membrane permeability and defined chemical structure (HELM notation, incl. non-natural residues and cyclization), compiled from 45 papers and 2 patents. The reference resource for cyclic-peptide chemistry and conformation–permeability relationships.
scale: 7,334 cyclic peptides with measured permeability
license: custom (free academic access) — no explicit SPDX license stated

provenance.maintainer: Li, Kihara et al. (Mitsubishi Tanabe / academic collaboration)

relevance.why: Cyclic/macrocyclic peptides are a prime therapeutic modality; this links peptide structure (incl. non-natural chemistry) to a measured developability property — training signal for cyclic-peptide structure/conformation and property models.

agent_access: Web download of structures + permeability tables; HELM strings give unambiguous structure. No auth. Scriptable; modest size.
caveats: No explicit CC/SPDX license; "freely accessed" by convention — confirm before commercial use. Permeability is the primary label; 3D conformers are derivable from HELM/structure but not all deposited as ensembles.

name: DBAASP (Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides)
description: Manually curated database of antimicrobial/cytotoxic peptides with sequence, chemical modifications, target-organism activity (MIC), and structural data — including >400 entries linked to experimental PDB structures and >3,200 peptides with computed MD models/trajectories viewable and downloadable in-browser.
scale: >15,700 entries (v3): ~14,500 monomers + ~400 multimers; >400 PDB-linked, >3,200 with MD models
license: open-access, free to use — no explicit SPDX/CC license stated (see caveats)

provenance.maintainer: Ivane Beritashvili Center / Pirtskhalava et al. (Georgia)

relevance.why: Pairs peptide sequence/chemistry with activity AND structure (PDB links + MD models) — directly on-domain for antimicrobial/therapeutic peptide design and for sequence-to-conformation learning on short peptides with non-natural residues.

agent_access: REST API with simple URL-addressable entries and query sets; per-entry PDB/MD downloads. No auth. Fully scriptable.
caveats: No explicit CC/SPDX license surfaced (site states free/open use) — confirm terms before redistribution/training. MD models are computed (not experimental) — treat as predicted conformers. Peptides include non-standard residues needing special parsing.

name: Electron Microscopy Data Bank (EMDB)
description: Public wwPDB repository for cryo-EM/cryo-ET 3D reconstructions: density maps, half-maps, additional maps and masks of macromolecular complexes and subcellular structures, plus representative tomograms. Each entry carries rich metadata (resolution, reconstruction method, symmetry, fitted-model cross-links to PDB). The processed-volume counterpart to EMPIAR's raw images.
scale: 64,332 entries (2026-11-11), growing fast with cryo-EM

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI, as part of wwPDB / EMDB-EMPIAR

relevance.why: Experimental 3D density for large and membrane/complex assemblies that crystallography misses. Maps + fitted models are training/validation signal for sequence-to-3D and complex-assembly models, complementing the PDB in domain-6.

agent_access: Fully anonymous FTP/HTTPS mirror (ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/emdb) is directly wget/rsync-able per entry; REST API at /emdb/api for metadata and search. No auth. Maps are large (tens of MB to several GB each) but individually scriptable.
caveats: wwPDB releases data to the public domain (CC0); the EBI general terms-of-use page governs the service. Maps alone are not atomic coordinates — pair with the fitted PDB model (cross-referenced in each entry) for sequence-to-structure supervision.

name: Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive (EMPIAR)
description: Public archive of the RAW image data underpinning cryo-EM maps and tomograms — motion-corrected/aligned movie frames, micrographs, tilt series and particle stacks — plus volume-EM and soft/hard X-ray tomography datasets. This is the "scan"-level resource: the primary detector output before reconstruction.
scale: 3,278 entries (2026-11-15); total archive 9.77 PiB; representative raw entries ~0.5–12 TB each (avg ~3 TB)

relevance.why: The only public source of raw cryo-EM/cryo-ET scans at scale — needed for any model that learns reconstruction, denoising, or image-to-3D, and for self- supervised pretraining on primary experimental data. The single largest raw-data resource in this domain.

agent_access: Anonymous download via Aspera (ascp), Globus, HTTPS/FTP and Python clients; per- entry directories under ftp.ebi.ac.uk/empiar. REST API for metadata. No auth, but entries are individually huge (multi-TB) — plan for Aspera/Globus, staging and bandwidth, not naive wget of the full archive (~9.8 PiB).
caveats: CC0, fully redistributable. Cost is scale, not license: downloading representative tomography/single-particle sets means terabytes per entry. Formats vary by microscope/detector (EER, TIFF, DM4, MRC). Needs substantial preprocessing to be ML-ready.

name: ESM Metagenomic Atlas (Meta/FAIR)
description: Meta AI's database of ESMFold-predicted structures for metagenomic proteins (MGnify-derived), expanding structural coverage into unexplored metagenomic sequence space far beyond UniProt. Each prediction carries pLDDT and pTM. One of the largest predicted sequence->structure corpora.
scale: ~617M structures (v0, 2022); ~772M total with the +150M 2023_02 update
license: CC BY 4.0 (also subject to Meta Open Source Terms)

relevance.why: Adds enormous structural diversity from metagenomic sequence space for pretraining/distillation beyond the UniProt-centric AFDB; embeddings and Foldseek DBs are directly usable for representation learning.

agent_access: Bulk tarballs of predicted structures plus Foldseek DBs and embeddings; recommended via s5cmd/aria2c. Metadata ~25 GB (SQLite/Parquet). Split by pLDDT/pTM so high-confidence subsets can be fetched. Also mirrored on AWS Open Data. No auth.
caveats: RED FLAG: hosting continuity uncertain — the original Meta-hosted endpoints (esmatlas.com / fbaipublicfiles) have had availability issues; the AWS Open Data mirror and the Biohub successor are more durable. Predictions, not experiments; many low-confidence models.

name: ESM Atlas (Biohub, ESMC/ESMFold2)
description: Large-scale public successor atlas of computational structure/feature outputs generated with ESMC and ESMFold2 over a deduplicated set of 6.8B+ public protein sequences, hosted on the AWS Registry of Open Data. Reported as ~1.1 billion predicted structures — the largest sequence->structure corpus found.
scale: ~1.1B predicted structures from ~6.8B deduplicated sequences (v1.0)

provenance.maintainer: Arc/Biohub (ESM lineage); hosted on AWS Open Data

relevance.why: Largest openly hosted predicted sequence->structure + features corpus; extreme scale and diversity for pretraining and distillation.

agent_access: AWS S3 Open Data bucket, downloadable with aws CLI --no-sign-request; no auth. Agent-downloadable at scale (expect multi-TB).
caveats: License not clearly stated in search results (AWS Open Data entries are usually open but verify the exact license on the registry page before ML/commercial use). Predictions, not experiments. Confirm exact counts against official docs.

name: Folding@home public datasets (incl. COVID Moonshot / SARS-CoV-2)
description: Openly released trajectory and free-energy datasets from the Folding@home distributed-computing project — notably the massive SARS-CoV-2 / COVID Moonshot simulations (Markov-state-model-scale adaptive sampling, absolute binding free energies, protein–ligand trajectories). Among the largest aggregate MD volumes ever released openly.
scale: Multi-TB to ~PB-scale aggregate trajectory data across releases (e.g. full SARS-CoV-2 proteome sampling + Moonshot FECs)
license: open data (AWS Open Data Program; CC-style open access) — verify per dataset

provenance.maintainer: Folding@home Consortium (Bowman, Chodera, Voelz labs et al.)

relevance.why: Enormous, equilibrium-and-enhanced-sampling MD plus rigorous free-energy data — high-value pretraining/benchmark signal for dynamics, kinetics (MSM) and binding models at a scale no single curated DB matches.

agent_access: Public S3 buckets via AWS CLI with --no-sign-request (no AWS account); index CSVs map RUNs to systems (MolSSI/BioExcel COVID Hub). Fully scriptable; just multi-TB per target, so stage selectively.
caveats: Multiple buckets with inconsistent naming across the AWS registry and GitHub YAML — verify bucket paths before scripting. Open-data access, but confirm the specific dataset's reuse terms. Preprocessing (framing, alignment) required.

name: GPCRmd
description: Community database of membrane molecular-dynamics simulations of G-protein-coupled receptors in realistic lipid bilayers, with a large analysis toolbox (contacts, allosteric networks, pockets, water, pharmacophores). Deep, target-focused MD for a major drug-target family.
scale: Thousands of trajectories across ~637 PDB structures, 50 GPCR families, 116 subtypes
license: custom / open academic — no explicit SPDX license stated (see caveats)

provenance.maintainer: GPCR Drug Discovery group, Barcelona (Selent lab) + consortium

relevance.why: Membrane-protein conformational dynamics at scale — the hardest class for static predictors. Useful for conformation/allostery modeling of integral-membrane targets relevant to immuno-oncology surface receptors.

agent_access: Per-simulation downloads via the DynaDB web interface; documented toolbox and scripts. No single documented bulk-tarball API — iterate over dynamics IDs. No auth.
caveats: No explicit CC/SPDX license surfaced; terms are open-academic by convention — confirm before commercial training/redistribution. Download is per-entry (web-driven), so automation needs ID enumeration.

name: HLA3DB (peptide/HLA class I structural database)
description: Auto-curated database of peptide/HLA class I complex structures with comprehensive annotation (peptide length, allele, backbone conformation classes), built to enable blind structure prediction of T-cell epitopes. A dedicated pMHC-I structural resource distinct from the general archives.
scale: ~605 PDB entries with an HLA structure, 61 alleles, 106 backbone classes (live); 393 non-redundant structures (15 octamer / 296 nonamer / 82 decamer) in the paper
license: unknown (associated modeling code on Zenodo; confirm DB terms on site)

provenance.maintainer: Sgourakis Lab, Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) / UPenn

relevance.why: The most focused public catalog of pMHC-I structures with backbone conformation classes — directly supports peptide-MHC binder design, template selection, and pMHC structure prediction benchmarking.

agent_access: Open web download of structure collections and statistics; modeling code archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.8372875). Coordinates derive from PDB.
caveats: Explicit DB data license not posted (marked unknown). pMHC-I only (no TCR, limited class II). Dedup against PDB/IMGT by PDB ID.

name: IEDB-3D (structural data within the Immune Epitope Database)
description: The structural component of IEDB: B- and T-cell epitopes and MHC ligands for which 3D structures of complexes with antibodies, TCRs or MHC molecules exist in the PDB, with computed intermolecular contacts, interface areas and an epitope-to-antigen-structure mapping (v2.0). Links immune epitopes to pMHC / TCR-pMHC / antibody-antigen structures.
scale: Structural subset of IEDB (thousands of epitope-mapped complexes); exact count via the 3D browse interface
license: free public use (non-commercial attribution; confirm current terms)

provenance.maintainer: La Jolla Institute for Immunology (NIH/NIAID funded)

relevance.why: Connects experimentally validated epitopes to their pMHC and TCR-pMHC structures with precomputed interface contacts — directly bridges the presentation/recognition datasets to the structural design program.

agent_access: Browse-by-3D-structure web interface plus IEDB bulk export and REST query API (query-api.iedb.org); structural subset reachable programmatically.
caveats: License marked as free-use attribution pending confirmation of exact current terms. Structural subset must be isolated from the full IEDB export; dedup against STCRDab/TCR3d/IMGT by PDB ID. Coordinates themselves are PDB (CC0).

name: IMGT/3Dstructure-DB
description: IMGT's structural database for immunoglobulins/antibodies, T-cell receptors, MHC (MH) and other IgSF/MhcSF/RPI proteins, with standardized IMGT numbering, IMGT Colliers de Perles, paratope/epitope contact analysis and pMHC contact site annotation. Provides consistent immunogenetic annotation of pMHC and TCR-pMHC complexes.
scale: ~9,431 structural entries (IG, TR, MH, RPI); historically ~294 pMHC complexes and ~920 antigen-receptor/antigen complexes

provenance.maintainer: IMGT / LIGM (CNRS, Montpellier, France); ELIXIR Core Data Resource (from 2026-07)

relevance.why: Uniform IMGT numbering and contact-site annotation of pMHC and TCR-pMHC complexes makes it the reference for consistent interface definitions across TCR/MHC structures used in design and recognition models.
