agent_access: Web query interface and download area; structured annotations downloadable. Programmatic access feasible but IMGT historically discourages heavy automated scraping — respect rate limits and robots.
caveats: Current data is CC BY 4.0 per the IMGT homepage (older 2010 article showed CC BY-NC — now superseded). Attribution required. Annotation-heavy; overlaps STCRDab/TCR3d for TCR-pMHC — dedup by PDB ID.

name: Integrated Resource for Reproducibility in Macromolecular Crystallography (IRRMC / proteindiffraction.org)
description: Archive of RAW X-ray diffraction images and metadata from macromolecular crystallography experiments, most tied to deposited PDB structures. The diffraction- "scan" counterpart to the PDB's processed structure factors — the primary detector data from which coordinates were refined.
scale: 11,223 indexed diffraction datasets across 7,007 projects (2026)

provenance.maintainer: Minor Lab, University of Virginia (orig. NIH BD2K U01 HG008424)

relevance.why: Raw diffraction data let models learn (or be validated on) the full experiment-to- structure pipeline, and expose refinement-quality and multi-conformer signal that the final deposited coordinates hide.

agent_access: Public browse/search by PDB ID, beamline, resolution; per-dataset downloads with DOIs; REST API documented at /api/docs. Datasets are large (GBs of images each). Automatable but bandwidth-heavy.
caveats: CC0, but each dataset has its own DOI the authors ask you to cite. Image formats vary by detector; converting to usable form needs crystallography tooling. Related: SBGrid Data Bank (data.sbgrid.org) hosts additional raw structural datasets.

name: mdCATH
description: Large-scale all-atom molecular-dynamics dataset spanning 5,398 CATH protein domains, each simulated in 5 replicas at 5 temperatures (320–450 K) to sample folding/unfolding and thermal conformational landscapes. Purpose-built as ML training data for dynamics- and generative-structure models.
scale: 5,398 domains, 134,950 trajectories, avg 464 ns/traj, 62.6 ms aggregate; 3.3–3.6 TB

provenance.maintainer: Compute Sciences Lab / Acellera / Giorgino & De Fabritiis

relevance.why: Directly trains sequence/structure-to-conformational-ensemble and dynamics models; the multi-temperature design exposes flexibility and (un)folding signal that static PDB entries lack. Already a standard ML-for-dynamics benchmark.

agent_access: HuggingFace datasets: huggingface-cli / datasets library streaming, no auth. Per-domain HDF5 files; torchmd-net dataloader and GitHub scripts provided. Fully agent-friendly (stream chunks rather than pulling all 3.6 TB).
caveats: CC BY 4.0 — redistributable with attribution. 3.6 TB total; stream per-domain. Single force field; high-temperature replicas are deliberately out-of-equilibrium.

name: MDRepo
description: Open data warehouse for community-contributed all-atom MD simulations of proteins, with standardized ingestion, metadata and search — an actively maintained successor- style resource to the legacy MoDEL library and complementary to BioExcel MDDB/ MDposit for depositing and querying trajectories.
scale: Community warehouse (thousands of contributed protein MD simulations; growing)
license: open (verify per-deposit; warehouse terms on site)

relevance.why: Standardized, queryable protein MD at warehouse scale for pretraining and benchmarking dynamics/ensemble models — curated enough to use directly, unlike a raw aggregator.

agent_access: Web warehouse with search and per-simulation download; programmatic access via the site. No auth for public deposits. Related systems: BioExcel MDDB / MDposit (mdposit.mddbr.eu) and the legacy MoDEL (mmb.irbbarcelona.org, no longer updated).
caveats: Deposit-level licenses vary — check per simulation before redistribution/training. Younger resource; coverage and metadata consistency still maturing.

name: MDverse
description: A search/indexing layer over the "dark matter" of public molecular-dynamics data: ~250,000 files and ~2,000 datasets harvested and indexed from Zenodo, Figshare and OSF (focused on GROMACS output). Not a single curated archive but a discovery engine plus metadata/API over dispersed MD deposits.
scale: ~2,000 datasets, ~250,000 indexed files (2024)
license: aggregator; per-dataset licenses vary (data from Zenodo/Figshare/OSF). Paper CC BY 4.0.

provenance.maintainer: Tiemann, Barnoud, Reddy, Fuchs et al. (academic consortium)

relevance.why: Lets an agent discover and pull large volumes of heterogeneous public MD for pretraining dynamics models — far more data than any single curated set, if you accept variable provenance.

agent_access: Searchable index + downloadable metadata; actual trajectories live on the host repositories (Zenodo/Figshare/OSF) and are fetched from there. Scriptable via the index, but you must resolve and download each dataset separately.
caveats: Per-dataset licenses are heterogeneous and often unstated — you MUST check each source dataset's terms before training/redistribution. Quality, force fields and completeness vary wildly; strong dedup/curation needed.

name: MISATO (protein–ligand MD + QM dataset)
description: ML dataset of protein–ligand complexes with 10 ns MD per complex (restart + topology files) and semi-empirical QM-refined ligand properties/electronic densities. Built for structure-based drug discovery and binding/dynamics ML.
scale: 16,972 MD-simulated complexes (10 ns each) + 19,443 QM-curated ligands; ~194 GiB
license: code LGPL-2.1; dataset on Zenodo (open access) — verify dataset-specific terms

relevance.why: Pairs complex dynamics with QM-level ligand chemistry — useful for binding-mode, affinity and ligand-conformation models that need movement, not just a docked pose. Relevant where peptide/small-molecule binders are designed.

agent_access: Zenodo wget of MD.hdf5 / QM.hdf5; PyTorch dataloaders and Lightning datamodules in the repo. No auth. ~194 GiB, easily scripted.
caveats: Repo code is LGPL-2.1; the dataset license on Zenodo is "open access" but a precise SPDX license is not clearly stated — confirm before redistribution. 10 ns is short sampling. Protein–ligand focus (not peptide-specific).

name: OpenProteinSet (OpenFold training data)
description: The open reconstruction of AlphaFold2's training inputs, released with OpenFold: precomputed MSAs and template hits for PDB chains plus large UniClust30 cluster MSAs, and self-distillation AlphaFold predictions. The canonical ready-to-train sequence->structure(+MSA) corpus for folding models.
scale: MSAs for ~140k unique PDB chains + ~16M UniClust30 clusters; ~270k AF2 self-distillation structures

relevance.why: Directly ML-training-ready: the exact paired sequence/MSA/structure inputs for training AlphaFold-style models without recomputing MSAs. Explicitly built for ML training and commercially usable (CC BY 4.0).

agent_access: AWS Registry of Open Data, bucket s3://openfold (us-east-1); list/copy with `aws s3 ... --no-sign-request` (no AWS account needed). Large (TB-scale); download scripts in the OpenFold GitHub repo. Fully agent-downloadable.
caveats: Very large; plan storage/bandwidth. Some postprocessing (sequence clustering) must be regenerated. Built on UniClust30/PDB snapshots of its era — may need refresh for newest structures.

name: PANDORA template database + reverse-peptide templates (Xue lab)
description: Data releases for PANDORA, an anchor-restrained MODELLER-based pMHC modeling pipeline: the pMHCI/pMHCII template structure database (plus reversed-pMHCII templates) deposited on Zenodo, used to generate 3D peptide-MHC models at scale.
scale: pMHCI + pMHCII + reversed-pMHCII template structures (Zenodo, periodically updated)

provenance.maintainer: Xue Lab (Radboud University / DTL), Nijmegen, NL

relevance.why: Curated pMHC-I/II template sets enable fast generation of peptide-MHC models (incl. class II and reverse-bound peptides) for design targets and for building training data where no crystal structure exists.

agent_access: Open Zenodo downloads (DB 10.5281/zenodo.15495898; reverse templates 10.5281/zenodo.6373630); PANDORA installable via Conda/pip (X-lab-3D/PANDORA).
caveats: Templates derive from PDB; generated models are predictions. Class II modeling accuracy is lower than class I. Verify current template DB version.

name: PDB-REDO databank
description: Re-refined, re-built and optimised versions of (nearly) every crystallographic PDB entry, produced by a uniform automated pipeline. Improves model quality and consistency relative to the deposited coordinates — a cleaner, homogenised sequence->structure training source for crystal structures, with per-entry validation metrics.
scale: ~140k+ entries (112,385 reported Feb 2018; grows with PDB)
license: Public domain (no copyright restrictions; attribution requested)

provenance.maintainer: Joana Pereira / Robbie Joosten, NKI & Utrecht/SURF

relevance.why: Quality-normalised structures reduce label noise for structure prediction and structure-based representation learning; validation JSON supports confidence-weighted training.

agent_access: Per-entry download by wget and whole-databank via rsync; no auth. Agent can bulk-mirror. Each entry ships re-refined/rebuilt PDB+mmCIF plus JSON validation.
caveats: X-ray only (no cryo-EM/NMR). Data are copyright-free but credit PDB-REDO and original authors. Models are optimised predictions of the true structure, not independent experiments — keep that provenance in mind for benchmarking.

name: PDBbind
description: Curated collection of experimental binding affinities (Kd/Ki/IC50) for biomolecular complexes with known 3D structures in the PDB — predominantly protein-ligand, plus protein-protein and protein-nucleic-acid subsets. Paired with the CASF scoring benchmarks. Relevant for structure-based affinity scoring methodology transferable to pMHC binders.
scale: ~19,000 complexes with affinity labels (v2020); CASF-2016 benchmark = 285 complexes
license: custom (free for academic/non-commercial use; registration required)

provenance.maintainer: Wang Lab (originally U. Michigan / Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry)

last_updated: ~annual (latest widely used: v2020); access/mirroring has varied

relevance.why: Benchmark that defined structure-based affinity scoring; its protein-protein subset and CASF methodology inform scoring/ranking of designed peptide-MHC binders even though its core is small-molecule.

agent_access: Requires free registration to download; bundled as archives (general/refined/ core sets) + CASF packages. Automatable after login, but gated — not anonymous.
caveats: Registration gate and terms restrict redistribution (academic/non-commercial). Documented train/test leakage with CASF (prompting LP-PDBbind, CC BY 4.0). Mostly small-molecule — tangential to pMHC except for scoring methodology.

name: Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) / PDBe-KB
description: EMBL-EBI wwPDB member: a full mirror of the PDB archive plus value-added derived data. SIFTS provides residue-level mappings between PDB structures and UniProt, Pfam, InterPro, CATH, SCOP and Ensembl — the authoritative crosswalk between sequence databases and structure. PDBe-KB aggregates functional/ structural annotations on top.
scale: Same global archive (~262k experimental structures); PDBe-KB aggregates annotations from ~40 partner resources
license: CC0 1.0 (wwPDB structure data); PDBe-KB aggregated annotations CC BY 4.0

relevance.why: SIFTS is the key resource for building sequence->structure training labels: it aligns PDB coordinate residues to canonical UniProt sequences, essential for assembling clean paired corpora and for transferring structure to sequence-only datasets.

agent_access: Open REST API (ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/api) returning JSON, PDBe-KB graph API, coordinate service for mmCIF/binaryCIF, plus FTP/rsync mirror of the full archive and SIFTS files. No auth; well-suited to automation.
caveats: Structure data is CC0; separate PDBe-KB aggregated-annotation terms (CC BY 4.0) apply to derived annotations. Redundant with RCSB for raw coordinates — use for its annotations/API ergonomics, not as a second copy of the archive.

name: Protein Ensemble Database (PED)
description: Primary deposition database for structural ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins/regions (IDPs/IDRs) and flexible multidomain proteins — experimentally and computationally derived conformer sets with optional per-conformer weights. The reference resource for "proteins that have no single structure."
scale: 461 entries / 538 ensembles (2024 release; growing, with predicted-ensemble integration planned)
license: CC BY 4.0 (per bio.tools/ELIXIR listings; some PED papers cite CC BY-NC 4.0 — see caveats)

provenance.maintainer: ELIXIR-Italy / consortium (Tompa, Tosatto, Lazar et al.)

relevance.why: Ground-truth conformational ensembles for IDPs/IDRs — essential for any model that predicts distributions rather than single structures, a known failure mode of AlphaFold-style tools on disorder.

agent_access: Multi-model PDB per entry; REST API (Django REST + OpenAPI/Swagger) at /api for metadata and selective download; Python SDK noted in the 2027 update. No auth. Small enough to mirror fully.
caveats: License is reported inconsistently (CC BY 4.0 in ELIXIR/bio.tools vs CC BY-NC 4.0 in some papers) — verify current site terms before commercial use. Small (hundreds of entries); ensembles differ in method/quality, so weighting and provenance matter.

name: PepBDB (Peptide–Protein Interaction Structure Database)
description: Comprehensive structural database of biological peptide–protein complexes derived from the PDB (peptide ligands up to ~50 residues), with cleaned coordinates, interface residues, binding data and per-complex annotation. A focused training set for peptide-binding and peptide-docking models.
scale: ~13,299 peptide–protein complexes (2020 release; monthly updates intended)
license: derived from PDB (CC0 underlying); no explicit DB license stated — see caveats

provenance.maintainer: Huang Lab, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

relevance.why: Core peptide-in-complex structure set for learning peptide primary-sequence-to- bound-3D and peptide docking/design — directly on-domain for peptide binder work.

agent_access: Bulk tarball of cleaned PDB files plus per-complex pages; no auth. Site hosted in CN and intermittently returns 5xx — retry / mirror. Scriptable once reachable.
caveats: Underlying coordinates are PDB-derived (CC0); the database adds no explicit license — attribute PepBDB + original PDB entries. Count is a 2020 figure; site availability is flaky. Overlaps the PDB (domain-6) — dedup against rcsb-pdb.

name: Peptipedia
description: Comprehensive peptide database and ML web app aggregating bioactive/therapeutic peptide sequences (antimicrobial, anticancer, hormonal, etc.) from 70+ sources, with activity annotations and sequence-analysis tooling. Primarily sequence+activity (not 3D), included here as the peptide-sequence backbone that pairs with peptide structure sets.
scale: v2.0: >3.8M peptide sequences from >70 sources (v1: ~92,055)
license: GPL-3.0 (software, per original paper); dataset terms not separately stated — see caveats

provenance.maintainer: ProteinEngineering-PESB2 group (Chile; Medina-Ortiz, Olivera-Nappa et al.)

relevance.why: Massive labeled peptide-sequence corpus for peptide property/activity models and for selecting sequences whose 3D/conformation is then learned from the structure sets in this domain.

agent_access: Web app + GitHub repo with source and sample data; download via repo. No auth. Full- DB bulk export is not clearly documented — may require the app or repo rather than a single dump.
caveats: Software is GPL-3.0; the aggregated dataset's reuse license is not clearly separated from its 70+ heterogeneous sources — check source terms before redistribution. Sequence/activity data, not structures.

name: pMHC / peptide-in-groove structure subsets (cross-reference)
description: Cross-reference, not a new dataset. The structures of peptides bound in the MHC groove (pMHC) and in TCR–pMHC complexes are the single most on-mission peptide- structure resource for Veritope, but they live in the main structure catalog (domain-6) and the presentation/recognition catalogs — not re-extracted here to avoid duplication.
scale: ~thousands of pMHC + hundreds of TCR–pMHC structures across PDB/IEDB-3D/STCRDab/TCR3d
license: CC0 (PDB coordinates); IEDB-3D CC BY 4.0 — see domain-6

provenance.maintainer: See domain-6: rcsb-pdb, pdbe, iedb-3d, stcrdab, tcr3d, atlas-tcr-pmhc

relevance.why: The peptide-conformation-in-context data most central to presentation and TCR recognition. Use the domain-6 entries for extraction; this pointer prevents double-counting.

agent_access: Via the referenced domain-6 resources: PDB/PDBe programmatic APIs and bulk mmCIF, IEDB-3D exports, STCRDab/TCR3d structural downloads. No auth. See those entries for exact endpoints.
caveats: DO NOT deep-duplicate: extract pMHC/TCR-pMHC from the domain-6 structure catalog and the presentation/recognition catalogs. Dedup across PDB, IEDB-3D, STCRDab and TCR3d, which overlap heavily.

name: Propedia (peptide–protein complex database)
description: Large PDB-derived database of peptide–protein complexes with graph-based structural signatures, clustered interfaces, and separate downloadable sets of complexes, peptides, receptors, interfaces and sequences. Broader coverage than PepBDB and richer interface representations (v2.3; a later "Propedia 26" release exists).
scale: ~49,300 complexes, 28,581 peptides, 35,478 receptors (v2.3)
license: annotations CC BY 4.0 (Propedia 26 Zenodo); underlying PDB data CC0 — verify v2.3 page

provenance.maintainer: Bioinformatics group, DCC/UFMG (Martins, de Melo et al.)

relevance.why: The largest curated peptide–protein structural collection with ready-made interface/signature features — strong supervision for peptide-binding, interface and peptide-design models.

agent_access: Direct zip downloads (e.g. complex2_3.zip ~2.4 GB) for each data class; web browse/ search. No auth. Fully scriptable. A versioned Zenodo release ("Propedia 26") gives a DOI'd, clearly-licensed snapshot.
caveats: v2.3 download page does not state its own license; the Zenodo "Propedia 26" record clarifies CC BY 4.0 annotations over CC0 PDB data — prefer the Zenodo release for clean terms. Heavy overlap with PDB/PepBDB — dedup.

name: RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB archive)
description: The primary worldwide archive of experimentally determined 3D structures of proteins, nucleic acids and complexes (X-ray, cryo-EM, NMR). The canonical ground-truth sequence->structure pairing: every entry carries SEQRES records and atomic coordinates. RCSB is the US wwPDB member and the most common bulk source. The archive is the foundation on which AlphaFold/ESMFold/OpenFold etc. were trained.
scale: ~262,786 experimental structures + ~1,062,058 computed models (Nov 2026); ~17,588 new structures in 2025

provenance.maintainer: RCSB PDB (Rutgers / UCSD-SDSC / UCSF), member of wwPDB, NSF/NIH/DOE funded

relevance.why: Ground-truth experimental structures for pretraining and representation learning; SEQRES<->coordinate pairs are the core supervised signal for any structure-prediction or structure-aware design model.

agent_access: Fully bulk-downloadable, no auth. HTTPS (files.rcsb.org), rsync, FTP, and AWS S3 Open Data (annual snapshots, s3://pdbsnapshots / Registry of Open Data). REST data API (data.rcsb.org) and search API (search.rcsb.org). Agent-friendly.
caveats: CC0 removes copyright restrictions; attribution to original authors is encouraged not required. mmCIF is the canonical format (legacy PDB format is frozen/capped at 99,999 atoms). Needs dedup/clustering for ML splits to avoid train/test leakage (use sequence/structure clustering, e.g. by CATH/SCOPe).

name: SAbDab / SAbDab-nano (Structural Antibody Database)
description: Oxford OPIG database collecting and annotating all experimentally determined antibody structures in the PDB (now served as SAbDab2), weekly-updated, with numbering, CDR definitions, antigen annotation and antibody-antigen complex identification. SAbDab-nano is the companion tracker for nanobodies / single-domain antibodies. Thera-SAbDab tracks therapeutic antibodies.
scale: Thousands of antibody structures (weekly from PDB); SAbDab-nano ~2,246 single-domain structures (live stats; 823 as of Sept 2021)

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), University of Oxford

last_updated: 2026 (weekly from PDB); SAbDab2 UI 2.1.x; ML splits refreshed ~6-monthly on Zenodo

relevance.why: Benchmark for antibody/nanobody binder design and the antibody-pMHC precedent for peptide-MHC binders; curated non-redundant sets and standardised train/test splits reduce leakage in design/affinity models.

agent_access: Open web search + bulk downloads; curated ML training sets with train/test splits hosted on Zenodo. Python API bundled in SAbBox (free academic license). Programmatic filtering/download feasible.
caveats: Derived annotations under CC BY 4.0 (attribution required). Counts shift weekly as PDB grows. Antibody-centric: covers TCR only via its sibling STCRDab, not here. Verify current CC BY 4.0 terms for any redistribution.

name: Small Angle Scattering Biological Data Bank (SASBDB)
description: Curated, free repository of small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering (SAXS/SANS) experimental data and the derived models (ab initio bead models, rigid-body and ensemble fits). SAS reports overall shape, size and flexibility in solution — a low-resolution but conformation-sensitive complement to crystallography and cryo-EM.
scale: 5,716 experimental datasets + 6,804 models (2026; plus ~570 datasets / ~900 models on hold)
license: custom (free access, attribution via citation) — no explicit SPDX license stated

provenance.maintainer: EMBL Hamburg (Svergun group lineage) / SASBDB consortium

relevance.why: Solution-scattering curves constrain overall conformation and flexibility, especially for multidomain and partially disordered proteins — useful ground truth for conformational-ensemble models where a single crystal structure is misleading.

agent_access: Freely downloadable per entry; REST API for programmatic metadata/data retrieval and search. No auth. Automatable, though there is no single one-click full-archive tarball documented — iterate over accession codes via the API.
caveats: No explicit SPDX/CC license on the site; terms are "freely accessible and downloadable" with citation requested. Treat redistribution conservatively and attribute. Data are curve+model, not atomic coordinates.

name: SKEMPI 2.0
description: Manually curated benchmark of experimentally measured changes in protein-protein binding affinity (and kinetics/thermodynamics) upon mutation, each mapped to a PDB complex structure. Includes antibody-antigen and TCR-pMHC complexes relevant to interface-mutation effect prediction.
scale: 7,085 mutations with binding affinity data; 1,844 with kinetics; 443 with enthalpy/entropy; 440 binding-abolishing
license: unknown (paper CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; database terms not explicitly stated)

relevance.why: Gold-standard ddG-on-mutation labels mapped to structures, including immune complexes — core training/benchmark data for affinity-maturation and binder-optimization models used in peptide-MHC binder design.

agent_access: Single CSV download of the full table plus the associated PDB structures; trivially scriptable. No API needed.
caveats: Database redistribution license not clearly posted (marked unknown); the paper is CC BY-NC-ND. Known duplicate/measurement-condition heterogeneity — deduplicate and normalize by pH/temperature. Cleaned subsets (e.g. DACUM, Apache-2.0) exist but do not relicense SKEMPI itself.

name: STAG structure-based TCR-pMHC binding dataset (Kavraki Lab)
description: Data for STAG, a structure-based TCR-pMHC binding predictor that generalizes to unseen peptides: a large labeled sample set plus deposited Rosetta-relaxed and TCRmodel2-generated TCR-pMHC structures used for training/evaluation.
scale: 19,282 labeled TCR-pMHC samples (GitHub); Rosetta-relaxed + TCRmodel2 structures (Zenodo)

relevance.why: Couples a large labeled TCR-pMHC binding set with modeled 3D structures and an unseen-peptide generalization split — directly supports structure-based affinity/specificity prediction for binder design.

agent_access: GitHub repo (KavrakiLab/STAG_public) for samples/code; modeled structures on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.18344673). Scriptable.
caveats: Licenses not confirmed (marked unknown). Structures are modeled (Rosetta/ TCRmodel2), not experimental. Human-focused.

name: STCRDab (Structural T-Cell Receptor Database)
description: OPIG's automated, weekly-updated database of all experimentally determined TCR structures in the PDB, annotated with IMGT numbering, CDR loops, chain pairing and (where present) peptide-MHC partners. The TCR analogue of SAbDab; directly supplies TCR and TCR-pMHC complex structures.
scale: Hundreds of TCR structures incl. alpha-beta and gamma-delta; subset are TCR-pMHC complexes (weekly from PDB)

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), University of Oxford

relevance.why: Primary curated source of TCR and TCR-pMHC complex structures with consistent IMGT numbering — a core training/benchmark set for TCR-pMHC recognition models and for engineering binders against peptide-MHC.

agent_access: Open web interface with filtered bulk download of annotated TCR structures; same OPIG tooling as SAbDab. Scriptable via the download endpoints.
caveats: Original paper states open-access but an explicit data license is not clearly posted (marked unknown) — confirm terms before redistribution. Coordinates themselves derive from PDB (CC0). Counts grow weekly.

name: SwiftMHC pMHC-I training & structure dataset
description: Supplementary data for SwiftMHC (attention network for MHC-bound peptide identification + 3D modeling): a large set of HLA-A*02:01 9-mer peptide-MHC complexes from IEDB and a curated set of X-ray pMHC-I structures used for training and evaluation.
scale: 7,726 IEDB 9-mer HLA-A*02:01 pMHC complexes + 202 X-ray HLA-A*02:01 9-mer pMHC structures

relevance.why: Pairs thousands of pMHC-I models with 202 experimental structures for a single allele — a ready training/benchmark corpus for structure-based peptide-MHC modeling and binder design on HLA-A*02:01.

agent_access: Single CC BY 4.0 Zenodo archive (swiftmhc-supplementary-data-8k-v1.tar.xz, ~10.5 GB). Direct download, scriptable.
caveats: Single allele (HLA-A*02:01), 9-mers only — narrow. Most entries are PANDORA/ IEDB-derived models, not experimental (only the 202 X-ray are experimental).

name: SWISS-MODEL Repository (SMR)
description: Database of annotated 3D homology (template-based) models for UniProtKB target sequences, generated continuously by the SWISS-MODEL pipeline, with per-model QMEAN/QMEANDisCo quality estimates and PDB->UniProt mappings. A pre-AlphaFold predicted sequence->structure corpus still useful for comparison.
scale: ~3.32M models + ~214k PDB structures mapped to UniProtKB

relevance.why: Template-based models with calibrated quality scores provide an alternative predicted-structure signal and a benchmark against learned folding; QMEANDisCo is a reference for confidence calibration.

agent_access: REST API gives programmatic model coordinates (bulk download feasible); per- proteome coordinate archives (e.g. ~5.5 GB for human). Large bulk pulls: contact maintainers. No auth for individual/API access.
caveats: RED FLAG: CC BY-SA 4.0 is share-alike — derivative datasets may need to carry the same license; check compatibility before combining with CC0/CC BY corpora. Homology models, not experiments.

name: TCR-pMHC structure prediction benchmark (unified evaluation)
description: A non-redundant TCR-pMHC benchmark released with a unified evaluation of modern folding models (AlphaFold, Boltz, Protenix, OpenFold-3, RoseTTAFold2, TCRmodel2, AlphaRED, ColabFold, ESM/OmegaFold), plus a ddG mutation subset, with code for reproducible scoring.
scale: 70 non-redundant TCR-pMHC complexes (56 class I, 14 class II) from TCR3d; 21-mutation ddG subset from SKEMPI v2

provenance.maintainer: Benchmark authors (academic); structures from TCR3d / PDB

relevance.why: A clean, non-redundant, class-I/II-split TCR-pMHC benchmark with a unified scoring protocol across current folding tools — the standard yardstick for choosing a modeling engine for the design pipeline.

agent_access: Code + benchmark lists on GitHub; structures fetched from PDB; ddG from SKEMPI v2. Fully scriptable.
caveats: Repo license not confirmed (marked unknown). Structures derive from PDB (CC0); the benchmark's value is the curated non-redundant split + scoring code.

name: TCR3d 2.0 (T-Cell Receptor Structural Repertoire Database)
description: Curated, annotated database of all experimentally determined TCR structures from the PDB, organized around TCR-pMHC complexes (class I and class II), unbound TCRs, and now also includes modeling tools and interaction mapping. Links each structure to binding affinities imported from ATLAS.
scale: ~250 TCR-pMHC complexes (241 class I + 90 class II in v2.0, vs 153/62 in 2019); plus unbound TCR structures

relevance.why: The most purpose-built catalog of TCR-pMHC complex structures, with class I/II split and affinity cross-links — a key benchmark set for TCR-pMHC recognition and for peptide-MHC binder design.

agent_access: Open web tables (complexes, class I/II pMHC) with per-structure links to PDB; downloadable listings. No explicit documented REST API; feasible to scrape curated tables and fetch coordinates from PDB.
caveats: Explicit data license not clearly stated (marked unknown) — coordinates come from PDB (CC0), annotations curated by the group. Affinities are re-exports from ATLAS/literature; dedup against STCRDab/IMGT before combining.

name: TCRBuilder2+ predicted TCR structures (OTS) + weights (OPIG)
description: Data releases from the TCRBuilder2+ / ImmuneBuilder TCR work: a large set of predicted structures for the Observed T-cell receptor Space (OTS) and the trained model weights, with training on experimentally resolved TCR structures from STCRDab.
scale: OTS: large-scale predicted TCR structures (Zenodo); trained on 704 experimentally resolved TCR structures from STCRDab

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), University of Oxford

relevance.why: Large predicted TCR structural space plus open weights enable rapid modeling of TCR V-domains for docking against peptide-MHC and for enriching training sets in the recognition/design pipeline.

agent_access: Open Zenodo downloads (OTS predictions 10.5281/zenodo.10854757; weights 10.5281/zenodo.10892159); code pip-installable (oxpig/ImmuneBuilder). Scriptable.
caveats: OTS entries are predictions, not experimental. A DOI discrepancy exists for the v1.2 code release (14727164 vs 14727165) — verify before citing.

name: TCRdock benchmark + ternary template set (Bradley)
description: Data released with TCRdock, a TCR-specialized AlphaFold pipeline for TCR-pMHC modeling: a curated ternary-complex template database, a human ternary fine-tuning set, and benchmark test sets, distributed via the GitHub repo and paper supplementary data.
scale: ~220 ternary TCR-pMHC template structures (ternary_templates_v2.tsv); 93 human ternary structures (279 fine-tuning examples); benchmark test cases in supplement

provenance.maintainer: Philip Bradley, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center

relevance.why: Provides a curated TCR-pMHC ternary template set and reproducible benchmark for docking-geometry and complex-prediction accuracy — core inputs/eval for TCR-pMHC structure prediction feeding binder design.

agent_access: Public GitHub clone; TSV template index + PDB templates + benchmark TSVs. Fully scriptable; fine-tuning code in separate alphafold_finetune repo.
caveats: Repo license not confirmed (marked unknown). Templates derive from PDB (CC0). Small curated sets; dedup ternary templates against STCRDab/TCR3d.

name: TCRmodel2 TCR-pMHC modeling server & benchmark (Pierce Lab)
description: TCRmodel2, a deep-learning (AlphaFold-based) method for high-resolution TCR and TCR-pMHC modeling, with a public server and code and a non-redundant time-split benchmark of recent TCR-pMHC complexes used to assess accuracy.
scale: Non-redundant TCR-pMHC benchmark (~20 test cases released after a cutoff date) drawn from TCR3d; web server + code

provenance.maintainer: Pierce Lab, University of Maryland IBBR

relevance.why: A high-accuracy, openly available TCR-pMHC modeling engine plus its benchmark — a candidate production modeler and an accuracy reference for the recognition/design pipeline.

agent_access: Public web server (tcrmodel.ibbr.umd.edu) and code (piercelab/tcrmodel2); benchmark complexes from TCR3d/PDB. Local runs scriptable.
caveats: Repo license not confirmed (marked unknown). Benchmark is small and sourced from TCR3d (dedup accordingly). Outputs are predictions.

name: tFold-TCR / TCRStructDB + STCRDab-22 benchmark (Tencent)
description: Releases accompanying tFold-TCR (fast TCR-peptide-MHC complex modeling): TCRStructDB, a large database of predicted TCR/TCR-pMHC structures, plus a held-out structural benchmark (STCRDab-22-TCR_pMHC) and model weights.
scale: TCRStructDB (large set of predicted TCR-pMHC structures); benchmark STCRDab-22-TCR_pMHC = 18 TCR-pMHC complexes (+6 unpublished); trained on STCRDab pre-2022

relevance.why: A large predicted TCR-pMHC structure database plus a clean held-out benchmark — scale useful for pretraining/structure mining and for evaluating TCR-pMHC modeling that underpins binder design.

agent_access: Code + weights on GitHub (TencentAI4S/tfold); dataset files via Tencent Weiyun Drive and ai4s.tencent.com/tcr portal. Predicted structures are models.
caveats: License/terms for TCRStructDB not confirmed (marked unknown). TCRStructDB is predictions, not experiments. Benchmark is small (18 complexes).

name: AIRR Data Commons (ADC) + iReceptor
description: Federated network of repositories serving AIRR-standard adaptive immune receptor repertoire (TCR/BCR-seq) data through a common query API; iReceptor is a gateway over it. A standardized programmatic layer for pulling repertoire data across many studies.
scale: billions of annotated sequences across federated repositories
license: API spec CC BY 4.0; per-repository/study data terms vary

relevance.why: Standardized cross-repository access to large repertoire datasets — background/negative TCR distributions and disease-associated repertoires for recognition modeling.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: ADC API (uniform JSON query/download) across all member repositories; iReceptor gateway exports sequences/clones/cells in AIRR TSV. One query spans many repositories. Highly automatable, no auth for public data.
caveats: API spec is CC BY 4.0 but underlying per-study data licenses are not centralized — check per repository/study before redistribution/ML use. Repertoire data is mostly specificity- agnostic (bulk) — pair with VDJdb/MIRA for labels.

name: DNA-barcoded peptide-MHC-I multimer screen (Bentzen 2016)
description: The founding dataset for DNA-barcode-labelled pMHC-I multimers, enabling simultaneous detection of >1,000 peptide specificities per sample by sequencing the barcodes of bound multimers. Release includes the barcode-labelled multimer panels (e.g. a 1,031- specificity panel and a 110-specificity panel) and the T-cell screening readouts as supplementary tables.
scale: >1,000 pMHC specificities per sample; 1,031- and 110-plex barcoded multimer panels

provenance.maintainer: Bentzen, Marquard, Hadrup et al. (DTU / Herlev Hospital)

relevance.why: The method and data that scaled antigen-specific T-cell detection beyond fluorescent multimers; a large pMHC-specificity screen independent of the 10x dextramer releases, useful for TCR-antigen pairing benchmarks.

agent_access: Supplementary Excel tables on the Nature Biotechnology article page (no auth for SI). No separate GEO/Zenodo repository was deposited.
caveats: Data only as journal SI under Springer Nature terms (no open license). Barcode panels describe reagents/specificities, not necessarily paired-TCR sequences.

name: pMHC yeast-display library screens (Birnbaum/Garcia lineage)
description: Deep-sequencing outputs of yeast-displayed peptide-MHC library selections against defined TCRs: large sets of peptides recovered (and depleted) over affinity-selection rounds, used to map TCR cross-reactivity landscapes. Method family includes YAMTAD and newer pMHC-pseudotyped-virus variants (e.g. VelociRAPTR).
scale: per-TCR: 10^6-10^9 library members screened; thousands of recovered peptides/TCR

relevance.why: Exhaustive per-TCR cross-reactivity maps are uniquely informative for modeling TCR specificity breadth and for de novo antigen/TCR design.

agent_access: No single portal — data live as journal supplementary tables and per-study GEO/SRA deposits (fetch via GEO/SRA APIs using accessions cited in each paper). Requires per-paper discovery; not a unified API.
caveats: Fragmented across publications; accessions and licenses vary per paper and some have no explicit data license — treat license as unknown and check each source. Selection-based read counts are enrichment signals, not calibrated affinities. Deduplicate/normalize across studies.

name: Canine TCR Repertoire Resources (single-cell + bulk + RNA-seq-derived)
description: The emerging but sparse canine T-cell-receptor repertoire landscape: validated single-cell TRA/TRB profiling on 10x Chromium; bulk TRB NGS protocols; and TCR CDR3 mining from public canine RNA-seq (>200k CDR3s assembled from ~2,000 samples via TRUST4/MiXCR).
scale: >200,000 CDR3 sequences (RNA-seq-mined); small primary single-cell/bulk cohorts
license: mixed (articles CC BY; raw reads via SRA public norms)

provenance.maintainer: multiple academic groups; data in SRA/GEO + article supplements

relevance.why: The core of canine RECOGNITION data — and it is thin. No paired TCR-pMHC specificity data for dogs exist publicly; what exists is repertoire composition, not antigen-labeled pairs.

agent_access: Article supplements (clonotype tables) + SRA FASTQ; reanalysis pipelines (TRUST4, MiXCR, SatTCR) on public canine RNA-seq. No auth.
caveats: MAJOR GAP: no canine equivalent of VDJdb/McPAS (no epitope-labeled TCRs); no canine germline V/D/J reference as mature as IMGT human. Repertoire only; specificity must be inferred or generated.

name: Canine TCR CDR3 Mining from Public RNA-seq (>200k CDR3)
description: >200,000 complete TCR CDR3 sequences assembled from ~2,000 public canine RNA-seq samples via TRUST4/MiXCR; plus bulk TRB NGS protocols and the SatTCR depth-analysis pipeline (2.5-3M reads to capture the canine repertoire).
scale: >200,000 CDR3s from ~2,000 RNA-seq samples
license: preprint CC BY; source reads via SRA public norms

relevance.why: Largest canine repertoire resource, assembled from existing RNA-seq; demonstrates reuse path for building canine TCR references without new wet-lab data.

agent_access: Reanalyze public canine RNA-seq with TRUST4/MiXCR; clonotype tables in supplements. No auth.
caveats: MAJOR GAP: repertoire composition only — NO epitope-labeled canine TCRs (no VDJdb/McPAS equivalent); no mature IMGT-grade canine germline V/D/J. Specificity must be generated.

name: Chu et al. 2023 — pan-cancer T-cell atlas (MD Anderson)
description: Pan-cancer single-cell T-cell atlas integrating many datasets, linking a cellular stress-response T-cell state to immunotherapy resistance. Provides an integrated reference and metadata across cancer types.
scale: integrated pan-cancer T cells (multi-study meta-atlas)

relevance.why: Integrated T-cell meta-atlas with an ICB-resistance-linked state; useful as a harmonized recognition reference and for label transfer.

agent_access: Processed atlas via the paper's portal/Zenodo (per Data Availability). Specific accession not verified in this pass — read the Data Availability section before scripting.
caveats: Meta-atlas built from many source datasets with their own licenses — check provenance of any slice before reuse. Accession not pinned here.

name: Dash et al. 2017 epitope-specific paired TCRab dataset
description: Single-cell-derived, in-frame paired TCR alpha/beta sequences spanning ten epitope-specific CD8+ repertoires from mice and humans — the foundational paired-chain, known-specificity set underlying TCRdist and many downstream specificity models.
scale: ~4,635 paired in-frame TCRab sequences; 10 epitope-specific repertoires; 110 subjects

relevance.why: Gold-standard paired-chain specificity data; the reference training/eval set for distance-based (TCRdist) and ML recognition methods, and a clean benchmark subset.

agent_access: Distributed as paper supplementary tables and bundled inside tcrdist/tcrdist3 example data on GitHub; small, trivially downloadable. CAVD DataSpace copy requires sign-in.
caveats: No explicit license on the supplementary data — verify. Small and epitope-biased (10 epitopes). No dog.

name: Dash et al. 2017 — epitope-specific TCR repertoires (TCRdist)
description: Paired single-cell TCRalpha/beta sequences for epitope-specific T cells (human and mouse, several immunodominant epitopes), released with the TCRdist method to show quantifiable, predictive features of epitope-specific repertoires.
scale: thousands of paired alpha/beta TCRs across multiple epitopes (human + mouse)

relevance.why: Benchmark paired alpha/beta epitope-specific TCR sets; the reference dataset for the widely-used TCRdist distance metric.

agent_access: Supplementary tables plus data bundled with the tcrdist/tcrdist3 repositories. No API; fetch supplements/repo. Automatable once located.
caveats: Supplementary-table license not explicitly stated — treat as unknown. Limited epitope set; small per-epitope counts. Paired chains are a key strength.

name: Glanville et al. 2017 (GLIPH) TCR specificity & naive reference data
description: TCR specificity-group reference from the GLIPH paper: antigen-specific CD4/CD8 TCR sets (e.g. tetramer-sorted and pathogen-specific repertoires) plus reference repertoires used to define 141 specificity groups via shared CDR3 motifs/global similarity.
scale: ~2,068 unique known-specificity TCRs; naive reference ~162,165 CDR3b sequences; 141 specificity groups

relevance.why: Motif-based TCR specificity grouping and its reference repertoires underpin many TCR-clustering/specificity methods; a standard benchmark input.

agent_access: Data as journal supplementary tables; reference repertoires redistributed via the immGLIPH / GLIPH tool packages ("human_v1.0_CD4/CD8/CD48"). No API; fetch supplements + package data.
caveats: Supplementary-table license not explicitly stated — treat as unknown. TCRbeta-centric. Pair with VDJdb/IEDB for broader epitope coverage.

name: Zhang et al. 2018 — colorectal cancer T-cell scRNA+TCR (GSE108989)
description: Smart-seq2 single-cell RNA-seq with paired TCR of T cells from colorectal cancer tumor, adjacent normal and blood (12 patients), characterizing T-cell subsets and clonal dynamics.
scale: ~11,138 T cells, 12 CRC patients (Smart-seq2 + TCR)

relevance.why: CRC TIL transcriptome+TCR reference completing the lung/liver/CRC trio from the Zhang lab for exhaustion-program modeling.

agent_access: GEO supplementary matrices + TCR tables via FTP. Automatable.
caveats: Smart-seq2; cell count approximate (confirm on series page). A companion 10x CRC dataset (GSE146771) exists from the same lab — separate accession.

name: Zheng et al. 2021 — pan-cancer T-cell atlas (GSE156728)
description: Pan-cancer single-cell landscape of tumor-infiltrating T cells: scRNA-seq (with TCR for many) across 316 donors / 21 cancer types, defining shared T-cell meta-clusters and exhaustion/activation programs. A major cross-cancer T-cell reference.
scale: ~397k+ T cells, 316 donors, 21 cancer types

relevance.why: The pan-cancer T-cell reference for harmonizing tumor T-cell states and clonality across cancers — anchor dataset for recognition-oriented modeling.

agent_access: GEO matrices + TCR tables via FTP; interactive browser also provided. Automatable.
caveats: Large, multi-batch; apply the authors' meta-clustering for cross-cancer harmonization. GEO sample count differs from donor count — read series metadata carefully.

name: Zheng et al. 2017 — HCC T-cell scRNA+TCR (GSE98638)
description: Smart-seq2 single-cell RNA-seq with paired TCR of ~5,063 T cells from hepatocellular carcinoma (tumor, adjacent normal, blood), mapping exhausted/regulatory T-cell states and clonal relationships. Early paired scRNA+TCR tumor dataset.
scale: ~5,063 T cells, 6 HCC patients (Smart-seq2 + TCR)

relevance.why: Paired transcriptome+TCR of tumor T cells links exhaustion state to clonality — a template for recognition-oriented tumor T-cell analysis.

agent_access: GEO supplementary matrices + TCR tables via FTP; metadata via E-utilities. Automatable.
caveats: Small cohort; Smart-seq2 (no UMI). TCR data is paired but low-throughput vs 10x.

name: Guo et al. 2018 — NSCLC T-cell scRNA+TCR (GSE99254)
description: Smart-seq2 single-cell RNA-seq with paired TCR of ~12,346 T cells from tumor, adjacent normal and blood of 14 treatment-naive non-small-cell lung cancer patients; defines T-cell states and clonal migration across compartments.
scale: ~12,346 T cells, 14 NSCLC patients (Smart-seq2 + TCR)

relevance.why: Lung TIL transcriptome+TCR reference for exhaustion/clonality modeling.

agent_access: GEO supplementary matrices + TCR tables via FTP. Verified NSCLC per GEO series record. Automatable.
caveats: Smart-seq2. Note a secondary paper mislabeled tissue for this accession; GEO record confirms NSCLC.

name: IEDB — T-cell assay / MHC-multimer export (cross-ref)
description: The Immune Epitope Database's T-cell assay records, including positive/negative peptide-MHC tetramer/multimer and functional readouts with TCR and MHC-restriction annotations. A very large labeled epitope/assay resource; catalogued deeply by the presentation agent — included here as the primary antigen-recognition label source.
scale: ~1M+ T-cell assay records; ~1.6M epitopes (whole IEDB)

relevance.why: Broadest curated source of TCR-epitope and multimer assay labels for building and benchmarking recognition models.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: bulk CSV/JSON export (no auth) + REST query API (query-api.iedb.org). Fully automatable. CC BY 4.0.
caveats: CROSS-REFERENCE ONLY — the presentation agent catalogs IEDB and MHC/HLA depth; do not duplicate here. Heterogeneous assay quality; filter by assay type/qualitative measure.

name: IEDB — Receptor/TCR records
description: The TCR/receptor portion of the Immune Epitope Database: curated T-cell assays with receptor sequences (CDR3, V/J) and their epitope + MHC context, plus the Receptor (IEDB-RF) tables. Large aggregate of published T-cell reactivity data.
scale: part of IEDB (~1.6M epitopes, >1M assays overall); hundreds of thousands of receptor rows

provenance.maintainer: La Jolla Institute for Immunology (NIH/NIAID funded)

relevance.why: Authoritative, deeply curated source of TCR-epitope assays; a backbone input for most TCR specificity training sets (NetTCR, TChard etc. draw from it).

agent_access: Bulk CSV/JSON export (database_export) plus a documented REST query API with rate limits. No auth; well suited to automated ingestion.
caveats: No SPDX license; terms are "free to use with citation" — confirm redistribution scope. Extracting clean TCR-epitope pairs needs schema-aware parsing. Non-human species present but dog TCR coverage is negligible.

name: IMMREP22 TCR-epitope specificity benchmark
description: Standardized community benchmark for TCR-epitope prediction: VDJdb-derived train/test data organized into peptide-specific buckets with defined negatives and evaluation files, used to compare 23 prediction models.
scale: 17 peptide-specific data buckets; VDJdb snapshot 2022-06-23

relevance.why: The de-facto standardized evaluation harness for TCR specificity models; use it to benchmark our models against published methods on identical splits.

agent_access: Flat CSVs + evaluation scripts in GitHub; clone/download, no auth. Fully automatable.
caveats: Repo license not stated — verify (data derived from VDJdb, so CC BY-ND redistribution limits may propagate). Peptide-restricted buckets; human only.

name: Adaptive Biotechnologies immuneACCESS / immunoSEQ public projects
description: Portal of published TCR-beta (immunoSEQ) bulk repertoire projects released alongside papers, spanning cancer, infection, autoimmunity and healthy cohorts. Very large collection of deeply sequenced human TCRB repertoires.
scale: hundreds of projects; billions of TCRB rearrangements aggregate
license: custom — 'For Research Use Only' (immuneACCESS Terms of Use)

relevance.why: Deepest public human TCRB repertoires; valuable for background/negative modeling and disease-cohort context, but terms constrain how we may reuse/redistribute.

agent_access: Account/registration required to download; data pulled per-project as TSV via the portal (no open API). Scriptable only after login and per-project EULA acceptance.
caveats: RED FLAG — bespoke "For Research Use Only" Terms of Use; redistribution, commercial use and ML/model-training permissions are not openly stated and are likely restricted. Could not retrieve the full clause text (JS-rendered terms page) — must be reviewed manually before any reuse/republication. TCRB only (no paired chains), not antigen-labeled. No dog.

name: ImmuneCODE / ImmuneRACE (Adaptive COVID release + MIRA)
description: Large open release of SARS-CoV-2-associated TCR-beta sequences and binding associations from natural and synthetic (MIRA antigen-stimulation) exposure, from the Adaptive/Microsoft ImmuneRACE study. Includes TCR-antigen association tables (MIRA) and raw repertoires.
scale: millions of TCRB sequences; thousands of subjects; MIRA antigen-association tables
license: custom — stated freely downloadable; governed by Adaptive terms

relevance.why: One of very few large public TCR-antigen association sets (MIRA) usable for recognition modeling; a benchmark for epitope-specific TCR prediction.

agent_access: Stated downloadable online/offline, but the download path sits behind the Adaptive portal (registration). Bulk TSV; scriptable after login. Has a DOI/release tag.
caveats: Governed by the same Adaptive Terms of Use red flag as immuneACCESS — confirm redistribution/ ML terms. MIRA uses antigen pools (peptide groups), not single-peptide resolution. TCRB only, human only.

name: ImmuneCODE / MIRA (immuneACCESS, Adaptive Biotechnologies)
description: Large-scale Multiplex Identification of T-cell Receptor Antigen (MIRA) assay data: SARS-CoV-2-specific TCRbeta sequences mapped to peptide/ORF antigen groups, plus deep TCR repertoire files from infected/exposed subjects. MIRA callsets provide experimentally associated TCR-to-antigen pairings (predominantly CD8/MHC-I).
scale: >160,000 high-confidence SARS-CoV-2-specific TCRs; repertoires from 1,414 subjects

relevance.why: The largest public experimentally-grounded TCR-to-antigen mapping (MIRA) — anchor training/benchmark set for TCR specificity models, even if single-antigen and TCRbeta-only.

agent_access: Download from immuneACCESS after accepting Terms of Use (account/click-through); MIRA callset zip is small (~3.7 MB), repertoire tgz is large (~23.8 GB). No open REST API; scripted download after auth.
caveats: Governed by immuneACCESS Terms of Use (custom) — review redistribution/commercial terms. TCR-antigen pairings are assay-associated, not individually functionally validated. TCRbeta-only (no paired alpha). SARS-CoV-2-centric.

name: iReceptor Gateway / AIRR Data Commons
description: Federated network of distributed AIRR-seq repositories queried through a common ADC API and the iReceptor Gateway. Hosts bulk and single-cell TCR (and BCR) repertoires from many studies under AIRR Community metadata standards.
scale: ~5.2B sequence annotations, >10,000 repertoires, >90 studies across ~9 repositories
license: varies per study/repository (CC BY 4.0 common in metadata)

relevance.why: Largest standardized source of raw repertoires for background modeling, V/J priors, and negative sampling; AIRR schema makes cross-study integration tractable.

agent_access: Read-only ADC REST API (JSON over HTTP POST), per-repository endpoints, no auth defined yet (controlled access planned). Supports programmatic bulk query/download; large pulls (TB-scale) are feasible but heavy.
caveats: Per-study licenses vary — the CC BY 4.0 seen in API metadata does not govern every dataset; check each study. Mostly unlabeled repertoires (no antigen specificity). Scale figures differ across sources. Some non-human species; dog coverage not confirmed.

name: McPAS-TCR — pathology-associated TCR database
description: Manually curated catalogue of TCR sequences associated with pathological conditions (cancer, infection, autoimmunity) in human and mouse, each linked to antigen/epitope, MHC and disease context. A labeled TCR-antigen reference distinct from VDJdb.
scale: >5,000 sequences (2017 paper); grown since via manual curation

provenance.maintainer: Friedman Lab, Weizmann Institute of Science

relevance.why: Disease-stratified TCR-antigen pairs (incl. cancer) complement VDJdb for recognition training and for benchmarking on oncology-relevant epitopes.

agent_access: Full database + filtered CSV exports downloadable directly over HTTP, no auth. No REST API; scripted file fetch. immunarch wraps it.
caveats: No explicit license stated (site asks only for citation) — treat redistribution as uncertain; verify before republishing. Manual curation means occasional inaccuracies (site disclaims this). Overlaps VDJdb/IEDB; dedup required. No dog coverage.

name: MixTCRpred training data & models
description: Training data (paired TCRs spanning many pMHCs) and pre-trained transformer models for MixTCRpred, predicting TCR binding to a panel of pMHCs including class I and II.
scale: ~17,715 TCRs across 146 pMHCs

provenance.maintainer: Gfeller lab, University of Lausanne / Ludwig Institute

relevance.why: Multi-pMHC paired-chain training set with class II and mouse coverage; strong recognition baseline and a reusable curated corpus.

agent_access: Training data in GitHub; pre-trained models on Zenodo; Colab notebook. No auth, automatable.
caveats: Data license not explicitly stated — verify. Restricted to the 146 pMHCs with enough data. No dog.

name: NetTCR-2.0 training/evaluation data
description: Data released with NetTCR-2.0 for paired alpha/beta TCR-peptide binding prediction: positive TCR-peptide pairs from IEDB+VDJdb, negatives derived from 10x single-cell data, with similarity-partitioned CDR3b training sets and MIRA/paired external evaluation files.
scale: ~2,744 unique paired positive pairs; ~387,598 10x-derived negatives

relevance.why: Widely used, pre-partitioned paired-chain benchmark with a principled negative set — a standard comparison point for any recognition model we build.

agent_access: Flat CSVs in the GitHub repo data folder; git clone / direct download, no auth. Fully automatable.
caveats: Stated academic/non-commercial only — red flag for commercial ML; confirm. Negatives inherit 10x dextramer assumptions; small positive set. Human only.

name: PanPep meta-learning TCR-antigen dataset
description: Curated TCR-peptide binding data and a large control (negative) dataset released with PanPep, a meta-learning model for zero-/few-shot TCR-antigen recognition across unseen peptides.
scale: control dataset ~927 MB; code package small

relevance.why: Few-shot/zero-shot framing matches the real problem of unseen tumor neoepitopes; its control set is a sizeable negative pool.

agent_access: Zenodo direct download (~928 MB control file + code zip); no auth. A later reusability-report deposit (10.5281/zenodo.16943691) adds re-curated data.
caveats: Zenodo record names no explicit license (open access right only) — verify reuse terms. Human only.

name: PIRD / TBAdb (Pan Immune Repertoire Database)
description: CNGB-hosted pan immune repertoire database collecting annotated TCR and BCR sequencing data across species and conditions. TBAdb is its manually curated sub-database of TCRs/BCRs targeting known antigens.
scale: TBAdb: curated antigen-specific TCR/BCR records; PIRD: many repertoire datasets

relevance.why: TBAdb is a third curated antigen-specific TCR set (alongside VDJdb/McPAS) for recognition training; PIRD adds repertoire breadth and some non-human species.

agent_access: Web portal on db.cngb.org; download may require a CNGB account. No documented open API; likely scripted/portal download. Confirm access gating.
caveats: No explicit license located — verify terms. Overlaps VDJdb/McPAS; dedup needed. Dog coverage not confirmed (PIRD claims multi-species but canine content unverified).

name: pMTnet / pMTnet-Omni training & validation datasets
description: Data accompanying the pMTnet family of TCR-pMHC affinity predictors. pMTnet-Omni covers Va/Vb/CDR3a/CDR3b + peptide + MHC (class I and II, human and mouse); the package ships reference databases and 5 validation datasets, with training data described in the papers.
scale: validation: 5 datasets; training: large aggregated pairs (see papers)

relevance.why: Paired-chain + class II coverage (incl. mouse) is rare; useful both as a baseline predictor and for its curated reference/validation pairs.

agent_access: Validation data and reference DB bundled with the pip package (pMTnet_Omni_Document); full prediction runs through the DBAI website (upload). Validation data auto-fetchable; training corpus must be assembled from the data-availability statement.
caveats: No explicit dataset license located — verify. Validation sets are formatting examples, not the full training data. Model drops records whose TCR names are not in its reference DB. No dog.

name: PRJNA742469 / SRP326193 — Canine Single-cell TCR + scRNA (Hoang 2024)
description: Validated single-cell TRA/TRB (paired alpha/beta) + scRNA profiling on 10x Chromium across 16 samples from 11 companion dogs — the reference canine single-cell TCR dataset.
scale: 16 samples, 11 dogs (paired scTCR+scRNA)

relevance.why: The core public canine paired-chain TCR resource; substrate for canine TCR modeling and for a canine V/D/J reference.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ (prefetch) + 10x outputs; no auth.
caveats: No antigen specificity (no pMHC-labeled TCRs). Small donor n.

name: PRJNA790470 — Canine Immunoglobulin (IGH/IGK/IGL) Repertoire NGS (PLoS ONE 2022)
description: 5'-RACE next-generation sequencing of the canine immunoglobulin (BCR) repertoire — IGH, IGK and IGL — from 25 healthy control dogs and 18 dogs with intermediate-to-large B-cell lymphoma (pre-treatment T1; 13 also sampled post-treatment T2), with a dedicated bioinformatics pipeline (PLoS ONE 2022). One of the few unbiased high-throughput canine BCR repertoire datasets.
scale: 25 healthy + 18 BCL dogs (13 paired post-treatment); IGH/IGK/IGL

relevance.why: Rare canine BCR/antibody repertoire resource with a disease (B-cell lymphoma) vs healthy contrast and longitudinal treatment samples — directly supports canine antibody/BCR modeling in the recognition arm.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Reads concatenated by sample/time point. Pair with IMGT canine germline for V(D)J assignment. Repertoire depth per sample should be checked before clonality analysis.

name: TChard
description: Aggregated benchmark dataset for TCR-peptide/pMHC binding prediction, built to be the largest such collection at publication by merging IEDB, VDJdb, McPAS-TCR and the NetTCR-2.0 data, with controlled negative generation and hard (unseen-peptide) evaluation splits.
scale: >500,000 samples

relevance.why: Ready-made, pre-split benchmark for honest unseen-peptide generalization testing — directly reusable for evaluating our recognition models.

agent_access: Direct Zenodo download (no auth) and loadable via PyTDC DataLoader(name="tchard"). Fully automatable.
caveats: Non-commercial license — a red flag for any commercial/productized ML use; confirm before use. Aggregated from upstream DBs so inherits their biases and overlaps; human only, no dog.

name: TCRdb (HUST / TCRdb2.0)
description: Large aggregated database of TCR sequences from reprocessed public TCR-seq/RNA-seq projects with a search function; TCRdb 2.0 (2025/26) massively expands it and adds a very large healthy-control reference. Mostly specificity-agnostic bulk repertoires.
scale: ~277M sequences / 130 studies (v1); ~700M sequences / 19,701 samples (v2.0)
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (paper; data terms per site)

provenance.maintainer: Guo Lab (HUST / West China Hospital, SCU)

relevance.why: Scale repertoire background for negative sampling, V/J usage priors and clonotype frequency modeling — not antigen-labeled, but foundational for repertoire context.

agent_access: Per-sample/per-project download via the web portal; no documented programmatic API or bulk tarball, so automated retrieval likely means scripted page-driven downloads.
caveats: Paper is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) — flag for commercial use; confirm data terms on site. TCRdb 2.0 DOI should be verified on the site (listed here as best-effort). Specificity-agnostic (no antigen labels) — pair with labeled sets.

name: 10x Genomics CD8+ T cells of Healthy Donors 1-4 (dextramer release)
description: Four public 10x single-cell datasets (one per healthy donor) pairing 5' gene expression, TotalSeq-C surface protein, paired TCR, and ~50 dCODE Dextramer (pMHC multimer) readouts (44 antigen + 6 negative controls). Each donor is a separate downloadable dataset with a per-cell binarized specificity matrix. The canonical large single-cell TCR-to-pMHC release.
scale: >150,000 CD8+ T cells total across 4 donors; ~50 pMHC multimers each

relevance.why: The most-used public single-cell dataset with paired TCR + pMHC specificity labels — core training/benchmark data for TCR-antigen recognition models.

agent_access: Four separate dataset pages (Donor 1-4); each offers direct file download (binarized matrix CSV, filtered feature matrices, VDJ), no auth (CC BY 4.0). Scriptable per donor.
caveats: Raw dextramer calls are noisy; specificity call = binding UMI >10 AND >5x max negative control, excluding cells with >4 specificities. Prefer the ICON-curated subset (~53,062 cells, Zhang et al. 2021) for clean labels. pMHC/HLA nomenclature: cross-ref presentation agent.

name: 10x Genomics "A New Way of Exploring Immunity" — CD8 dextramer dataset
description: Public 10x single-cell immune-profiling dataset pairing gene expression, cell-surface protein (feature barcoding) and paired TCR sequence with ~44 dextramer (pMHC multimer) readouts per cell across four healthy donors — i.e. single-cell TCR-to-pMHC specificity labels from barcoded multimer binding.
scale: >150,000 CD8+ T cells across 4 donors, ~44 dextramers each

relevance.why: One of the largest public single-cell datasets with paired TCR + pMHC specificity labels — core training data for TCR-antigen recognition models.

agent_access: Direct file download from the 10x datasets/support site, no auth (CC BY). Scriptable per-donor. Multiple files (GEX, protein, VDJ, dextramer counts) per donor.
caveats: Raw dextramer calls are noisy (high background); most downstream work uses the ICON- curated subset (~53k cells, Zhang et al. 2021) with corrected pMHC/TCR annotations — prefer that for labels. pMHC/HLA nomenclature: cross-ref the presentation agent.

name: TetTCR-seq barcoded-tetramer single-cell TCR specificity dataset (Zhang 2018)
description: Data from TetTCR-seq, which pairs DNA-barcoded pMHC tetramers (made rapidly by in vitro transcription/translation) with single-cell TCR sequencing to link TCR sequence to antigen specificity at scale. Released as six "TetTCR-seq summary" supplementary tables (experiments 1-6) linking TCRs to tetramer-barcode specificities.
scale: Thousands of single cells; 6 experiment summary tables of TCR-to-antigen pairings

provenance.maintainer: Zhang, Ma, Jiang et al. (UT Austin / UPenn)

relevance.why: Paired TCR-sequence/antigen-specificity data from a non-10x barcoded-tetramer platform; direct training/test material for TCR-pMHC specificity prediction.

agent_access: Six supplementary Excel tables from the Nature Biotechnology article page (no auth for SI). Raw sequencing not clearly deposited in a public GEO/SRA accession.
caveats: Data only as journal SI (Springer Nature terms, no open license). Raw reads location not confirmed — pairings available, raw FASTQ may be restricted/absent.

name: TetTCR-SeqHD high-dimensional barcoded-tetramer T-cell dataset (Ma 2021)
description: TetTCR-SeqHD jointly profiles antigen specificity (DNA-barcoded pMHC tetramers), gene expression, surface phenotype, and paired alpha/beta TCR sequence in single CD8 T cells. The study profiled ~33,000 single cells from healthy donors and type-1-diabetes donors; raw sequencing is deposited at dbGaP (controlled access).
scale: ~32,992 single cells; GEX + phenotype + paired TCR + tetramer-barcode antigen

provenance.maintainer: Ma, Schonnesen, Jiang et al. (UT Austin / UPenn); dbGaP

relevance.why: A rich multimodal barcoded-tetramer dataset (antigen + TCR + transcriptome + phenotype) beyond the 10x releases; valuable for jointly modelling TCR specificity and T-cell state, if dbGaP access is obtained.

agent_access: Raw sequencing is controlled-access under dbGaP phs002441 (requires an approved Data Use Certification). Summary tables accompany the paper as SI.
caveats: Controlled-access (dbGaP DUA) for raw data — catalog but note the gate. SI tables are open but under Springer Nature terms.

name: TITAN TCR-epitope dataset (VDJdb + ImmuneCODE)
description: Training/eval data for TITAN bimodal-attention TCR specificity model, assembled from VDJdb plus the Adaptive ImmuneCODE COVID release, filtered to single-epitope productive sequences with generated negatives. ESM-1b embedding copy also released for the TDC task.
scale: large VDJdb+ImmuneCODE TCR-epitope set (incl. COVID expansion)

relevance.why: Demonstrates the VDJdb+ImmuneCODE combination we would likely use; TDC embedding copy is a ready feature set.

agent_access: Data via GitHub repo + Zenodo (ESM embeddings); no auth. Note ImmuneCODE-derived rows inherit Adaptive terms.
caveats: Incorporates ImmuneCODE (Adaptive "Research Use Only" terms — redistribution/ML red flag). Repo data license unspecified. Human only.

name: VDJdb
description: Manually curated database of TCR sequences (CDR3 alpha/beta plus V/J) with known antigen (epitope + restricting MHC) specificity, aggregated from the literature and from paired single-cell studies. Each record carries a confidence score and, in recent releases, paratope embeddings, noise filtering and predicted 3D structures.
scale: tens of thousands of TCR-epitope records across many epitopes (growing)
license: CC BY 4.0 (database records; verify current repo LICENSE)

relevance.why: Standardized, confidence-scored TCR-epitope ground truth — a backbone training/eval set for antigen-recognition models and for harmonizing other assay sources.

agent_access: GitHub release tarballs (vdjdb-db) and Zenodo DOI snapshots for reproducible pinning; REST API (POST /api/database/search) via vdjdb-web; vdjmatch (GPL-3) and immunarch for programmatic querying. Fully automatable, no auth.
caveats: CC BY-ND forbids distributing modified versions, a redistribution/ML red flag — our derived training files cannot be republished verbatim. License metadata is inconsistent across sources (one GitHub listing showed AGPL-3.0); verify the LICENSE file per release. Heavy overlap with IEDB/McPAS requires dedup. No dog coverage.

name: VDJdb high-confidence subset
description: Filtered view of VDJdb restricted to records with higher confidence scores (legacy 0-3 score >= 1, or the newer v3.2a assay-validation / v3.2b cross-study probabilities). Not a separate database — a quality-gated slice of VDJdb used by most benchmark pipelines to reduce false positives.
scale: subset of VDJdb; size depends on score threshold (tens of thousands)

relevance.why: The cleaner slice we would actually train/evaluate recognition models on; filtering is done client-side after download.

agent_access: Same as VDJdb; apply score filter locally after bulk download or via the web filter params.
caveats: Thresholds are not standardized across papers — document the exact filter. Same CC BY-ND redistribution limit as VDJdb.

name: Baker lab de novo pMHC-I binder design (code + designed structure)
description: Release accompanying "Design of high-specificity binders for peptide-MHC-I complexes": RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN design code and examples for building proteins that read out disease-linked peptides on MHC-I, plus a deposited experimental structure of a designed binder-antigen complex.
scale: Design code + examples (Zenodo v1.0.0); specific binders identified for 11 target pMHC-I; MART-1 binder-antigen complex in PDB (9O5S)
license: unknown (check Zenodo record); PDB entry 9O5S is CC0

provenance.maintainer: Baker Lab / Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington

relevance.why: The flagship public demonstration and code for de novo peptide-MHC-I binder design — the most directly applicable methodology and worked example for Veritope's pMHC binder program.

agent_access: Code + examples archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.15169815); designed structure retrievable from PDB (9O5S). Scriptable.
caveats: Zenodo license not confirmed (marked unknown). Only one designed complex is deposited (9O5S); full design sets live in supplements. Companion NY-ESO-1 minibinder paper (10.1126/science.adv0422) reuses prior RFdiffusion releases.

name: Canine Immunology Reagents / CD-Marker Antibody Resources
description: The practical reagent layer for canine immunology: commercial anti-dog CD-marker monoclonal antibodies (CD3/CD4/CD5/CD8/CD21 etc., with clones + RRIDs) from Bio-Rad and others, rooted in the International Canine Leukocyte Antigen Workshop (CLAW) homolog assignments. No central curated public database — a scattered vendor/literature landscape.
scale: dozens of validated clones across core CD markers; no unified count

relevance.why: Reagent availability constrains any wet-lab canine immunology (sorting DLA+ cells, validating T-cell subsets); documents the tooling gap relative to human/mouse.

agent_access: Vendor catalogs scrapeable; RRIDs queryable via SciCrunch API. No research dataset to download.
caveats: GAP ALERT: canine immune reagents are scarce and fragmented vs human/mouse; many rely on cross-reactive anti-human/anti-bovine clones. No open, curated reagent database.

name: cBioPortal for Cancer Genomics
description: Aggregation, query and visualization platform hosting hundreds of published cancer genomics studies (TCGA, MSK-IMPACT, GENIE public, metastatic cohorts, and more) as harmonized mutation, copy-number, fusion, expression and clinical matrices. The public instance exposes everything through a documented REST API and downloadable per-study archives; private deployments can host controlled data.
scale: hundreds of studies (public instance); counts vary by release
license: ODC Open Database License (ODbL) for data unless noted; software Apache-2.0 (AGPL-3.0 pre-2026)

relevance.why: Fastest programmatic route to harmonized somatic mutation + expression across many cohorts without per-study DUAs — ideal for assembling neoantigen candidate sets and recurrence/frequency priors.

agent_access: Public REST API (Swagger), R (cBioPortalData, cbioportalR) and Python clients, plus per-study ZIP archives and a Data Hub for bulk. No auth on the public instance; rate limits apply to the API. Fully automatable.
caveats: Data under ODbL (attribution + share-alike of derived databases) unless a study notes otherwise — check per-study. Processed/derived data only (no raw reads). Hosts public GENIE, which still carries GENIE's no-redistribution terms (see aacr-genie).

name: CZ CELLxGENE Discover (+ Census)
description: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative portal aggregating standardized, cell-typed single-cell datasets (incl. Tabula Sapiens, HLCA, heart/gut atlases, HCA collections) with a programmatic Census for querying tens of millions of normal cells in a harmonized schema. The primary access layer for normal single-cell references.
scale: >100M cells across standardized collections; Census spans the corpus

relevance.why: Single harmonized interface + API to most normal single-cell references — the efficient way to query "which cell types express target X across normal tissues" at scale.

agent_access: cellxgene-census (Python/R, SOMA/TileDB) for programmatic slicing without downloading whole datasets; per-dataset .h5ad download via HTTPS. No auth.
caveats: Aggregator: each underlying dataset keeps its own license/consent — check per collection before redistribution. Schema standardization can lose study-specific detail.

name: CRI iAtlas (Cancer Research Institute iAtlas)
description: Interactive analysis platform and open data resource built on the TCGA immune-landscape (Thorsson) features plus ICI trial cohorts, exposing immune subtypes, cell composition, neoantigen/TCR metrics and immunomodulator expression through a web app and programmatic data packages/API.
scale: TCGA pan-cancer (>10,000 tumors) + multiple ICI cohorts
license: Open (code/data open; built on TCGA-derived features)

provenance.maintainer: Cancer Research Institute + Sage Bionetworks / ISB

relevance.why: Convenient programmatic access to harmonized immune features and ICI cohorts — a fast layer for pulling neoantigen/immune-context covariates without recomputing them.

agent_access: Web app plus an open API and R data packages (iatlas-data on GitHub) — no auth, scriptable.
caveats: Aggregates/derives from upstream sources (TCGA + published ICI cohorts); for read-level or controlled upstream data you still hit the original access tiers. Feature values are method-dependent.

name: EMBL-EBI BioStudies / ArrayExpress
description: EMBL-EBI's study archive; ArrayExpress (functional genomics, incl. single-cell) now runs as a BioStudies collection. European counterpart to GEO for discovering and retrieving deposited expression/single-cell studies.
scale: ArrayExpress: >70k experiments; BioStudies: hundreds of thousands of studies
license: EMBL-EBI Terms of Use; per-study terms vary

relevance.why: Complementary discovery/retrieval layer to GEO (some EU studies are here first/only), widening coverage for an ingestion pipeline.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: BioStudies REST API returns JSON (search + per-study); files via BioStudies FTP organized by accession prefix. Legacy ArrayExpress v3 XML API is deprecated. bioservices (Python) and ArrayExpress Bioconductor wrap it. Automatable, no auth.
caveats: No single data license (EMBL-EBI Terms of Use + per-study terms) — check each study. ArrayExpress migrated onto BioStudies (2021); use BioStudies endpoints, not legacy API.

name: European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA)
description: Archive for personally identifiable / consented human genetic and phenotypic data under controlled access governed by per-dataset Data Access Committees (DACs). Holds many tumor genomics and some single-cell datasets not releasable openly.
scale: thousands of controlled-access datasets/studies

relevance.why: Source for high-value controlled human tumor datasets (e.g. the one 3CA study held only on EGA) that are unavailable in open repositories.

agent_access: Public Metadata API for discovery (open); Permissions API lists datasets a requester may access. Downloads via EGA Secure Download Client / pyEGA3 over SFTP, files encrypted and decrypted client-side. Actual data retrieval requires DAC approval — NOT agent-automatable end-to-end; metadata discovery is.
caveats: Controlled access: each person/dataset needs individual DAC approval under a custom DAA; EGA does not enforce the agreement. Cannot be bulk-ingested without institutional approval. Factor approval lead time into any pipeline relying on it.

name: epiTCR training data
description: Large TCR-peptide binding training set (with/without MHC) released with epiTCR, a random-forest predictor, including categorized full-training files and negative construction.
scale: large (>3M rows across categories per repo); full-training file zipped in repo

relevance.why: One of the larger aggregated TCR-peptide training corpora; useful for scale experiments and as a comparison baseline.

agent_access: CSV (zipped) in GitHub repo data/ folder; clone/download, no auth. Automatable.
caveats: Repo license not confirmed — verify. Aggregated from public DBs (inherits biases/overlaps). Human only, no dog.

name: ERGO / ERGO-II training sets
description: Training/evaluation data bundled with the ERGO and ERGO-II TCR-peptide binding predictors. Users select McPAS-TCR or VDJdb as the training database; repos include preprocessed pairs and negative-sampling scripts.
scale: derived from VDJdb + McPAS-TCR (tens of thousands of pairs)

provenance.maintainer: Louzoun Lab, Bar-Ilan University (Springer et al.)

relevance.why: Reference preprocessing + negative-sampling pipeline over VDJdb/McPAS; useful as a baseline and for reproducing standard splits.

agent_access: Code + data in GitHub (ERGO, ERGO-II); web predictor at tcr2.cs.biu.ac.il. Clone/download, no auth.
caveats: Data is downstream of VDJdb/McPAS (inherits their licenses/biases, incl. VDJdb CC BY-ND). Repo-level license unclear — verify. No dog.

name: ERVmap — genome-wide human endogenous retrovirus transcription tool + locus set
description: Open-source pipeline and curated set of 3,220 human proviral ERV loci for quantifying genome- wide ERV transcription from RNA-seq, with an accompanying web tool. The reference method/locus annotation for measuring ERV expression — the substrate for ERV-derived tumor antigens.
scale: 3,220 annotated ERV loci; per-locus normalized/raw expression outputs

provenance.maintainer: Yale University (Iwasaki lab; Tokuyama et al.)

relevance.why: ERV-derived antigens depend on accurately quantifying locus-specific ERV transcription; ERVmap provides the standard locus set and pipeline to screen tumors for ERV antigen sources.

agent_access: Code + locus annotation on GitHub, no auth. Accuracy debated vs Telescope (see PNAS exchange 10.1073/pnas.1907705116 / 10.1073/pnas.1915450116).
caveats: NO LICENSE file located in the GitHub repo (flag before reuse). It is a tool + annotation, not a tumor antigen dataset per se. Human only; read-assignment accuracy is contested.

name: figshare
description: General-purpose research data repository (Digital Science) that mints DOIs for datasets and files. Hosts major single-cell releases (e.g. Tabula Sapiens figshare archives) and much supplementary data.
scale: millions of items; ~20 GB per-file free limit
license: per-item (CC0 default for data; MIT/GPL/Apache for code; CC-BY on some)

relevance.why: Primary host for several key single-cell atlas releases and supplementary datasets a pipeline must fetch by DOI/article id.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: REST API (articles, files, search) + OAI-PMH; direct file download by article id. No auth for public items. Automatable.
