caveats: Per-item license varies (data often CC0, but confirm) — read it per record. Very large single-file archives (tens of GB) need resumable download handling. Self-deposit, so curation varies.

name: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) + ArrayExpress/BioStudies
description: Primary public repositories for functional genomics (bulk + single-cell RNA-seq, arrays): NCBI GEO and EMBL-EBI ArrayExpress/BioStudies. Host the raw/processed matrices for most expression-based normal references here (e.g. GSE201333, GSE134355, GSE107011; E-MTAB-9543).
scale: >200k GEO series; millions of samples

relevance.why: Retrieval layer for the expression accessions cited across this catalog; enables scripted bulk fetch of normal transcriptome datasets (human and dog).

agent_access: GEO: E-utilities / NCBI Datasets API + FTP (supplementary matrices); raw reads via SRA. ArrayExpress/BioStudies: REST API + FTP. No auth for public records; NCBI API key raises limits.
caveats: GEO metadata is author-supplied (variable quality); raw reads live in SRA/ENA (large, separate fetch). Processed-matrix availability varies per series.

name: Human Cell Atlas (HCA) Data Portal
description: The Human Cell Atlas Data Coordination Platform: standardized ingestion, processing and distribution of HCA single-cell/spatial projects of (mostly healthy) human tissues, with metadata and bulk access (ERP/EGA accessions for raw data).
scale: Hundreds of HCA projects across organs; millions of cells

provenance.maintainer: Human Cell Atlas consortium / HCA DCP (EMBL-EBI, UCSC, Broad)

relevance.why: Canonical source and metadata backbone for normal human tissue single-cell atlases; resolves raw-data accessions (e.g. ERP123138 for the heart atlas) feeding the self references above.

agent_access: REST/Azul APIs + bulk matrix download; raw sequence via linked ERP/EGA accessions. Open metadata; some raw data managed-access.
caveats: Per-project licensing/consent varies; some raw data behind EGA/managed access. Processed matrices often more accessible on CELLxGENE.

name: ImRex TCR-epitope training data & models
description: Raw/preprocessed VDJdb-derived TCRb-epitope data (human TRB, 10x excluded, CDR3 10-20aa, epitope 8-11aa, shuffled negatives) plus trained CNN models and decoy/downsampled variants, from the ImMunoinformatics image-classification approach.
scale: VDJdb 2019-08 derived; data.zip ~34 MB; full record ~10 GB incl. models/comparisons

provenance.maintainer: Meysman lab, University of Antwerp (Moris et al.)

relevance.why: Clean, reproducible VDJdb preprocessing + negative-generation recipe and a CNN baseline for recognition; CC BY data is reusable.

agent_access: Zenodo direct download (data.zip ~34 MB is the useful part; full record ~10 GB with models); GitHub code. No auth, automatable.
caveats: Negatives are shuffle-generated (known to inflate performance vs real negatives). Underlying pairs from VDJdb. Human only, no dog.

name: NCBI GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus)
description: Primary public archive for functional genomics data including the majority of published single-cell and bulk tumor/immune studies (processed matrices + links to raw in SRA). The canonical first stop for discovering and retrieving deposited datasets by accession.
scale: millions of samples (GSM) across >200k series (GSE)
license: NCBI public-domain terms (no blanket license; submitter-dependent)

relevance.why: The main discovery+retrieval layer for nearly all deposited tumor-immune single-cell and functional-assay data — foundational to any ingestion pipeline.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: Entrez E-utilities (esearch/esummary/efetch) for metadata discovery (set tool+email; API key raises limits to 10 req/s). Bulk raw/processed files over FTP/HTTPS by accession path (GSEnnn/GSExxx/suppl). GEOparse/GEOquery wrap both. Robust for automation.
caveats: No single data license — reuse terms depend on the submitting study; GEO itself places no restriction but downstream terms vary. E-utilities does not serve all file bodies — use FTP for raw/supplementary. Rate-limit without an API key (3 req/s).

name: NCBI SRA (Sequence Read Archive)
description: Primary archive for raw high-throughput sequencing reads underlying GEO and many other submissions (FASTQ/BAM-level data for scRNA-seq, TCR-seq, etc.). Where raw reads are retrieved for reprocessing when processed matrices are insufficient.
scale: petabase-scale; tens of millions of runs (SRR)
license: NCBI public-domain terms (open) + dbGaP controlled tier

relevance.why: Raw-read source for reprocessing single-cell/TCR studies to a uniform pipeline and for recovering data not released as processed matrices.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: SRA Toolkit (prefetch/fasterq-dump) reads directly from AWS/GCP buckets; full corpus mirrored on AWS + GCP Open Data; metadata queryable via BigQuery (GCP) and Athena (AWS) for SQL-style discovery. Cloud Data Delivery Service copies originals to your bucket. Highly automatable.
caveats: Egress/compute costs when pulling from cloud outside the hosting region. Controlled human data (dbGaP) needs approval — not auto-ingestible. Large volumes; plan storage. Toolkit cannot deliver every original submitted file (use Cloud Data Delivery Service).

name: ProteinMPNN / RFdiffusion (design models, weights & training data)
description: Open-source protein-design toolchain: RFdiffusion (backbone generation / de novo binder design, incl. target-conditioned binders) and ProteinMPNN (sequence design given backbone). Models and weights are public; training data is PDB-derived (multi-chain assemblies). No single packaged "benchmark dataset" is released — benchmarks live in the papers' supplements.
scale: Model weights + inference code; trained on PDB assemblies (RFdiffusion up to ~2020; RFD3/foundry reports PDB through Dec 2024)
license: ProteinMPNN: MIT; RFdiffusion: BSD (code + weights); RFantibody: MIT

provenance.maintainer: Baker Lab / Institute for Protein Design (UW); RosettaCommons

relevance.why: The core generative + sequence-design stack for building de novo binders, including against peptide-MHC. Public weights make it directly usable in the binder-design pipeline; benchmarks guide validation.

agent_access: Public GitHub repos; weights fetched via README wget (IPD file server for RFdiffusion) or Hugging Face mirrors for ProteinMPNN. Fully scriptable.
caveats: No standalone released benchmark dataset — reconstruct benchmarks from paper supplements. Mind license differences (MIT vs BSD) per component and whether weights are covered. Training sets are PDB-derived, not separately distributed.

name: ProteomeXchange / PRIDE (+ MassIVE)
description: Central federated infrastructure for mass-spectrometry proteomics and immunopeptidomics data. PRIDE (EMBL-EBI) and MassIVE (UCSD) are the main repositories; nearly all normal-proteome and normal-immunopeptidome accessions in this catalog (PXD*/MSV*) resolve here.
scale: >20,000 PXD datasets; petabyte-scale raw MS

relevance.why: The retrieval layer for every normal-proteome / normal-immunopeptidome PXD accession here (PXD016999, PXD010154, PXD000561, PXD000865, PXD020186/PXD024837); enables automated bulk fetch.

agent_access: PRIDE Archive REST API (ws/archive/v2) for metadata + file lists (JSON); download via FTP, Aspera, or Globus. No auth for public datasets. Large raw files.
caveats: Each deposit sets its own license (CC0/CC BY common but not universal) — resolve per PXD record. Raw MS usually needs reprocessing to usable tables.

name: STAPLER fine-tuning dataset
description: Data for STAPLER, a joint TCRab-peptide language model for specificity prediction. The model is fine-tuned on labeled full-length CD8+ alpha/beta TCR paired with 9-mer MHC-I peptides; the repo documents the training/evaluation data and negative construction.
scale: ~23,544 labeled TCRab-peptide pairs (fine-tuning set)

relevance.why: Full-length paired-chain labeled set (rarer than CDR3-only) for recognition modeling and as a strong transformer baseline.

agent_access: Data/code via GitHub; direct download/clone, no auth. Automatable.
caveats: Repo license not confirmed — verify before reuse. Underlying pairs drawn from public DBs (inherits their terms). MHC-I 9-mer scope only; human only, no dog.

name: UCSC Xena (public cancer genomics hubs)
description: Open visualization and bulk-download platform mirroring processed cancer genomics data from TCGA, PCAWG, GDC, TARGET, CCLE and others as tidy expression, mutation, copy-number, methylation and clinical matrices. The simplest no-auth route to many major cohorts' derived data.
scale: ~1,500+ datasets across public hubs (TCGA, PCAWG, GDC, TARGET, CCLE)
license: Software Apache-2.0; underlying data follow each source's policy (TCGA/PCAWG/GDC)

relevance.why: Lowest-friction way to pull harmonized expression + mutation matrices across TCGA/PCAWG for building and benchmarking antigen-expression models without DUAs.

agent_access: Fully open: direct file URLs per hub (e.g. tcga.xenahubs.net/download/...), the UCSCXenaTools R client, and a query interface — no account, bulk-friendly, scriptable.
caveats: Processed/derived data only (no raw reads); these are mirrors, so the ORIGINAL source's use terms still govern (open-tier TCGA/PCAWG summaries are fine; raw/germline remain controlled upstream). No formal documented REST API beyond hub endpoints.

name: Wilhelm 2021 Prosit / ProteomeTools synthetic immunopeptidome
description: ~305,000 SYNTHETIC non-tryptic (HLA class I/II) peptides measured in ProteomeTools to train the Prosit deep-learning spectrum/retention-time predictor, boosting immunopeptidomics identification sensitivity. Ground-truth spectra, not elution data.
scale: ~305,000 synthetic non-tryptic peptides (HLA-I/II + AspN/LysN)

relevance.why: Rescoring immunopeptidomics searches with Prosit substantially increases peptide IDs - a force-multiplier for any in-house reprocessing of raw HLA-elution data.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD021398 (API/FTP); Prosit served via ProteomicsDB/Koina. Bulk-downloadable.
caveats: Synthetic reference (for rescoring), not a ligand set. Paper also argues ~87% of proposed spliced peptides are likely wrong - relevant QC caution. Human sequences.

name: Zenodo
description: CERN/EU-backed general-purpose research data repository that mints DOIs (concept + versioned) for datasets, code and supplementary files. Common host for immunology/ single-cell dataset snapshots (e.g. dated VDJdb releases) for reproducible pinning.
scale: millions of records; 50 GB per record free tier
license: per-record (depositor-chosen); must be set for public records

relevance.why: Reproducible, DOI-pinned snapshots of community datasets and model inputs; a stable place to resolve versioned dependencies in a pipeline.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: REST API (records search, metadata, file download) + OAI-PMH harvesting; DOIs resolve to files. No auth for public records (token needed only to deposit). Fully automatable.
caveats: License is per-record and must be read programmatically — ranges from CC0 to restrictive; never assume. Quality/curation varies (self-deposit). Prefer concept DOI's latest or pin a specific version.
